1.s: manumekāgramāsīnamabhigamya maharṣayaḥ pratipūjya yathānyāyamidaṃ vacanamabruvan
1.d: मनुमेकाग्रमासीनमभिगम्य महर्षयः प्रतिपूज्य यथान्यायमिदं वचनमब्रुवन्
1.e: The Great Sages, having approached Manu, paid their respect to him in due form, and finding him seated with mind calm and collected, addressed him these words

1.s: bhagavan sarvavarṇānāṃ yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ antaraprabhavānāṃ ca dharmānno vaktumarhasi
1.d: भगवन् सर्ववर्णानां यथावदनुपूर्वशः अन्तरप्रभवानां च धर्मान्नो वक्तुमर्हसि
1.e: May Thou, O blessed One, explain to us, in due form and in proper order, the duties of all castes and intermediate castes!

1.s: tvameko hyasya sarvasya vidhānasya svayaṃbhuvaḥ acintyasyāprameyasya kāryatattvārthavit prabho
1.d: त्वमेको ह्यस्य सर्वस्य विधानस्य स्वयंभुवः अचिन्त्यस्याप्रमेयस्य कार्यतत्त्वार्थवित् प्रभो
1.e: Thou alone, O Lord, art conversant with what ought to be done, which forms the true import of this entire Veda—which is eternal, inconceivable and not directly cognisable.

1.s: sa taiḥ pṛṣṭastathā samyagamitojā mahātmabhiḥ pratyuvācārcya tān sarvān maharṣīṃśrūyatāmiti
1.d: स तैः पृष्टस्तथा सम्यगमितोजा महात्मभिः प्रत्युवाचार्च्य तान् सर्वान् महर्षींश्रूयतामिति
1.e: Being thus questioned by the high-souled Great Sages, he, possessed op illimitable vigour, received them with reverence, and with proper courtesy answered them—‘listen.’

1.s: āsīdidaṃ tamobhūtamaprajñātamalakṣaṇam apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ prasuptamiva sarvataḥ
1.d: आसीदिदं तमोभूतमप्रज्ञातमलक्षणम् अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं प्रसुप्तमिव सर्वतः
1.e: This (World) was in existence in the form, as it were, of dense Darkness,—unperceived, undifferentiated, incogitable, (hence) incognizable; as it was wholly merged in deep sleep.

1.s: tataḥ svayaṃbhūrbhagavānavyakto vyañjayannidam mahābhūtādi vṛttojāḥ prādurāsīt tamonudaḥ
1.d: ततः स्वयंभूर्भगवानव्यक्तो व्यञ्जयन्निदम् महाभूतादि वृत्तोजाः प्रादुरासीत् तमोनुदः
1.e: Thereafter, the supreme being Hiraṇyagarbha, self-born, unmanifest and bringing into view this (universe), appeared,—dispelling darkness and having his (creative) power operating upon the Elemental Substances and other things.

1.s: yo 'sāvatīndriyagrāhyaḥ sūkṣmo 'vyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ sarvabhūtamayo 'cintyaḥ sa eva svayamudbabhau sa eṣa
1.d: यो ऽसावतीन्द्रियग्राह्यः सूक्ष्मो ऽव्यक्तः सनातनः सर्वभूतमयो ऽचिन्त्यः स एव स्वयमुद्बभौ स एष
1.e: He,—who is apprehended beyond the senses, who is subtile, unmanifest and eternal, absorbed in all created things and inconceivable,—appeared by himself.

1.s: so 'bhidhyāya śarīrāt svāt sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryamavāsṛjat
1.d: सो ऽभिध्याय शरीरात् स्वात् सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः अप एव ससर्जादौ तासु वीर्यमवासृजत्
1.e: Desiring to create the several kinds of created things, he, in the beginning, by mere willing, produced, out op his own body, Water; and in that he threw the seed.

1.s: tadaṇḍamabhavaddhaimaṃ sahasrāṃśusamaprabham tasmiñjajñe svayaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
1.d: तदण्डमभवद्धैमं सहस्रांशुसमप्रभम् तस्मिञ्जज्ञे स्वयं ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः
1.e: That became the golden egg, resplendent like the Sun; in that (egg) he (Hiraṇyagarbha) himself was born as Brahmā, the ‘Grand-father’ of the whole world.

1.s: āpo narā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ tā yadasyāyanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
1.d: आपो नरा इति प्रोक्ता आपो वै नरसूनवः ता यदस्यायनं पूर्वं तेन नारायणः स्मृतः
1.e: Water is called ‘nara,’—water being the offspring of nara; since water was the first thing created by (or, the original residence of) that being, he is, on that account, described as ‘nārāyaṇa.’

1.s: yat tat kāraṇamavyaktaṃ nityaṃ sadasadātmakam tadvisṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣo loke brahmaiti kīrtyate
1.d: यत् तत् कारणमव्यक्तं नित्यं सदसदात्मकम् तद्विसृष्टः स पुरुषो लोके ब्रह्मैति कीर्त्यते
1.e: That which is the cause—unmanifest, eternal and partaking of the nature of the existent and the non-existent,—the being produced by that (cause) is described among people as ‘brahmā.’

1.s: tasminnaṇḍe sa bhagavānuṣitvā parivatsaram svayamevātmano dhyānāt tadaṇḍamakaroddvidhā
1.d: तस्मिन्नण्डे स भगवानुषित्वा परिवत्सरम् स्वयमेवात्मनो ध्यानात् तदण्डमकरोद्द्विधा
1.e: That supreme lord, having dwelt in that egg for a y ear, himself, by his own thought, broke that egg into two parts.

1.s: tābhyāṃ sa śakalābhyāṃ ca divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca nirmame madhye vyoma diśaścāṣṭāvapāṃ sthānaṃ ca śāśvatam
1.d: ताभ्यां स शकलाभ्यां च दिवं भूमिं च निर्ममे मध्ये व्योम दिशश्चाष्टावपां स्थानं च शाश्वतम्
1.e: Out of those two pieces (of the egg) he formed Heaven and Earth, and, between them, the Ākāśa, the eight quarters and the eternal receptacle of water.

1.s: udbabarhātmanaścaiva manaḥ sadasadātmakam manasaścāpyahaṅkāramabhimantāramīśvaram ahaṅkāram
1.d: उद्बबर्हात्मनश्चैव मनः सदसदात्मकम् मनसश्चाप्यहङ्कारमभिमन्तारमीश्वरम् अहङ्कारम्
1.e: From out of himself he brought forth the mind, which partakes of the nature of the existent and non-existent; and before the mind, he brought up the all-powerful principle of egoism, whose function consists in self-consciousness.

1.s: mahāntameva cātmānaṃ sarvāṇi triguṇāni ca viṣayāṇāṃ grahītr̥̄ṇi śanaiḥ pañcaindriyāṇi ca
1.d: महान्तमेव चात्मानं सर्वाणि त्रिगुणानि च विषयाणां ग्रहीत्र्̥̄णि शनैः पञ्चैन्द्रियाणि च
1.e: From out of himself he brought forth the mind, which partakes of the nature of the existent and non-existent; and before the mind, he brought up the all-powerful principle of egoism, whose function consists in self-consciousness.

1.s: teṣāṃ tvavayavān sūkṣmān ṣaṇṇāmapyamitojasām saṃniveśyātmamātrāsu sarvabhūtāni nirmame sanniveśya
1.d: तेषां त्ववयवान् सूक्ष्मान् षण्णामप्यमितोजसाम् संनिवेश्यात्ममात्रासु सर्वभूतानि निर्ममे सन्निवेश्य
1.e: Having combined the subtile components of the said six principles of illimitable potency with their own evolutes, he created even all beings.

1.s: yan mūrtiavayavāḥ sūkṣmāstānīmānyāśrayanti ṣaṭ tasmātśarīramityāhustasya mūrtiṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
1.d: यन् मूर्तिअवयवाः सूक्ष्मास्तानीमान्याश्रयन्ति षट् तस्मात्शरीरमित्याहुस्तस्य मूर्तिं मनीषिणः
1.e: Because the six subtile components of the frame (of primordial matter) enter into (produce) these, therefore the wise ones have described the frame of that (primordial matter) as ‘body.’

1.s: tadāviśanti bhūtāni mahānti saha karmabhiḥ manaścāvayavaiḥ sūkṣmaiḥ sarvabhūtakṛdavyayam
1.d: तदाविशन्ति भूतानि महान्ति सह कर्मभिः मनश्चावयवैः सूक्ष्मैः सर्वभूतकृदव्ययम्
1.e: The great elemental substances, along with their functions, as also the mind, along with its subtile components, enter into that which (on that account) is the generator of all things and imperishable.

1.s: teṣāmidaṃ tu saptānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ mahaujasām sūkṣmābhyo mūrtimātrābhyaḥ saṃbhavatyavyayādvyayam
1.d: तेषामिदं तु सप्तानां पुरुषाणां महौजसाम् सूक्ष्माभ्यो मूर्तिमात्राभ्यः संभवत्यव्ययाद्व्ययम्
1.e: From out of the Subtile constituents of the frames of the said exceedingly potent principles is produced this (Gross Body)—the perishable proceeding from the imperishable.

1.s: ādyādyasya guṇaṃ tveṣāmavāpnoti paraḥ paraḥ yo yo yāvatithaścaiṣāṃ sa sa tāvadguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
1.d: आद्याद्यस्य गुणं त्वेषामवाप्नोति परः परः यो यो यावतिथश्चैषां स स तावद्गुणः स्मृतः
1.e: Among these (Elementary Substances), each succeeding one acquires the quality of what precedes it; and each elemental substance is endowed with as many qualities as the place it occupies (in the order in which the said substances are set forth).

1.s: sarveṣāṃ tu sa nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthak pṛthak vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthak saṃsthāśca nirmame
1.d: सर्वेषां तु स नामानि कर्माणि च पृथक् पृथक् वेदशब्देभ्य एवादौ पृथक् संस्थाश्च निर्ममे
1.e: At the outset he designated distinct names for add things; and devised acts and Laws, on the basis of the words of the veda.

1.s: karmātmanāṃ ca devānāṃ so 'sṛjat prāṇināṃ prabhuḥ sādhyānāṃ ca gaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ yajñaṃ caiva sanātanam
1.d: कर्मात्मनां च देवानां सो ऽसृजत् प्राणिनां प्रभुः साध्यानां च गणं सूक्ष्मं यज्ञं चैव सनातनम्
1.e: For the sake of living beings intent upon action, he created the eternal sacrifice; as also the host of Gods and the subtile multitude of the lesser divinities, the Sādhyas.

1.s: agnivāyuravibhyastu trayaṃ brahma sanātanam dudoha yajñasiddhiarthaṃ ṛcyajussāmalakṣaṇam
1.d: अग्निवायुरविभ्यस्तु त्रयं ब्रह्म सनातनम् दुदोह यज्ञसिद्धिअर्थं ऋच्यजुस्सामलक्षणम्
1.e: From out of (the three deities) Agni, Vāyu and Ravi, he extracted, for the due fulfilment of sacrifices, the eternal Brahman, threefold, in the forms of ‘Ṛk,’ ‘Yajuṣ’ and ‘Sāman.’

1.s: kālaṃ kālavibhaktīśca nakṣatrāṇi grahāṃstathā saritaḥ sāgarāṃśailān samāni viṣamāni ca
1.d: कालं कालविभक्तीश्च नक्षत्राणि ग्रहांस्तथा सरितः सागरांशैलान् समानि विषमानि च
1.e: [He created] also Time, the Divisions of Time, the Lunar Mansions, the Planets, the Rivers, the Oceans, the Mountains and the tracts of land, plain and rugged.

1.s: tapo vācaṃ ratiṃ caiva kāmaṃ ca krodhameva ca sṛṣṭiṃ sasarja caivaimāṃ sraṣṭumicchannimāḥ prajāḥ
1.d: तपो वाचं रतिं चैव कामं च क्रोधमेव च सृष्टिं ससर्ज चैवैमां स्रष्टुमिच्छन्निमाः प्रजाः
1.e: Being desirous of bringing into existence these creatures, he created this entire creation (comprising) austerity, speech, happiness, desire and anger.

1.s: karmaṇāṃ ca vivekārthaṃ dharmādharmau vyavecayat vivekāya dvandvairayojayaccaimāḥ sukhaduḥkhādibhiḥ prajāḥ
1.d: कर्मणां च विवेकार्थं धर्माधर्मौ व्यवेचयत् विवेकाय द्वन्द्वैरयोजयच्चैमाः सुखदुःखादिभिः प्रजाः
1.e: For the due discrimination of actions, he differentiated Virtue and Vice; and he connected these creatures with such pairs of opposites as Pleasure-Pain and the like.

1.s: aṇvyo mātrā vināśinyo daśārdhānāṃ tu yāḥ smṛtāḥ tābhiḥ sārdhamidaṃ sarvaṃ saṃbhavatyanupūrvaśaḥ
1.d: अण्व्यो मात्रा विनाशिन्यो दशार्धानां तु याः स्मृताः ताभिः सार्धमिदं सर्वं संभवत्यनुपूर्वशः
1.e: The evanescent subtile constituents of the half-ten (Elemental Substances) that have been described,—along with those, this whole (world) comes forth, in due order.

1.s: yaṃ tu karmaṇi yasmin sa nyayuṅkta prathamaṃ prabhuḥ sa tadeva svayaṃ bheje sṛjyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
1.d: यं तु कर्मणि यस्मिन् स न्ययुङ्क्त प्रथमं प्रभुः स तदेव स्वयं भेजे सृज्यमानः पुनः पुनः
1.e: Each being, when created again and again, naturally conformed to that same act to which the lord had, at first, directed him.

1.s: hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharmāvṛtānṛte yadyasya so 'dadhāt sarge tat tasya svayamāviśat
1.d: हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मावृतानृते यद्यस्य सो ऽदधात् सर्गे तत् तस्य स्वयमाविशत्
1.e: Each being, when created again and again, naturally conformed to that same act to which the lord had, at first, directed him.

1.s: yathāṛtuliṅgāny ṛtavaḥ svayamevaṛtuparyaye svāni svānyabhipadyante tathā karmāṇi dehinaḥ
1.d: यथाऋतुलिङ्गान्य् ऋतवः स्वयमेवऋतुपर्यये स्वानि स्वान्यभिपद्यन्ते तथा कर्माणि देहिनः
1.e: Just as on the approach of the turn of the Seasons, each season, by itself, acquires its own seasonal characteristics,—so in the same manner living beings take up their respective lines of action.

1.s: lokānāṃ tu vivṛddhiarthaṃ mukhabāhūrupādataḥ brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ ca niravartayat
1.d: लोकानां तु विवृद्धिअर्थं मुखबाहूरुपादतः ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं वैश्यं शूद्रं च निरवर्तयत्
1.e: With a view to the development of the (three) regions, He brought into existence the Brāhmaṇa, the Kṣatriya, the Vaiśya and the Śūdra, from out of His mouth, arms, thighs and feet (respectively).

1.s: dvidhā kṛtvā 'tmano dehamardhena puruṣo 'bhavat ardhena nārī tasyāṃ sa virājamasṛjat prabhuḥ
1.d: द्विधा कृत्वा ऽत्मनो देहमर्धेन पुरुषो ऽभवत् अर्धेन नारी तस्यां स विराजमसृजत् प्रभुः
1.e: Having divided his body into two halves, with the one half, the Lord became Male, and with the other half, Female; from her he produced Virāj.

1.s: tapastaptvā 'sṛjadyaṃ tu sa svayaṃ puruṣo virāṭ taṃ māṃ vittāsya sarvasya sraṣṭāraṃ dvijasattamāḥ
1.d: तपस्तप्त्वा ऽसृजद्यं तु स स्वयं पुरुषो विराट् तं मां वित्तास्य सर्वस्य स्रष्टारं द्विजसत्तमाः
1.e: O best of Brāhmaṇas, know me, the creator, of this whole (would), to be that whom the said Being Virāj himself, after having performed austerities, produced.

1.s: ahaṃ prajāḥ sisṛkṣustu tapastaptvā suduścaram patīn prajānāmasṛjaṃ maharṣīnādito daśa
1.d: अहं प्रजाः सिसृक्षुस्तु तपस्तप्त्वा सुदुश्चरम् पतीन् प्रजानामसृजं महर्षीनादितो दश
1.e: Being desirous of bringing into existence the (various kinds of) created beings, I, at the very outset, performed most arduous austerities and called into being the ten great sages, the directors of all created things; (34)—viz: Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Pracetas, Vaśiṣṭha, Bhṛgu and also Nārada.

1.s: marīcimatriaṅgirasau pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum pracetasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca bhṛguṃ nāradameva ca
1.d: मरीचिमत्रिअङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् प्रचेतसं वसिष्ठं च भृगुं नारदमेव च
1.e: Being desirous of bringing into existence the (various kinds of) created beings, I, at the very outset, performed most arduous austerities and called into being the ten great sages, the directors of all created things; (34)—viz: Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Pracetas, Vaśiṣṭha, Bhṛgu and also Nārada.

1.s: ete manūṃstu saptān yānasṛjan bhūritejasaḥ devān devanikāyāṃśca maharṣīṃścāmitojasaḥ
1.d: एते मनूंस्तु सप्तान् यानसृजन् भूरितेजसः देवान् देवनिकायांश्च महर्षींश्चामितोजसः
1.e: These mighty (Sages) called into being the seven Manus, gods and gods’ habitations, as also Great Sages,—all possessed of illimitable power.

1.s: yakṣarakṣaspiśācāṃśca gandharvāpsaraso 'surān nāgān sarpān suparṇāṃśca pitr̥̄ṇāṃśca pṛthaggaṇam pitr̥̄ṇāṃ
1.d: यक्षरक्षस्पिशाचांश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसो ऽसुरान् नागान् सर्पान् सुपर्णांश्च पित्र्̥̄णांश्च पृथग्गणम् पित्र्̥̄णां
1.e: [They called into being] also Yakṣas, Rakṣasas, Piśācas, Gandharvas, Apsarases, Asuras, Nāgas, Sarpas, Suparṇas, and the several orders of Pitṛs.

1.s: vidyuto 'śanimeghāṃśca rohitaindradhanūṃṣi ca ulkānirghātaketūṃśca jyotīṃṣyuccāvacāni ca
1.d: विद्युतो ऽशनिमेघांश्च रोहितैन्द्रधनूंषि च उल्कानिर्घातकेतूंश्च ज्योतींष्युच्चावचानि च
1.e: [They called into being] Lightnings, Hails, Clouds, Vertical Phosphorescence, Rainbows, Meteors, Portentous Sounds, Comets, and Stars of varying magnitudes.

1.s: kinnarān vānarān matsyān vividhāṃśca vihaṅgamān paśūn mṛgān manuṣyāṃśca vyālāṃścaubhayatodataḥ
1.d: किन्नरान् वानरान् मत्स्यान् विविधांश्च विहङ्गमान् पशून् मृगान् मनुष्यांश्च व्यालांश्चौभयतोदतः
1.e: [They called into being] Kinnaras, Apes, Fishes, Birds of various kinds, Cattle, Deer, Men and wild beasts with two rows of teeth.

1.s: kṛmikīṭapataṅgāṃśca yūkāmakṣikamatkuṇam sarvaṃ ca daṃśamaśakaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca pṛthagvidham
1.d: कृमिकीटपतङ्गांश्च यूकामक्षिकमत्कुणम् सर्वं च दंशमशकं स्थावरं च पृथग्विधम्
1.e: [They called into being] Worms, Beetles and Moths; Lice, Flies and Bugs; Gadflies and Gnats; and also the entire host of the several kinds of immovable things.

1.s: evametairidaṃ sarvaṃ madniyogān mahātmabhiḥ yathākarma tapoyogāt sṛṣṭaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
1.d: एवमेतैरिदं सर्वं मद्नियोगान् महात्मभिः यथाकर्म तपोयोगात् सृष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम्
1.e: In this manner was all this, movable and immovable, called into being, through the force of austerities, by these high-souled sages, under my direction,—in accordance with their actions.

1.s: yeṣāṃ tu yādṛṣaṃ karma bhūtānāmiha kīrtitam tat tathā vo 'bhidhāsyāmi kramayogaṃ ca janmani
1.d: येषां तु यादृषं कर्म भूतानामिह कीर्तितम् तत् तथा वो ऽभिधास्यामि क्रमयोगं च जन्मनि
1.e: That kind of action which belongs to the several beings has been described here. I am now going to explain the manner of their birth.

1.s: paśavaśca mṛgāścaiva vyālāścaubhayatodataḥ rakṣāṃsi ca piśācāśca manuṣyāśca jarāyujāḥ manuṣāśca
1.d: पशवश्च मृगाश्चैव व्यालाश्चौभयतोदतः रक्षांसि च पिशाचाश्च मनुष्याश्च जरायुजाः मनुषाश्च
1.e: Cattle, Deer, Wild Beasts with two rows of teeth, Rākṣasas, Piśācas and Men are viviparous.

1.s: aṇḍājāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarpā nakrā matsyāśca kacchapāḥ yāni caivaṃprakārāṇi sthalajānyaudakāni ca
1.d: अण्डाजाः पक्षिणः सर्पा नक्रा मत्स्याश्च कच्छपाः यानि चैवंप्रकाराणि स्थलजान्यौदकानि च
1.e: Birds, Serpents, Crocodiles, Fishes, Tortoises, and other animals of similar kinds, terrestrial as well as aquatic,—are oviparous.

1.s: svedajaṃ daṃśamaśakaṃ yūkāmakṣikamatkuṇam ūṣmaṇaścaupajāyante yaccānyat kiṃ cidīdṛṣam
1.d: स्वेदजं दंशमशकं यूकामक्षिकमत्कुणम् ऊष्मणश्चौपजायन्ते यच्चान्यत् किं चिदीदृषम्
1.e: Gadflies and Gnats, Lice, Flies and Bugs, are sweat- born; whatever else is of similar character is born from heat

1.s: udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ sarve bījakāṇḍaprarohiṇaḥ oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntā bahupuṣpaphalaupagāḥ
1.d: उद्भिज्जाः स्थावराः सर्वे बीजकाण्डप्ररोहिणः ओषध्यः फलपाकान्ता बहुपुष्पफलौपगाः
1.e: All those immovable brings that are produced by splitting (i.e., Plants) grow out of seeds and slips. those that, abounding in flowers, perish with the ripening of their fruit, are called ‘oṣadhis’ (‘Annuals’).

1.s: apuṣpāḥ phalavanto ye te vanaspatayaḥ smṛtāḥ puṣpiṇaḥ phalinaścaiva vṛkṣāstūbhayataḥ smṛtāḥ
1.d: अपुष्पाः फलवन्तो ये ते वनस्पतयः स्मृताः पुष्पिणः फलिनश्चैव वृक्षास्तूभयतः स्मृताः
1.e: Those trees that are called ‘vanaspati’ bear fruits without flowers; and those called ‘vṛkṣa’ bear both flowers and fruits.

1.s: gucchagulmaṃ tu vividhaṃ tathaiva tṛṇajātayaḥ bījakāṇḍaruhāṇyeva pratānā vallya eva ca
1.d: गुच्छगुल्मं तु विविधं तथैव तृणजातयः बीजकाण्डरुहाण्येव प्रताना वल्ल्य एव च
1.e: The various kinds op clumps and thickets, and the other species of grass, as also low-spreading tendrils and creepers—all these grow out of seeds and slips.

1.s: tamasā bahurūpeṇa veṣṭitāḥ karmahetunā antassaṃjñā bhavantyete sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ
1.d: तमसा बहुरूपेण वेष्टिताः कर्महेतुना अन्तस्संज्ञा भवन्त्येते सुखदुःखसमन्विताः
1.e: All these (vegetable beings) are invested by manifold ‘darkness’ (inertia), the result of their acts; and possessing inner consciousness, they are affected by pleasure and pain.

1.s: etadantāstu gatayo brahmādyāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ ghore 'smin bhūtasaṃsāre nityaṃ satatayāyini
1.d: एतदन्तास्तु गतयो ब्रह्माद्याः समुदाहृताः घोरे ऽस्मिन् भूतसंसारे नित्यं सततयायिनि
1.e: Thus have been described the conditions of life, beginning with brahmā and ending with those just mentioned, which occur in this ever frightful and constantly fluctuating cycle of births and deaths of created beings.

1.s: evaṃ sarvaṃ sa sṛṣṭvaidaṃ māṃ cācintyaparākramaḥ ātmanyantardadhe bhūyaḥ kālaṃ kālena pīḍayan
1.d: एवं सर्वं स सृष्ट्वैदं मां चाचिन्त्यपराक्रमः आत्मन्यन्तर्दधे भूयः कालं कालेन पीडयन्
1.e: Thus repeatedly suppressing time (of dissolution) by time (of creation and maintenance), he, of inconceivable power, created all this and also myself; [he directed me to maintain it] and then disappeared within himself.

1.s: yadā sa devo jāgarti tadevaṃ ceṣṭate jagat yadā svapiti śāntātmā tadā sarvaṃ nimīlati
1.d: यदा स देवो जागर्ति तदेवं चेष्टते जगत् यदा स्वपिति शान्तात्मा तदा सर्वं निमीलति
1.e: When that divine being is awake, then this world is active; when he slumbers, with his mind in calm repose, then all vanishes.

1.s: tasmin svapiti tu svasthe karmātmānaḥ śarīriṇaḥ svapati svakarmabhyo nivartante manaśca glāniṃ ṛcchati
1.d: तस्मिन् स्वपिति तु स्वस्थे कर्मात्मानः शरीरिणः स्वपति स्वकर्मभ्यो निवर्तन्ते मनश्च ग्लानिं ऋच्छति
1.e: When he slumbers, having retired within himself, all active embodied beings desist from their actions, and their mind falls into depression.

1.s: yugapat tu pralīyante yadā tasmin mahātmani tadā 'yaṃ sarvabhūtātmā sukhaṃ svapiti nirvṛtaḥ
1.d: युगपत् तु प्रलीयन्ते यदा तस्मिन् महात्मनि तदा ऽयं सर्वभूतात्मा सुखं स्वपिति निर्वृतः
1.e: When this Soul of all things sleeps happy and contented, then all things become absorbed all at once in that Great Soul.

1.s: tamo 'yaṃ tu samāśritya ciraṃ tiṣṭhati saindriyaḥ na ca svaṃ kurute karma tadautkrāmati mūrtitaḥ
1.d: तमो ऽयं तु समाश्रित्य चिरं तिष्ठति सैन्द्रियः न च स्वं कुरुते कर्म तदौत्क्रामति मूर्तितः
1.e: This (individual Soul), on entering into ‘Darkness,’ remains, for a long time, equipped with the sense-organs, but does not perform its functions; then it departs from the body.

1.s: yadā 'ṇumātriko bhūtvā bījaṃ sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca samāviśati saṃsṛṣṭastadā mūrtiṃ vimuñcati
1.d: यदा ऽणुमात्रिको भूत्वा बीजं स्थास्नु चरिष्णु च समाविशति संसृष्टस्तदा मूर्तिं विमुञ्चति
1.e: When, invested with minute particles, the Individual enters the moveable or immoveable Seed;—then, becoming united with the aforesaid (Subtile body), it assumes the (new) body.

1.s: evaṃ sa jāgratsvapnābhyāmidaṃ sarvaṃ carācaram sañjīvayati cājasraṃ pramāpayati cāvyayaḥ
1.d: एवं स जाग्रत्स्वप्नाभ्यामिदं सर्वं चराचरम् सञ्जीवयति चाजस्रं प्रमापयति चाव्ययः
1.e: Thus by waking and sleeping, the Imperishable One incessantly brings to like and destroys all this that is moveable and immoveable.

1.s: idaṃ śāstraṃ tu kṛtvā 'sau māmeva svayamāditaḥ vidhivadgrāhayāmāsa marīciādīṃstvahaṃ munīn
1.d: इदं शास्त्रं तु कृत्वा ऽसौ मामेव स्वयमादितः विधिवद्ग्राहयामास मरीचिआदींस्त्वहं मुनीन्
1.e: Having prounded this Law, he himself, first of all, taught it to me with due care; I then taught it to Marīci and other Sages.

1.s: etadvo 'yaṃ bhṛguḥ śāstraṃ śrāvayiṣyatyaśesataḥ etaddhi matto 'dhijage sarvameṣo 'khilaṃ muniḥ
1.d: एतद्वो ऽयं भृगुः शास्त्रं श्रावयिष्यत्यशेसतः एतद्धि मत्तो ऽधिजगे सर्वमेषो ऽखिलं मुनिः
1.e: This Bhṛgu will fully describe to you this (Law); this sage has learnt the whole of this in its entirety, from me.

1.s: tatastathā sa tenaukto maharṣimanunā bhṛguḥ tānabravīdṛṣīn sarvān prītātmā śrūyatāmiti
1.d: ततस्तथा स तेनौक्तो महर्षिमनुना भृगुः तानब्रवीदृषीन् सर्वान् प्रीतात्मा श्रूयतामिति
1.e: Thereupon, being thus directed by Manu, the great sage Bhṛgu, with a gladdened heart, said to the sages—‘Listen.’

1.s: svāyaṃbhuvasyāsya manoḥ ṣaḍvaṃśyā manavo 'pare sṛṣṭavantaḥ prajāḥ svāḥ svā mahātmāno mahaujasaḥ
1.d: स्वायंभुवस्यास्य मनोः षड्वंश्या मनवो ऽपरे सृष्टवन्तः प्रजाः स्वाः स्वा महात्मानो महौजसः
1.e: There are Six other Manus, high-souled and mighty, who belong to the same race as this Svāyambhuva Manu, and have called into being, each his own offsprings.

1.s: svārociṣaścauttamaśca tāmaso raivatastathā cākṣuṣaśca mahātejā vivasvatsuta eva ca
1.d: स्वारोचिषश्चौत्तमश्च तामसो रैवतस्तथा चाक्षुषश्च महातेजा विवस्वत्सुत एव च
1.e: [These six Manus are]—Svārociṣa, Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata, Cākṣuṣa, and the glorious Vivasvat-suta (the Son of Vivasvat).

1.s: svāyaṃbhuvādyāḥ saptaite manavo bhūritejasaḥ sve sve 'ntare sarvamidamutpādyāpuścarācaram
1.d: स्वायंभुवाद्याः सप्तैते मनवो भूरितेजसः स्वे स्वे ऽन्तरे सर्वमिदमुत्पाद्यापुश्चराचरम्
1.e: These seven almighty Manus, of whom Svāyambhuva is the first, having called into existence the whole of this world, consisting of movable and immovable beings, sustained it, each during his own regime.

1.s: nimeṣā daśa cāṣṭau ca kāṣṭhā triṃśat tu tāḥ kalā triṃśat kalā muhūrtaḥ syādahorātraṃ tu tāvataḥ
1.d: निमेषा दश चाष्टौ च काष्ठा त्रिंशत् तु ताः कला त्रिंशत् कला मुहूर्तः स्यादहोरात्रं तु तावतः
1.e: Ten and eight ‘nimeṣas’ (should be known as) one ‘Kāṣṭhā’; thirty such (Kāṣṭhās) one ‘Kalā’; thirty ‘Kalās’ one ‘muhūrta’; and as many ‘muhūrtas’ one ‘Ahorātra’ (Day and Night).

1.s: ahorātre vibhajate sūryo mānuṣadaivike rātriḥ svapnāya bhūtānāṃ ceṣṭāyai karmaṇāmahaḥ
1.d: अहोरात्रे विभजते सूर्यो मानुषदैविके रात्रिः स्वप्नाय भूतानां चेष्टायै कर्मणामहः
1.e: The Sun divides the ‘Day’ and ‘Night’ of Men and Gods; [of others] what is conducive to the repose of beings is ‘Night,’ and what is conducive to activity is ‘Day.’

1.s: pitrye rātriahanī māsaḥ pravibhāgastu pakṣayoḥ karmaceṣṭāsvahaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śuklaḥ svapnāya śarvarī
1.d: पित्र्ये रात्रिअहनी मासः प्रविभागस्तु पक्षयोः कर्मचेष्टास्वहः कृष्णः शुक्लः स्वप्नाय शर्वरी
1.e: One month (of men) forms the ‘day and night’ of the ‘Pitṛs’; and their division is by fortnights: the darker fortnight, conducive to activity, is ‘Day,’ and the lighter fortnight, conducive to repose, is ‘Night.’

1.s: daive rātriahanī varṣaṃ pravibhāgastayoḥ punaḥ ahastatraudagayanaṃ rātriḥ syāddakṣiṇāyanam
1.d: दैवे रात्रिअहनी वर्षं प्रविभागस्तयोः पुनः अहस्तत्रौदगयनं रात्रिः स्याद्दक्षिणायनम्
1.e: One ‘year’ (of men) forms the ‘Day and Night’ of the Gods; and the division of these is that the ‘Northern course’ is the ‘Day,’ and the ‘Southern Course’ the ‘Night.’

1.s: brāhmasya tu kṣapāhasya yat pramāṇaṃ samāsataḥ ekaikaśo yugānāṃ tu kramaśastannibodhata
1.d: ब्राह्मस्य तु क्षपाहस्य यत् प्रमाणं समासतः एकैकशो युगानां तु क्रमशस्तन्निबोधत
1.e: Learn in brief, in due order, the measure of the Brahmic ‘day and night,’ as also that of the ‘Time-cycles’ (Yugas) one by one.

1.s: catvāryāhuḥ sahasrāṇi varsāṇāṃ tat kṛtaṃ yugam tasya tāvatśatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ
1.d: चत्वार्याहुः सहस्राणि वर्साणां तत् कृतं युगम् तस्य तावत्शती संध्या संध्यांशश्च तथाविधः
1.e: They say that four thousnd ‘years’ are what is the ‘Kṛta-cycle’; as many hundred ‘years’ form the ‘Juncture’ (Morning); and of equal measure is the ‘Juncture-end’ (Evening).

1.s: itareṣu sasaṃdhyeṣu sasaṃdhyāṃśeṣu ca triṣu ekāpāyena vartante sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
1.d: इतरेषु ससंध्येषु ससंध्यांशेषु च त्रिषु एकापायेन वर्तन्ते सहस्राणि शतानि च
1.e: In each of the other time-cycles, along with their ‘junctures’ and ‘juncture-ends’, the ‘thousands’ and ‘hundreds’ are reduced by one.

1.s: yadetat parisaṅkhyātamādāveva caturyugam etaddvādaśasāhasraṃ devānāṃ yugamucyate
1.d: यदेतत् परिसङ्ख्यातमादावेव चतुर्युगम् एतद्द्वादशसाहस्रं देवानां युगमुच्यते
1.e: This period of the four time-cycles that have been just computed,—twelve thousand such periods are called the ‘time-cycle of the gods.’

1.s: daivikānāṃ yugānāṃ tu sahasraṃ parisaṅkhyayā brāhmamekamaharjñeyaṃ tāvatīṃ rātrimeva ca tāvatī rātrireva ca
1.d: दैविकानां युगानां तु सहस्रं परिसङ्ख्यया ब्राह्ममेकमहर्ज्ञेयं तावतीं रात्रिमेव च तावती रात्रिरेव च
1.e: The ‘Time-cycles’ of the Gods, one thousand in number, should be regarded as one ‘day’ of brahmā; and (his) ‘night’ also is of the same extent.

1.s: tadvai yugasahasrāntaṃ brāhmaṃ puṇyamaharviduḥ rātriṃ ca tāvatīmeva te 'horātravido janāḥ
1.d: तद्वै युगसहस्रान्तं ब्राह्मं पुण्यमहर्विदुः रात्रिं च तावतीमेव ते ऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः
1.e: Those who know the ‘Day of Brahmā’ as ending with the (said) thousand ‘time-cycles,’ and the ‘night’ also as of the same extent,—are people who alone know what is ‘day and night’, and acquire merit.

1.s: tasya so 'harṃiśasyānte prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate pratibuddhaśca sṛjati manaḥ sadasadātmakam
1.d: तस्य सो ऽहर्ंइशस्यान्ते प्रसुप्तः प्रतिबुध्यते प्रतिबुद्धश्च सृजति मनः सदसदात्मकम्
1.e: At the end of the said ‘Day and Night,’ Brahmā, who was asleep, wakes up, and ha vino woken up, he creates mind, which partakes op the nature op the existent and the non-existent.

1.s: manaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute codyamānaṃ sisṛkṣayā ākāśaṃ jāyate tasmāt tasya śabdaṃ guṇaṃ viduḥ
1.d: मनः सृष्टिं विकुरुते चोद्यमानं सिसृक्षया आकाशं जायते तस्मात् तस्य शब्दं गुणं विदुः
1.e: The ‘Mind’ impelled by (Brahmā’s) desire to create, evolves creation;—from out of that (Mind) is produced Ākāśa; of this they know sound to be the quality.

1.s: ākāśāt tu vikurvāṇāt sarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ balavāñjāyate vāyuḥ sa vai sparśaguṇo mataḥ
1.d: आकाशात् तु विकुर्वाणात् सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः बलवाञ्जायते वायुः स वै स्पर्शगुणो मतः
1.e: After Ākāśa, from out of the same evolvent [‘Mind’], there comes into existence the pure and potent Wind, the vehicle of all odours; and it is held to be endowed with the quality of Touch.

1.s: vāyorapi vikurvāṇādvirociṣṇu tamonudam jyotirutpadyate bhāsvat tadrūpaguṇamucyate
1.d: वायोरपि विकुर्वाणाद्विरोचिष्णु तमोनुदम् ज्योतिरुत्पद्यते भास्वत् तद्रूपगुणमुच्यते
1.e: After wind, from out of the same Evolvent, emanates the bright and radiant light, the dispeller of darkness; it is said to be endowed with the quality of colour.

1.s: jyotiṣaśca vikurvāṇādāpo rasaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ adbhyo gandhaguṇā bhūmirityeṣā sṛṣṭirāditaḥ
1.d: ज्योतिषश्च विकुर्वाणादापो रसगुणाः स्मृताः अद्भ्यो गन्धगुणा भूमिरित्येषा सृष्टिरादितः
1.e: After light, from out of the same Evolvent, emanates water, which has been declared to be endowed with the quality of taste. and after water, comes earth, endowed with the quality of odour.—Such is creation at the outset.

1.s: yadprāg dvādaśasāhasramuditaṃ daivikaṃ yugam tadekasaptatiguṇaṃ manvantaramihaucyate
1.d: यद्प्राग् द्वादशसाहस्रमुदितं दैविकं युगम् तदेकसप्ततिगुणं मन्वन्तरमिहौच्यते
1.e: The ‘Time-cycle of the Gods’ which has been described above as consisting of ‘twelve thousand periods,’—this multiplied by ‘seventy-one’ forms what is known here as ‘Manvantara’ (Regime of a Manu).

1.s: manvantarāṇyasaṅkhyāni sargaḥ saṃhāra eva ca krīḍannivaitat kurute parameṣṭhī punaḥ punaḥ
1.d: मन्वन्तराण्यसङ्ख्यानि सर्गः संहार एव च क्रीडन्निवैतत् कुरुते परमेष्ठी पुनः पुनः
1.e: Innumerable Manvantaras, as also Creation and Dissolution—all this the supreme lord calls into being again and again, as if in amusement

1.s: catuṣpāt sakalo dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiva kṛte yuge nādharmeṇāgamaḥ kaścin manuṣyān prati vartate upavartate
1.d: चतुष्पात् सकलो धर्मः सत्यं चैव कृते युगे नाधर्मेणागमः कश्चिन् मनुष्यान् प्रति वर्तते उपवर्तते
1.e: In the Kṛta Cycle Virtue exists in its perfect form, with all its four feet; and so does Truth;—No benefit accrues to men by vice

1.s: itareṣvāgamāddharmaḥ pādaśastvavaropitaḥ caurikānṛtamāyābhirdharmaścāpaiti pādaśaḥ
1.d: इतरेष्वागमाद्धर्मः पादशस्त्ववरोपितः चौरिकानृतमायाभिर्धर्मश्चापैति पादशः
1.e: In the other Cycles, virtue fell off from the scriptures, foot by foot; and on account of theft, falsehood and fraud, virtuous acts deteriorated foot by foot

1.s: arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāścaturvarṣaśatāyuṣaḥ kṛte tretādiṣu hyeṣāmāyurhrasati pādaśaḥ vayo hrasati
1.d: अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश्चतुर्वर्षशतायुषः कृते त्रेतादिषु ह्येषामायुर्ह्रसति पादशः वयो ह्रसति
1.e: During the Kṛta Cycle, men are free from disease, they have all their aims fulfilled, and their life lasts trhough four hundred years;—During the Tretā and other Cycles, their life becomes shortened, quarter by quarter.

1.s: vedauktamāyurmartyānāmāśiṣaścaiva karmaṇām phalantyanuyugaṃ loke prabhāvaśca śarīriṇām
1.d: वेदौक्तमायुर्मर्त्यानामाशिषश्चैव कर्मणाम् फलन्त्यनुयुगं लोके प्रभावश्च शरीरिणाम्
1.e: The full age of mortals spoken of in the Veda, the results of actions and the powers of embodied beings,—are obtained in accordance with the character of the Cycle.

1.s: anye kṛtayuge dharmāstretāyāṃ dvāpare 'pare pare anye kaliyuge nr̥̄ṇāṃ yugahrāsānurūpataḥ
1.d: अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरे ऽपरे परे अन्ये कलियुगे न्र्̥̄णां युगह्रासानुरूपतः
1.e: During the Kṛta-cycle, the characteristics of men are of one kind,—of different kinds during the Tretā and the dvāpara,—and of yet another kind during the Kali-cycle;—this being due to the deterioration of each suceeding Cycle.

1.s: tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānamucyate dvāpare yajñamevāhurdānamekaṃ kalau yuge
1.d: तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानमुच्यते द्वापरे यज्ञमेवाहुर्दानमेकं कलौ युगे
1.e: In the Kṛta Cycle, ‘Austerity’ is the highest; in the Tretā ‘knowledge’ is described as such; in the Dvāpara they call the ‘Sacrifice’ the highest, and ‘Charity’ alone in the Kali-Cycle

1.s: sarvasyāsya tu sargasya guptiarthaṃ sa mahādyutiḥ mukhabāhūrupajjānāṃ pṛthakkarmāṇyakalpayat
1.d: सर्वस्यास्य तु सर्गस्य गुप्तिअर्थं स महाद्युतिः मुखबाहूरुपज्जानां पृथक्कर्माण्यकल्पयत्
1.e: With a view to the protection of this entire creation, the Resplendent One ordained the distinct functions of those who sprang from the mouth, the arms, the thighs and the feet

1.s: adhyāpanamadhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tathā dānaṃ pratigrahaṃ caiva brāhmaṇānāmakalpayat
1.d: अध्यापनमध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा दानं प्रतिग्रहं चैव ब्राह्मणानामकल्पयत्
1.e: For the Brāhmaṇas he ordained teaching, studying, sacrificing and officiating at sacrifices, as also the giving and accepting of gifts.

1.s: prajānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānamijyā 'dhyayanameva ca viṣayeṣvaprasaktiśca kṣatriyasya samāsataḥ samādiśat
1.d: प्रजानां रक्षणं दानमिज्या ऽध्ययनमेव च विषयेष्वप्रसक्तिश्च क्षत्रियस्य समासतः समादिशत्
1.e: For the Kṣatriya he ordained protecting of the people, giving of gifts, sacrificing and studying, as also abstaining prom being addicted to the objects of sense.

1.s: paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānamijyā 'dhyayanameva ca vaṇikpathaṃ kusīdaṃ ca vaiśyasya kṛṣimeva ca
1.d: पशूनां रक्षणं दानमिज्या ऽध्ययनमेव च वणिक्पथं कुसीदं च वैश्यस्य कृषिमेव च
1.e: For the Vaiśya, tending of cattle, giving of gifts, sacrificing and studying; as also trade, money-lending and cultivating of land.

1.s: ekameva tu śūdrasya prabhuḥ karma samādiśat eteṣāmeva varṇānāṃ śuśrūṣāmanasūyayā
1.d: एकमेव तु शूद्रस्य प्रभुः कर्म समादिशत् एतेषामेव वर्णानां शुश्रूषामनसूयया
1.e: For the Śūdra the Lord ordained only one function: the ungrudging service of the said castes.

1.s: ūrdhvaṃ nābhermedhyataraḥ puruṣaḥ parikīrtitaḥ tasmān medhyatamaṃ tvasya mukhamuktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā
1.d: ऊर्ध्वं नाभेर्मेध्यतरः पुरुषः परिकीर्तितः तस्मान् मेध्यतमं त्वस्य मुखमुक्तं स्वयंभुवा
1.e: Man is described as purer above his naval; hence the Self-existent One has declared the mouth to be his purest part.

1.s: uttamāṅgaudbhavāj jyeṣṭhyādbrahmaṇaścaiva dhāraṇāt jyaiṣṭhyād sarvasyaivāsya sargasya dharmato brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
1.d: उत्तमाङ्गौद्भवाज् ज्येष्ठ्याद्ब्रह्मणश्चैव धारणात् ज्यैष्ठ्याद् सर्वस्यैवास्य सर्गस्य धर्मतो ब्राह्मणः प्रभुः
1.e: In matters regauding ‘Dharma’, the Brāhmaṇa is the Lord of this whole world;—because he sprang out of the best part of (Prajāpati’s) body, because he is the eldest ok all, and because he upholds the Veda.

1.s: taṃ hi svayaṃbhūḥ svādāsyāt tapastaptvā 'dito 'sṛjat havyakavyābhivāhyāya sarvasyāsya ca guptaye
1.d: तं हि स्वयंभूः स्वादास्यात् तपस्तप्त्वा ऽदितो ऽसृजत् हव्यकव्याभिवाह्याय सर्वस्यास्य च गुप्तये
1.e: Him the Sself-existent one, after performing austerities, created, in the beginning, out of his own mouth, for the conveying of offerings (to the gods) and of oblations (to the Pitṛs), and for the preservation of this entire creation.

1.s: yasyāsyena sadā 'śnanti havyāni tridivokasaḥ kavyāni caiva pitaraḥ kiṃ bhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ
1.d: यस्यास्येन सदा ऽश्नन्ति हव्यानि त्रिदिवोकसः कव्यानि चैव पितरः किं भूतमधिकं ततः
1.e: What being is superior to him through whose mouth the gods always eat the offerings and the Pitṛs the oblations?

1.s: bhūtānāṃ prāṇinaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prāṇināṃ buddhijīvinaḥ buddhimatsu narāḥ śreṣṭhā nareṣu brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
1.d: भूतानां प्राणिनः श्रेष्ठाः प्राणिनां बुद्धिजीविनः बुद्धिमत्सु नराः श्रेष्ठा नरेषु ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः
1.e: Among beings, aminated ones are regarded as foremost; among aminated ones, those that subsist by reason: among rational beings men are foremost; and among men, Brāhmaṇas.

1.s: brāhmaṇeṣu ca vidvāṃso vidvatsu kṛtabuddhayaḥ kṛtabuddhiṣu kartāraḥ kartṛṣu brahmavedinaḥ
1.d: ब्राह्मणेषु च विद्वांसो विद्वत्सु कृतबुद्धयः कृतबुद्धिषु कर्तारः कर्तृषु ब्रह्मवेदिनः
1.e: Among Brāhmaṇas, the learned are the best, among the learned, those with firm convictions, among the men with firm convictions, those that act up to them; and among the actors, those that know Brahman.

1.s: utpattireva viprasya mūrtirdharmasya śāśvatī sa hi dharmārthamutpanno brahmabhūyāya kalpate
1.d: उत्पत्तिरेव विप्रस्य मूर्तिर्धर्मस्य शाश्वती स हि धर्मार्थमुत्पन्नो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते
1.e: The very genesis of the Brāhmaṇa is the eternal incarnation of Virtue; for he is born for the sake of Virtue; and this (birth) leads to the state of Brahman.

1.s: brāhmaṇo jāyamāno hi pṛthivyāmadhijāyate īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmakośasya guptaye
1.d: ब्राह्मणो जायमानो हि पृथिव्यामधिजायते ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां धर्मकोशस्य गुप्तये
1.e: The Brāhmaṇa, on coming into existence, becomes supreme on earth; he is the supreme lord of all beings, serving the purpose of guarding the treasure of Virtue.

1.s: sarvaṃ svaṃ brāhmaṇasyaidaṃ yat kiṃ citjagatīgatam śraiṣṭhyenābhijanenaidaṃ sarvaṃ vai brāhmaṇo 'rhati
1.d: सर्वं स्वं ब्राह्मणस्यैदं यत् किं चित्जगतीगतम् श्रैष्ठ्येनाभिजनेनैदं सर्वं वै ब्राह्मणो ऽर्हति
1.e: Whatever is contained in this world is all the property of the Brāhmaṇa; the Brāhmaṇa verily deserves all by virtue of his superiority and noble birth.

1.s: svameva brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte svaṃ vaste svaṃ dadāti ca ānṛśaṃsyādbrāhmaṇasya bhuñjate hītare janāḥ
1.d: स्वमेव ब्राह्मणो भुङ्क्ते स्वं वस्ते स्वं ददाति च आनृशंस्याद्ब्राह्मणस्य भुञ्जते हीतरे जनाः
1.e: What the Brāhmana eats is his own; his own what he wears and his own also what he gives; it ts due to the good will of the Brāhmaṇa that other people enjoy (things).

1.s: tasya karmavivekārthaṃ śeṣāṇāmanupūrvaśaḥ svāyaṃbhuvo manurdhīmānidaṃ śāstramakalpayat
1.d: तस्य कर्मविवेकार्थं शेषाणामनुपूर्वशः स्वायंभुवो मनुर्धीमानिदं शास्त्रमकल्पयत्
1.e: It was for the purpose of regulating the actions of the Brāhmaṇa,—and incidentally of others also,—that the wise Manu Svāyambhuva Elaborated these institutes.

1.s: viduṣā brāhmaṇenaidamadhyetavyaṃ prayatnataḥ śiśyebhyaśca pravaktavyaṃ samyalg nānyena kena cit
1.d: विदुषा ब्राह्मणेनैदमध्येतव्यं प्रयत्नतः शिश्येभ्यश्च प्रवक्तव्यं सम्यल्ग् नान्येन केन चित्
1.e: This may he studied with care, and duly taught to pupils, by the learned Brāhmaṇa,—not by any one else.

1.s: idaṃ śāstram adhīyāno brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ manasvācdehajairnityaṃ karmadoṣairna lipyate
1.d: इदं शास्त्रम् अधीयानो ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः मनस्वाच्देहजैर्नित्यं कर्मदोषैर्न लिप्यते
1.e: The Brāhmaṇa studying these institutes, and (thence) discharging all prescribed duties, is never defiled by sins of commission (or omission), proceeding from mind, speech or body.

1.s: punāti paṅktiṃ vaṃśyāṃśca saptasapta parāvarān pṛthivīmapi caivaimāṃ kṛtsnāmeko 'pi so 'rhati
1.d: पुनाति पङ्क्तिं वंश्यांश्च सप्तसप्त परावरान् पृथिवीमपि चैवैमां कृत्स्नामेको ऽपि सो ऽर्हति
1.e: He purifies his company, and also his kindreds—seven higher (ancestors) and seven lower (descendants). he alone deserves this entire earth.

1.s: idaṃ svastyayanaṃ śreṣṭhamidaṃ buddhivivardhanam idaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ idaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ param idaṃ yaśasyaṃ satatam
1.d: इदं स्वस्त्ययनं श्रेष्ठमिदं बुद्धिविवर्धनम् इदं यशस्यमायुष्यं इदं निःश्रेयसं परम् इदं यशस्यं सततम्
1.e: This (treatise) is ever conducive to welfare; it is most excellent; it expands the understanding brings fame and constitutes the highest good.

1.s: asmin dharmo 'khilenaukto guṇadoṣau ca karmaṇām caturṇāmapi varṇānāmācāraścaiva śāśvataḥ
1.d: अस्मिन् धर्मो ऽखिलेनौक्तो गुणदोषौ च कर्मणाम् चतुर्णामपि वर्णानामाचारश्चैव शाश्वतः
1.e: Herein has been expounded Dharma in its entirety: the good and bad features of actions of all the four castes; as also eternal Morality.

1.s: ācāraḥ paramo dharmaḥ śrutyoktaḥ smārta eva ca tasmādasmin sadā yukto nityaṃ syādātmavān dvijaḥ
1.d: आचारः परमो धर्मः श्रुत्योक्तः स्मार्त एव च तस्मादस्मिन् सदा युक्तो नित्यं स्यादात्मवान् द्विजः
1.e: Morality [Right Behaviour] is highest Dharma; that which is prescribed in the śruti and laid down in the Smṛti. hence the twice-born person, desiring the welfare of his soul, should be always intent upon Right Behaviour.

1.s: ācārādvicyuto vipro na vedaphalamaśnute ācāreṇa tu saṃyuktaḥ sampūrṇaphalabhāj bhavet saṃpūrṇaphalabhāk smṛtaḥ
1.d: आचाराद्विच्युतो विप्रो न वेदफलमश्नुते आचारेण तु संयुक्तः सम्पूर्णफलभाज् भवेत् संपूर्णफलभाक् स्मृतः
1.e: The Brāhmaṇa who departs from Right Behaviour, does not obtain the fruit of the Veda; he however who is equipped with Right Behaviour obtains the full reward.

1.s: evamācārato dṛṣṭvā dharmasya munayo gatim sarvasya tapaso mūlamācāraṃ jagṛhuḥ param
1.d: एवमाचारतो दृष्ट्वा धर्मस्य मुनयो गतिम् सर्वस्य तपसो मूलमाचारं जगृहुः परम्
1.e: Having thus seen that virtue is got at from Right Behaviour, the sages regarded Right Behaviour as the very root of all Austerity.

1.s: jagataśca samutpattiṃ saṃskāravidhimeva ca vratacaryaupacāraṃ ca snānasya ca paraṃ vidhim
1.d: जगतश्च समुत्पत्तिं संस्कारविधिमेव च व्रतचर्यौपचारं च स्नानस्य च परं विधिम्
1.e: The coming into existence of the world,—the rule relating to the sacramental Rites,—the method of keeping observances,—as also the excellent rules bearing upon the Final Ablution.

1.s: dārādhigamanaṃ caiva vivāhānāṃ ca lakṣaṇam mahāyajñavidhānaṃ ca śrāddhakalpaṃ ca śāśvatam
1.d: दाराधिगमनं चैव विवाहानां च लक्षणम् महायज्ञविधानं च श्राद्धकल्पं च शाश्वतम्
1.e: The taking of wife,—the definition of the several forms of Marriage,—the method of the Great Sacrifices,—the eternal regulations relating to the offering toPitṛs.

1.s: vṛttīnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ caiva snātakasya vratāni ca bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ śuddhimeva ca
1.d: वृत्तीनां लक्षणं चैव स्नातकस्य व्रतानि च भक्ष्याभक्ष्यं च शौचं च द्रव्याणां शुद्धिमेव च
1.e: The duty of the Vaiśya and the Śūdra,—the birth of the mixed castes—the duties of all castes during times of distress—the method of expiation.

1.s: strīdharmayogaṃ tāpasyaṃ mokṣaṃ saṃnyāsameva ca rājñaśca dharmamakhilaṃ kāryāṇāṃ ca vinirṇayam
1.d: स्त्रीधर्मयोगं तापस्यं मोक्षं संन्यासमेव च राज्ञश्च धर्ममखिलं कार्याणां च विनिर्णयम्
1.e: The duty of the Vaiśya and the Śūdra,—the birth of the mixed castes—the duties of all castes during times of distress—the method of expiation.

1.s: sākṣipraśnavidhānaṃ ca dharmaṃ strīpuṃsayorapi vibhāgadharmaṃ dyūtaṃ ca kaṇṭakānāṃ ca śodhanam
1.d: साक्षिप्रश्नविधानं च धर्मं स्त्रीपुंसयोरपि विभागधर्मं द्यूतं च कण्टकानां च शोधनम्
1.e: The duty of the Vaiśya and the Śūdra,—the birth of the mixed castes—the duties of all castes during times of distress—the method of expiation.

1.s: vaiśyaśūdraupacāraṃ ca saṅkīrṇānāṃ ca saṃbhavam āpaddharmaṃ ca varṇānāṃ prāyaścittavidhiṃ tathā
1.d: वैश्यशूद्रौपचारं च सङ्कीर्णानां च संभवम् आपद्धर्मं च वर्णानां प्रायश्चित्तविधिं तथा
1.e: The duty of the Vaiśya and the Śūdra,—the birth of the mixed castes—the duties of all castes during times of distress—the method of expiation.

1.s: saṃsāragamanaṃ caiva trividhaṃ karmasaṃbhavam niḥśreyasaṃ karmaṇāṃ ca guṇadoṣaparīkṣaṇam
1.d: संसारगमनं चैव त्रिविधं कर्मसंभवम् निःश्रेयसं कर्मणां च गुणदोषपरीक्षणम्
1.e: The threefold transmigration of the Soul, arising from actions,—the highest good,—and the examination of the good and bad features of actions.

1.s: deśadharmānjātidharmān kuladharmāṃśca śāśvatān pāṣaṇḍagaṇadharmāṃśca śāstre 'sminnuktavān manuḥ
1.d: देशधर्मान्जातिधर्मान् कुलधर्मांश्च शाश्वतान् पाषण्डगणधर्मांश्च शास्त्रे ऽस्मिन्नुक्तवान् मनुः
1.e: The eternal laws op countries, duties op castes and laws of dynasties,—also the laws relating to heretics and to guilds,—all this manu has expounded in these Institutes.

1.s: yathaidamuktavāṃśāstraṃ purā pṛṣṭo manurmayā tathaidaṃ yūyamapyadya matsakāśātnibodhata
1.d: यथैदमुक्तवांशास्त्रं पुरा पृष्टो मनुर्मया तथैदं यूयमप्यद्य मत्सकाशात्निबोधत

2.s: vidvadbhiḥ sevitaḥ sadbhirnityamadveṣarāgibhiḥ hṛdayenābhyanujñāto yo dharmastaṃ nibodhata
2.d: विद्वद्भिः सेवितः सद्भिर्नित्यमद्वेषरागिभिः हृदयेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो यो धर्मस्तं निबोधत
2.e: Learn that Dharma, which has been ever followed by, and sanctioned by the heart of, the learned and the good, who are free from love and hate.

2.s: kāmātmatā na praśastā na caivaihāstyakāmatā kāmyo hi vedādhigamaḥ karmayogaśca vaidikaḥ
2.d: कामात्मता न प्रशस्ता न चैवैहास्त्यकामता काम्यो हि वेदाधिगमः कर्मयोगश्च वैदिकः
2.e: It is not right to be absorbed in desires—“But there is in this world, no absolute absence of desire; for the study of the Vedas itself is prompted by desire, as also every act prescribed in the Veda.”

2.s: saṅkalpamūlaḥ kāmo vai yajñāḥ saṅkalpasaṃbhavāḥ vratāni yamadharmāśca sarve saṅkalpajāḥ smṛtāḥ
2.d: सङ्कल्पमूलः कामो वै यज्ञाः सङ्कल्पसंभवाः व्रतानि यमधर्माश्च सर्वे सङ्कल्पजाः स्मृताः
2.e: Desire has its root in Thought; Sacrifices proceed from Thought; Vows and Restraints—all these have been described as originating in Thought.

2.s: akāmasya kriyā kā ciddṛśyate naiha karhi cit yadyaddhi kurute kiṃ cit tat tat kāmasya ceṣṭitam
2.d: अकामस्य क्रिया का चिद्दृश्यते नैह कर्हि चित् यद्यद्धि कुरुते किं चित् तत् तत् कामस्य चेष्टितम्
2.e: No action is ever found in this world to be done by a man entirely without desires; whatever a man does is. the outcome of desire.

2.s: teṣu samyag vartamāno gacchatyamaralokatām yathā saṅkalpitāṃścaiha sarvān kāmān samaśnute
2.d: तेषु सम्यग् वर्तमानो गच्छत्यमरलोकताम् यथा सङ्कल्पितांश्चैह सर्वान् कामान् समश्नुते
2.e: Behaving in the right manner, in regard to these (desires), a man attains the position of Immortals; and even in this world he obtains all the desires that he may have thought of.

2.s: vedo 'khilo dharmamūlaṃ smṛtiśīle ca tadvidām ācāraścaiva sādhūnāmātmanastuṣṭireva ca
2.d: वेदो ऽखिलो धर्ममूलं स्मृतिशीले च तद्विदाम् आचारश्चैव साधूनामात्मनस्तुष्टिरेव च
2.e: The entire Veda is the root-source of Dharma; also the Conscientious Recollection of righteous persons versed in the Veda, the Practice of Good (and learned) Men, and their self-satisfaction.

2.s: yaḥ kaścit kasya ciddharmo manunā parikīrtitaḥ sa sarvo 'bhihito vede sarvajñānamayo hi saḥ
2.d: यः कश्चित् कस्य चिद्धर्मो मनुना परिकीर्तितः स सर्वो ऽभिहितो वेदे सर्वज्ञानमयो हि सः
2.e: Whatever Dharma for whatever person has been described by Manu,—all this is declared in the Veda; since the Veda embodies all knowledge.

2.s: sarvaṃ tu samavekṣyaidaṃ nikhilaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā śrutiprāmāṇyato vidvān svadharme niviśeta vai
2.d: सर्वं तु समवेक्ष्यैदं निखिलं ज्ञानचक्षुषा श्रुतिप्रामाण्यतो विद्वान् स्वधर्मे निविशेत वै
2.e: Having fully perceived all this with the eye of knowledge, the learned man should enter upon his own duties, resting upon the authority of the Revealed Word.

2.s: śrutismṛtyoditaṃ dharmamanutiṣṭhan hi mānavaḥ iha kīrtimavāpnoti pretya cānuttamaṃ sukham
2.d: श्रुतिस्मृत्योदितं धर्ममनुतिष्ठन् हि मानवः इह कीर्तिमवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चानुत्तमं सुखम्
2.e: For the man performing the duty laid down by the revealed word and the recollections obtains fame here, and after death, unsurpassed happiness.

2.s: śrutistu vedo vijñeyo dharmaśāstraṃ tu vai smṛtiḥ te sarvārtheṣvamīmāṃsye tābhyāṃ dharmo hi nirbabhau
2.d: श्रुतिस्तु वेदो विज्ञेयो धर्मशास्त्रं तु वै स्मृतिः ते सर्वार्थेष्वमीमांस्ये ताभ्यां धर्मो हि निर्बभौ
2.e: The Veda should be known as the ‘revealed word,’ and the Dharmaśāstra as the ‘recollections’; in all matters, these two do not deserve to be criticised, as it is out op these that Dharma shone forth.

2.s: yo 'vamanyeta te mūle hetuśāstrāśrayāddvijaḥ sa sādhubhirbahiṣkāryo nāstiko vedanindakaḥ
2.d: यो ऽवमन्येत ते मूले हेतुशास्त्राश्रयाद्द्विजः स साधुभिर्बहिष्कार्यो नास्तिको वेदनिन्दकः
2.e: If a twice-born person, relying upon the science of dialectics, should disregard these two sources, he should be cast out by good men,—the detractor of the Veda being an infidel.

2.s: vedaḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāraḥ svasya ca priyamātmanaḥ etaccaturvidhaṃ prāhuḥ sākṣāddharmasya lakṣaṇam
2.d: वेदः स्मृतिः सदाचारः स्वस्य च प्रियमात्मनः एतच्चतुर्विधं प्राहुः साक्षाद्धर्मस्य लक्षणम्
2.e: The Veda, the Smṛti, the Practice of cultured Men, and what is agreeable to oneself—these directly constitute the fourfold means of knowing Dharma.

2.s: arthakāmeṣvasaktānāṃ dharmajñānaṃ vidhīyate dharmaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ pramāṇaṃ paramaṃ śrutiḥ
2.d: अर्थकामेष्वसक्तानां धर्मज्ञानं विधीयते धर्मं जिज्ञासमानानां प्रमाणं परमं श्रुतिः
2.e: The knowledge of Dharma is ordained for those who are not addicted to the pursuit of wealth and pleasures; and for those seeking for the knowledge of Dharma, the Revealed Word is the highest authority.

2.s: śrutidvaidhaṃ tu yatra syāt tatra dharmāvubhau smṛtau ubhāvapi hi tau dharmau samyaguktau manīṣibhiḥ
2.d: श्रुतिद्वैधं तु यत्र स्यात् तत्र धर्मावुभौ स्मृतौ उभावपि हि तौ धर्मौ सम्यगुक्तौ मनीषिभिः
2.e: Where there is conflict between two Vedic texts, both are held to be Dharma; both have been rightly pronounced by the wise to be Dharma.

2.s: udite 'nudite caiva samayādhyuṣite tathā sarvathā vartate yajña itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ
2.d: उदिते ऽनुदिते चैव समयाध्युषिते तथा सर्वथा वर्तते यज्ञ इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः
2.e: At sunrise, or before sunrise, or at early dawn,—the sacrificial act may be performed at any time,—such is the pronouncement of the Veda.

2.s: niṣekādiśmaśānānto mantrairyasyaudito vidhiḥ tasya śāstre 'dhikāro 'smiñ jñeyo nānyasya kasya cit
2.d: निषेकादिश्मशानान्तो मन्त्रैर्यस्यौदितो विधिः तस्य शास्त्रे ऽधिकारो ऽस्मिञ् ज्ञेयो नान्यस्य कस्य चित्
2.e: That person alone, and none other, should be regarded as entitled to the scripture, for whom the sacraments beginning with conception and ending with the crematorium, are prescribed as to be done with mantras.

2.s: sarasvatīdṛśadvatyordevanadyoryadantaram taṃ devanirmitaṃ deśaṃ brahmāvartaṃ pracakṣate
2.d: सरस्वतीदृशद्वत्योर्देवनद्योर्यदन्तरम् तं देवनिर्मितं देशं ब्रह्मावर्तं प्रचक्षते
2.e: The region lying between the divine rivers Sarasvati and Dṛṣasvatī which has been created by the gods,—they call ‘Brahmāvarta’

2.s: tasmin deśe ya ācāraḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ varṇānāṃ sāntarālānāṃ sa sadācāra ucyate
2.d: तस्मिन् देशे य आचारः पारम्पर्यक्रमागतः वर्णानां सान्तरालानां स सदाचार उच्यते
2.e: That practice, which has comb down through an unbroken line op tradition among the several castes and subcastes in that country, is called the ‘Practice of Good Men.’

2.s: kurukṣetraṃ ca matsyāśca pañcālāḥ śūrasenakāḥ eṣa brahmarṣideśo vai brahmāvartādanantaraḥ
2.d: कुरुक्षेत्रं च मत्स्याश्च पञ्चालाः शूरसेनकाः एष ब्रह्मर्षिदेशो वै ब्रह्मावर्तादनन्तरः
2.e: Next to Brahmāvarta is the ‘Brahmarṣideśa,’ comprising the regions op Kurukṣetra, Matsyas, Pañchālas and Śukasenakas.

2.s: etaddeśaprasūtasya sakāśādagrajanmanaḥ svaṃ svaṃ caritraṃ śikṣeran pṛthivyāṃ sarvamānavāḥ
2.d: एतद्देशप्रसूतस्य सकाशादग्रजन्मनः स्वं स्वं चरित्रं शिक्षेरन् पृथिव्यां सर्वमानवाः
2.e: All men on the earth may learn their respective duties from the Brāhmaṇa born in these countries.

2.s: himavadvindhyayormadhyaṃ yat prāg vinaśanādapi pratyageva prayāgācca madhyadeśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
2.d: हिमवद्विन्ध्ययोर्मध्यं यत् प्राग् विनशनादपि प्रत्यगेव प्रयागाच्च मध्यदेशः प्रकीर्तितः
2.e: The country lying between the Himālaya and the Vindhya, to the east of Vinaśana and to the west of Prayāga, is called the ‘Madhyadeśa,’ the ‘Middle Country.’

2.s: ā samudrāt tu vai pūrvādā samudrācca paścimāt tayorevāntaraṃ giryorāryāvartaṃ vidurbudhāḥ
2.d: आ समुद्रात् तु वै पूर्वादा समुद्राच्च पश्चिमात् तयोरेवान्तरं गिर्योरार्यावर्तं विदुर्बुधाः
2.e: The country extending as far as the Eastern Ocean and as far as the Western Ocean, and lying between the same two mountains,—the learned know as ‘Āryāvarta.’

2.s: kṛṣṇasārastu carati mṛgo yatra svabhāvataḥ sa jñeyo yajñiyo deśo mlecchadeśastvataḥ paraḥ
2.d: कृष्णसारस्तु चरति मृगो यत्र स्वभावतः स ज्ञेयो यज्ञियो देशो म्लेच्छदेशस्त्वतः परः
2.e: But the region where the spotted deer roams by nature is to be known as the ‘land fit for sacrificial acts’; beyond that is the ‘land op the Mlecchas.’

2.s: etāṇ dvijātayo deśān saṃśrayeran prayatnataḥ śūdrastu yasmin kasmin vā nivasedvṛttikarśitaḥ yasmiṃstasmin vā
2.d: एताण् द्विजातयो देशान् संश्रयेरन् प्रयत्नतः शूद्रस्तु यस्मिन् कस्मिन् वा निवसेद्वृत्तिकर्शितः यस्मिंस्तस्मिन् वा
2.e: The twice-born people should seek to resort to these countries; the Śūdra may however, when distressed for a living, reside in any land.

2.s: eṣā dharmasya vo yoniḥ samāsena prakīrtitā saṃbhavaścāsya sarvasya varṇadharmānnibodhata
2.d: एषा धर्मस्य वो योनिः समासेन प्रकीर्तिता संभवश्चास्य सर्वस्य वर्णधर्मान्निबोधत
2.e: Thus has the source of Dharma been briefly explained to you, as also the origin of all this (world). Learn now the duties of the several castes.

2.s: vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyairniṣekādirdvijanmanām kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya caiha ca
2.d: वैदिकैः कर्मभिः पुण्यैर्निषेकादिर्द्विजन्मनाम् कार्यः शरीरसंस्कारः पावनः प्रेत्य चैह च
2.e: For the twice-born persons corporeal consecration, beginning with ‘Conception,’ should be performed with auspicious Vedic rites; it purifies in this world and also after death.

2.s: gārbhairhomairjātakarmacauḍamauñjīnibandhanaiḥ baijikaṃ gārbhikaṃ caino dvijānāmapamṛjyate
2.d: गार्भैर्होमैर्जातकर्मचौडमौञ्जीनिबन्धनैः बैजिकं गार्भिकं चैनो द्विजानामपमृज्यते
2.e: Of twice-born men the taint of seed and womb is removed by the ‘Libations in connection with Pregnancy’ and by ‘Jātakarman’ (Rites attendant upon birth), ‘Chauḍa’ (Tonsure) and ‘Mauñjībandhana’ (Tying of the grass-girdle).

2.s: svādhyāyena vratairhomaistraividyenaijyayā sutaiḥ mahāyajñaiśca yajñaiśca brāhmīiyaṃ kriyate tanuḥ
2.d: स्वाध्यायेन व्रतैर्होमैस्त्रैविद्येनैज्यया सुतैः महायज्ञैश्च यज्ञैश्च ब्राह्मीइयं क्रियते तनुः
2.e: This body is made godly,—by a thorough study of the three Vedas, by Observances, by libations, by offerings, by children, by the Great Sacrifices and by the Sacrifices.

2.s: prālg nābhivardhanāt puṃso jātakarma vidhīyate mantravat prāśanaṃ cāsya hiraṇyamadhusarpiṣām
2.d: प्राल्ग् नाभिवर्धनात् पुंसो जातकर्म विधीयते मन्त्रवत् प्राशनं चास्य हिरण्यमधुसर्पिषाम्
2.e: For the male child, before the cutting of the umbilical cord the performance of the Jāta-karma (Birth-rite) has been ordained: (it consists of) the feeding of him with gold, honey and butter, to the accompaniment of Mantras.

2.s: nāmadheyaṃ daśamyāṃ tu dvādaśyāṃ vā 'sya kārayet puṇye tithau muhūrte vā nakṣatre vā guṇānvite
2.d: नामधेयं दशम्यां तु द्वादश्यां वा ऽस्य कारयेत् पुण्ये तिथौ मुहूर्ते वा नक्षत्रे वा गुणान्विते
2.e: One should have his ‘naming’ (Nāmadheya) done on the tenth or the twelfth (day), on an auspicious lunar date and at an auspicious moment. and under a propitious lunar asterism.

2.s: maṅgalyaṃ brāhmaṇasya syāt kṣatriyasya balānvitam vaiśyasya dhanasaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya tu jugupsitam
2.d: मङ्गल्यं ब्राह्मणस्य स्यात् क्षत्रियस्य बलान्वितम् वैश्यस्य धनसंयुक्तं शूद्रस्य तु जुगुप्सितम्
2.e: The name of the Brāhmaṇa should be auspicious, that of the Kṣatriya connected with power, that of the Vaiśya associated with wealth; while that of the Śūdra contemptible.

2.s: śarmavadbrāhmaṇasya syādrājño rakṣāsamanvitam rājñā ? vaiśyasya puṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya preṣyasaṃyutam
2.d: शर्मवद्ब्राह्मणस्य स्याद्राज्ञो रक्षासमन्वितम् राज्ञा ? वैश्यस्य पुष्टिसंयुक्तं शूद्रस्य प्रेष्यसंयुतम्
2.e: The name of the Brāhmaṇa should be expressive of ‘peace,’ that of the Kṣatriya, of ‘protection’; that ot the Vaiśya, of ‘prosperity,’ and that of the Śūdra, of ‘submissiveness.’

2.s: strīṇāṃ sukhaudyamakrūraṃ vispaṣṭārthaṃ manoharam maṅgalyaṃ dīrghavarṇāntamāśīrvādābhidhānavat
2.d: स्त्रीणां सुखौद्यमक्रूरं विस्पष्टार्थं मनोहरम् मङ्गल्यं दीर्घवर्णान्तमाशीर्वादाभिधानवत्
2.e: That of women should be easily pronouncible, not harsh, of plain meaning, heart-captivating and auspicious; it should end in a long vowel and contain a benedictory term.

2.s: caturthe māsi kartavyaṃ śiśorniṣkramaṇaṃ gṛhāt ṣaṣṭhe 'nnaprāśanaṃ māsi yadvaiṣṭaṃ maṅgalaṃ kule
2.d: चतुर्थे मासि कर्तव्यं शिशोर्निष्क्रमणं गृहात् षष्ठे ऽन्नप्राशनं मासि यद्वैष्टं मङ्गलं कुले
2.e: In the fourth month should be performed the ceremony of the child’s ‘Egress’ from the room; and in the sixth month the ceremony of ‘Feeding’; or, whatever might be regarded as auspicious in the family.

2.s: cūḍākarma dvijātīnāṃ sarveṣāmeva dharmataḥ prathame 'bde tṛtīye vā kartavyaṃ śruticodanāt śrutinodanāt
2.d: चूडाकर्म द्विजातीनां सर्वेषामेव धर्मतः प्रथमे ऽब्दे तृतीये वा कर्तव्यं श्रुतिचोदनात् श्रुतिनोदनात्
2.e: In view or the injunctions or the Veda, the Tonsure-ceremony of all twice-born children should be performed, according to law, in the first year or the third.

2.s: garbhāṣṭame 'bde kurvīta brāhmaṇasyaupanāyanam garbhādekādaśe rājño garbhāt tu dvādaśe viśaḥ
2.d: गर्भाष्टमे ऽब्दे कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणस्यौपनायनम् गर्भादेकादशे राज्ञो गर्भात् तु द्वादशे विशः
2.e: In the eighth year from conception one should perform the initiation of the Brāhmaṇa; of the king in the eleventh year from conception; and of the Vaiśya in the twelfth.

2.s: brahmavarcasakāmasya kāryo viprasya pañcame rājño balārthinaḥ ṣaṣṭhe vaiśyasyaihārthino 'ṣṭame
2.d: ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य कार्यो विप्रस्य पञ्चमे राज्ञो बलार्थिनः षष्ठे वैश्यस्यैहार्थिनो ऽष्टमे
2.e: For the Brāhmaṇa desirous of Brahmic glory, it should be done in the fifth year; for the ‘King’ desirous of power, in the sixth; and for the Vaiśya desirous of business, in the eighth.

2.s: ā ṣodaśādbrāhmaṇasya sāvitrī nātivartate ā dvāviṃśāt kṣatrabandhorā caturviṃśaterviśaḥ
2.d: आ षोदशाद्ब्राह्मणस्य सावित्री नातिवर्तते आ द्वाविंशात् क्षत्रबन्धोरा चतुर्विंशतेर्विशः
2.e: For the Brāhmaṇa the Sāvitrī does not lapse till the sixteenth year; for the Kṣatriya till the twenty-second year; and for the Vaiśya till the twenty-fourth year.

2.s: ata ūrdhvaṃ trayo 'pyete yathākālamasaṃskṛtāḥ sāvitrīpatitā vrātyā bhavantyāryavigarhitāḥ
2.d: अत ऊर्ध्वं त्रयो ऽप्येते यथाकालमसंस्कृताः सावित्रीपतिता व्रात्या भवन्त्यार्यविगर्हिताः
2.e: Beyond this, all these three, not having received the sacrament at the proper time, become excluded from Sāvitrī (initiation), and thereby come to be known as ‘Vrātyas’ (apostates), despised by all good men.

2.s: naitairapūtairvidhivadāpadyapi hi karhi cit brāhmān yaunāṃśca saṃbandhānnācaredbrāhmaṇaḥ saha brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
2.d: नैतैरपूतैर्विधिवदापद्यपि हि कर्हि चित् ब्राह्मान् यौनांश्च संबन्धान्नाचरेद्ब्राह्मणः सह ब्राह्मणैः सह
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa should not in ant case, even in times of distress, establish spiritual or uterine relationship with these persons, until they have been duly purified.

2.s: kārṣṇarauravabāstāni carmāṇi brahmacāriṇaḥ vasīrannānupūrvyeṇa śāṇakṣaumāvikāni ca
2.d: कार्ष्णरौरवबास्तानि चर्माणि ब्रह्मचारिणः वसीरन्नानुपूर्व्येण शाणक्षौमाविकानि च
2.e: Brahmacāris should wear the skin of the black (deer), of the Ruru deer and of the goat respectively; and also the cloth of hemp, flax and wool.’

2.s: mauñjī trivṛt samā ślakṣṇā kāryā viprasya mekhalā kṣatriyasya tu maurvī jyā vaiśyasya śaṇatāntavī
2.d: मौञ्जी त्रिवृत् समा श्लक्ष्णा कार्या विप्रस्य मेखला क्षत्रियस्य तु मौर्वी ज्या वैश्यस्य शणतान्तवी
2.e: For, the Brāhmaṇa the girdle should be threefold, of even thickness, soft and smooth, made of muñja grass; for the Kṣatriya it should be the bow-string made of murvā grass; and for the Vaiśya the cord made of hempen fibres.”

2.s: muñjālābhe tu kartavyāḥ kuśāśmantakabalvajaiḥ trivṛtā granthinaikena tribhiḥ pañcabhireva vā
2.d: मुञ्जालाभे तु कर्तव्याः कुशाश्मन्तकबल्वजैः त्रिवृता ग्रन्थिनैकेन त्रिभिः पञ्चभिरेव वा
2.e: In the event of Muñja (and thb rest) being not available, they should be made of Kuśa, Ashmantaka and Balvaja,—triplicated with one, three or four knots.

2.s: kārpāsamupavītaṃ syādviprasyaurdhvavṛtaṃ trivṛt śaṇasūtramayaṃ rājño vaiśyasyāvikasautrikam
2.d: कार्पासमुपवीतं स्याद्विप्रस्यौर्ध्ववृतं त्रिवृत् शणसूत्रमयं राज्ञो वैश्यस्याविकसौत्रिकम्
2.e: The Sacrificial Thread worn over the shoulder,—which is triple and twisted upwards,—should be hade op cotton for the Brāhmaṇa, of hempen fibres for the Kṣatriya, and op woolen fibres for the Vaiśya.

2.s: brāhmaṇo bailvapālāśau kṣatriyo vāṭakhādirau pailavaudumbarau vaiśyo daṇḍānarhanti dharmataḥ
2.d: ब्राह्मणो बैल्वपालाशौ क्षत्रियो वाटखादिरौ पैलवौदुम्बरौ वैश्यो दण्डानर्हन्ति धर्मतः
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa should, by law, have staves of Bilva and Palāśa wood; the Kṣatriya those of Vaṭa and Khadira; and the Vaiśya those of Pīlu and Udumbara.

2.s: keśāntiko brāhmaṇasya daṇḍaḥ kāryaḥ pramāṇataḥ lalāṭasammito rājñaḥ syāt tu nāsāntiko viśaḥ
2.d: केशान्तिको ब्राह्मणस्य दण्डः कार्यः प्रमाणतः ललाटसम्मितो राज्ञः स्यात् तु नासान्तिको विशः
2.e: For the Brāhmaṇa the staff should be made in size reaching up to the end of his hair, for the Kṣatriya it should reach up to the forehead, and for the Vaiśya to the nose;

2.s: ṛjavaste tu sarve syuravraṇāḥ saumyadarśanāḥ anudvegakarā nr̥̄ṇāṃ satvaco 'nagnidūṣitāḥ
2.d: ऋजवस्ते तु सर्वे स्युरव्रणाः सौम्यदर्शनाः अनुद्वेगकरा न्र्̥̄णां सत्वचो ऽनग्निदूषिताः
2.e: All these should be straight, unimpaired, handsome-looking, not frightening to men, with dark and unspoilt by fire

2.s: pratigṛhyaipsitaṃ daṇḍamupasthāya ca bhāskaram pradakṣiṇaṃ parītyāgniṃ caredbhaikṣaṃ yathāvidhi
2.d: प्रतिगृह्यैप्सितं दण्डमुपस्थाय च भास्करम् प्रदक्षिणं परीत्याग्निं चरेद्भैक्षं यथाविधि
2.e: Taking up the staff of his liking, having worshipped the sun and walked round the fire to his right, he should beg for alms according to the prescribed rule.

2.s: bhavatpūrvaṃ caredbhaikṣamupanīto dvijottamaḥ bhavanmadhyaṃ tu rājanyo vaiśyastu bhavaduttaram
2.d: भवत्पूर्वं चरेद्भैक्षमुपनीतो द्विजोत्तमः भवन्मध्यं तु राजन्यो वैश्यस्तु भवदुत्तरम्
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa, having undergone Initiation, should beg for food with words of which ‘bhavat’ (‘Lady’) forms the beginning; the Kṣatriya with words of which ‘bhavat’ forms the middle; and the Vaiśya with words of which ‘bhavat’ forms the end.

2.s: mātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vā māturvā bhaginīṃ nijām bhikṣeta bhikṣāṃ prathamaṃ yā cainaṃ nāvamānayet
2.d: मातरं वा स्वसारं वा मातुर्वा भगिनीं निजाम् भिक्षेत भिक्षां प्रथमं या चैनं नावमानयेत्
2.e: First of all he should beg food of his mother, or of his sister, or of his mother’s own sister, or of such another lady as may not insult him.

2.s: samāhṛtya tu tadbhaikṣaṃ yāvadannamamāyayā yāvadarthaṃ nivedya gurave 'śnīyādācamya prālgmukhaḥ śuciḥ
2.d: समाहृत्य तु तद्भैक्षं यावदन्नममायया यावदर्थं निवेद्य गुरवे ऽश्नीयादाचम्य प्राल्ग्मुखः शुचिः
2.e: Having collected as much food as may be needed, and having offered it, without guile, to his Teacher, he should eat it, with his face to the east, after having sipped water and become pure.

2.s: āyuṣyaṃ prālgmukho bhuṅkte yaśasyaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ śriyaṃ pratyalgmukho bhuṅkte ṛtaṃ bhuṅkte hyudalgmukhaḥ
2.d: आयुष्यं प्राल्ग्मुखो भुङ्क्ते यशस्यं दक्षिणामुखः श्रियं प्रत्यल्ग्मुखो भुङ्क्ते ऋतं भुङ्क्ते ह्युदल्ग्मुखः
2.e: Eating with face to the East, he does what is conducive to longevity; eating with face to the South, he does what brings fame; eating with face to the West, he does what brings prosperity; and eating with face to the North, he does what leads to the true.

2.s: upaspṛśya dvijo nityamannamadyāt samāhitaḥ bhuktvā caupaspṛśet samyagadbhiḥ khāni ca saṃspṛśet
2.d: उपस्पृश्य द्विजो नित्यमन्नमद्यात् समाहितः भुक्त्वा चौपस्पृशेत् सम्यगद्भिः खानि च संस्पृशेत्
2.e: The twice-b orn person should always take his food after having sipped water and with due care; and after having eaten, he should rinse his mouth in the proper manner and touch the cavities with water.

2.s: pūjayedaśanaṃ nityamadyāccaitadakutsayan dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyet prasīdecca pratinandecca sarvaśaḥ
2.d: पूजयेदशनं नित्यमद्याच्चैतदकुत्सयन् दृष्ट्वा हृष्येत् प्रसीदेच्च प्रतिनन्देच्च सर्वशः
2.e: He should always worship the food and eat it without disparaging it. When he sees it, he should rejoice and peel gratified, and he should always welcome it.

2.s: pūjitaṃ hyaśanaṃ nityaṃ balamūrjaṃ ca yacchati apūjitaṃ tu tadbhuktamubhayaṃ nāśayedidam
2.d: पूजितं ह्यशनं नित्यं बलमूर्जं च यच्छति अपूजितं तु तद्भुक्तमुभयं नाशयेदिदम्
2.e: The food, thus worshipped always, imparts strength and vigour. If eaten irreverently, it destroys them both.

2.s: naucchiṣṭaṃ kasya ciddadyānnādyādetat tathā 'ntarā na caivātyaśanaṃ kuryānna caucchiṣṭaḥ kva cidvrajet
2.d: नौच्छिष्टं कस्य चिद्दद्यान्नाद्यादेतत् तथा ऽन्तरा न चैवात्यशनं कुर्यान्न चौच्छिष्टः क्व चिद्व्रजेत्
2.e: He should not give the leavings to anyone; he should not eat in between; he should not do over-rating; and he should not go any-where with particles of food still on him.

2.s: anārogyamanāyuṣyamasvargyaṃ cātibhojanam apuṇyaṃ lokavidviṣṭaṃ tasmāt tat parivarjayet
2.d: अनारोग्यमनायुष्यमस्वर्ग्यं चातिभोजनम् अपुण्यं लोकविद्विष्टं तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत्
2.e: Over-eating destroys health, cuts off life and bars heaven; it is unrighteous and detested by people; for these reasons one should avoid it.

2.s: brāhmeṇa viprastīrthena nityakālamupaspṛśet kāyatraidaśikābhyāṃ vā na pitryeṇa kadā cana
2.d: ब्राह्मेण विप्रस्तीर्थेन नित्यकालमुपस्पृशेत् कायत्रैदशिकाभ्यां वा न पित्र्येण कदा चन
2.e: Every time, the Brāhmana should sip water, either though the receptacle dedicated to Brahmā, or through that dedicated to Prajāpati, or through that dedicated to the ‘Thrice-ten’ (Gods); but never through that dedicated to the Pitṛs.

2.s: aṅguṣṭhamūlasya tale brāhmaṃ tīrthaṃ pracakṣate kāyamaṅgulimūle 'gre devaṃ pitryaṃ tayoradhaḥ
2.d: अङ्गुष्ठमूलस्य तले ब्राह्मं तीर्थं प्रचक्षते कायमङ्गुलिमूले ऽग्रे देवं पित्र्यं तयोरधः
2.e: The part of the palm at the root of the thumb they call ‘the receptacle dedicated to Brahmā’; that which is at the root of the finger ‘Sacred to Prajāpati’; that on the finger-tops ‘dedicated to the Gods’; and that which is below these two ‘dedicated to the Pitṛs.’

2.s: trirācāmedapaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāt tato mukham khāni caiva spṛśedadbhirātmānaṃ śira eva ca
2.d: त्रिराचामेदपः पूर्वं द्विः प्रमृज्यात् ततो मुखम् खानि चैव स्पृशेदद्भिरात्मानं शिर एव च
2.e: First of all he should sip water thrice; then he should wipe his mouth twice, and touch with water the cavities, the soul and also the head.

2.s: anuṣṇābhiraphenābhiradbhistīrthena dharmavit śaucaipsuḥ sarvadā 'cāmedekānte prāgudalgmukhaḥ
2.d: अनुष्णाभिरफेनाभिरद्भिस्तीर्थेन धर्मवित् शौचैप्सुः सर्वदा ऽचामेदेकान्ते प्रागुदल्ग्मुखः
2.e: One who knows his duties, when desiring cleanliness, should always sip, through the proper receptacle, water which is neither hot nor frothy,—in solitude, with his face towards the North or the East.

2.s: hṛdgābhiḥ pūyate vipraḥ kaṇṭhagābhistu bhūmipaḥ vaiśyo 'dbhiḥ prāśitābhistu śūdraḥ spṛṣṭābhirantataḥ
2.d: हृद्गाभिः पूयते विप्रः कण्ठगाभिस्तु भूमिपः वैश्यो ऽद्भिः प्राशिताभिस्तु शूद्रः स्पृष्टाभिरन्ततः
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa is purified by the water reaching the heart; the Kṣatriya by that reaching the throat; the Vaiśya by water that is just sipped, and the Śūdra by what is touched with the end.

2.s: uddhṛte dakṣine pāṇāvupavītyaucyate dvijaḥ savye prācīnāvītī nivītī kaṇṭhasajjane
2.d: उद्धृते दक्षिने पाणावुपवीत्यौच्यते द्विजः सव्ये प्राचीनावीती निवीती कण्ठसज्जने
2.e: When the right hand is held above (the sacred thread etc.), the twice-born person is described as ‘Upavītin’; when the left hand is held above, ‘Prācīnāvītin [Prachinaviti]’, and on its hanging by the neck, ‘Nivītin.’

2.s: mekhalāmajinaṃ daṇḍamupavītaṃ kamaṇḍalum apsu prāsya vinaṣṭāni gṛhṇītānyāni mantravat
2.d: मेखलामजिनं दण्डमुपवीतं कमण्डलुम् अप्सु प्रास्य विनष्टानि गृह्णीतान्यानि मन्त्रवत्
2.e: When the girdle, the skin, the staff, the sacred thread or the water-pot becomes damaged, he should throw it into the water and take up another with the proper formulas.

2.s: keśāntaḥ ṣoḍaśe varṣe brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate rājanyabandhordvāviṃśe vaiśyasya dvyadhike mataḥ
2.d: केशान्तः षोडशे वर्षे ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते राजन्यबन्धोर्द्वाविंशे वैश्यस्य द्व्यधिके मतः
2.e: The sacrament of Keśānta is ordained for the Brāhmaṇa in his sixteenth year; for the Kṣatriya in his twenty-second year, and for the Vaiśya two years later.

2.s: amantrikā tu kāryaiyaṃ strīṇāmāvṛdaśeṣataḥ saṃskārārthaṃ śarīrasya yathākālaṃ yathākramam
2.d: अमन्त्रिका तु कार्यैयं स्त्रीणामावृदशेषतः संस्कारार्थं शरीरस्य यथाकालं यथाक्रमम्
2.e: For females, this whole series should be performed at the right time and in the proper order, for the purpose of sanctifying the body; but without the Vedic formulas

2.s: vaivāhiko vidhiḥ strīṇāṃ saṃskāro vaidikaḥ smṛtaḥ patisevā gurau vāso gṛhārtho 'gniparikriyā
2.d: वैवाहिको विधिः स्त्रीणां संस्कारो वैदिकः स्मृतः पतिसेवा गुरौ वासो गृहार्थो ऽग्निपरिक्रिया
2.e: For females the Rites of marriage have been ordained to be their ‘Vedic Sacrament,’ the serving of the husbands their ‘residence with the Teacher,’ and the household-duties their ‘tending of fire.’

2.s: eṣa prokto dvijātīnāmaupanāyaniko vidhiḥ utpattivyañjakaḥ puṇyaḥ karmayogaṃ nibodhata
2.d: एष प्रोक्तो द्विजातीनामौपनायनिको विधिः उत्पत्तिव्यञ्जकः पुण्यः कर्मयोगं निबोधत
2.e: Thus has been described the Initiatory Ceremony of twice-born men,—that which sanctifies them and marks their (real) birth. Learn now the duties to which they should apply themselves.

2.s: upanīya guruḥ śiṣyaṃ śikṣayetśaucamāditaḥ ācāramagnikāryaṃ ca saṃdhyaupāsanameva ca
2.d: उपनीय गुरुः शिष्यं शिक्षयेत्शौचमादितः आचारमग्निकार्यं च संध्यौपासनमेव च
2.e: Having initiated the pupil, the Teacher should, first of all, teach him cleanliness, right behaviour, firetending and also the twilight-devotions.

2.s: adhyeṣyamāṇastvācānto yathāśāstramudalgmukhaḥ brahmāñjalikṛto 'dhyāpyo laghuvāsā jitaindriyaḥ
2.d: अध्येष्यमाणस्त्वाचान्तो यथाशास्त्रमुदल्ग्मुखः ब्रह्माञ्जलिकृतो ऽध्याप्यो लघुवासा जितैन्द्रियः
2.e: When about to study, he shall be taught with his face to the north, when he has sipped water according to law, has formed the Brahmāñjali (with his hands), wears light clothing and has the organs under full control.

2.s: brahmārambhe 'vasāne ca pādau grāhyau guroḥ sadā saṃhatya hastāvadhyeyaṃ sa hi brahmāñjaliḥ smṛtaḥ
2.d: ब्रह्मारम्भे ऽवसाने च पादौ ग्राह्यौ गुरोः सदा संहत्य हस्तावध्येयं स हि ब्रह्माञ्जलिः स्मृतः
2.e: At the beginning and at the end op the (study of) the Veda, the feet of the Teacher should always be clasped; and the veda should me studied with joined palms; this is what has been called the ‘Brahmāñjali.’

2.s: vyatyastapāṇinā kāryamupasaṅgrahaṇaṃ guroḥ savyena savyaḥ spraṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena ca dakṣiṇaḥ
2.d: व्यत्यस्तपाणिना कार्यमुपसङ्ग्रहणं गुरोः सव्येन सव्यः स्प्रष्टव्यो दक्षिणेन च दक्षिणः
2.e: The clasping op the teacher’s feet should be done with crossed hands: the left should be touched with the left and the right with the right.

2.s: adhyeṣyamāṇaṃ tu gururnityakālamatandritaḥ adhīṣva bho iti brūyādvirāmo 'stviti cāramet
2.d: अध्येष्यमाणं तु गुरुर्नित्यकालमतन्द्रितः अधीष्व भो इति ब्रूयाद्विरामो ऽस्त्विति चारमेत्
2.e: When the pupil is going to study, the Teacher, ever free from indolence, should say—‘ho, read!’ and he should cease when he says ‘let there be a stop!’

2.s: brahmanaḥ praṇavaṃ kuryādādāvante ca sarvadā sravatyanoṅkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ parastācca viśīryati
2.d: ब्रह्मनः प्रणवं कुर्यादादावन्ते च सर्वदा स्रवत्यनोङ्कृतं पूर्वं परस्ताच्च विशीर्यति
2.e: One should always pronounce the Praṇava in the beginning and at the end of the Veda. if it is not accompanied by the syllable ‘oṃ’ in the beginning, it trickles away; and (if it is not accompanied by it) at the end, it becomes shattered.

2.s: prākkūlān paryupāsīnaḥ pavitraiścaiva pāvitaḥ prāṇāyāmaistribhiḥ pūtastata oṃkāramarhati
2.d: प्राक्कूलान् पर्युपासीनः पवित्रैश्चैव पावितः प्राणायामैस्त्रिभिः पूतस्तत ओंकारमर्हति
2.e: Seated upon Kuśa-blades pointing eastwards and sanctified by Kuśa-blades, when one has purified himself by means of three ‘breath-suspensions,’—then alone he becomes entitled to the syllable ‘oṃ.’

2.s: akāraṃ cāpyukāraṃ ca makāraṃ ca prajāpatiḥ vedatrayātniraduhadbhūrbhuvaḥ svaritīti ca
2.d: अकारं चाप्युकारं च मकारं च प्रजापतिः वेदत्रयात्निरदुहद्भूर्भुवः स्वरितीति च
2.e: Out of the three Vedas, Prajāpati milked the letter ‘a,’ the letter ‘u’ and the letter ‘m’; as also the syllables ‘bhūḥ-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ.’

2.s: tribhya eva tu vedebhyaḥ pādaṃ pādamadūduhat tadity ṛco 'syāḥ sāvitryāḥ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ
2.d: त्रिभ्य एव तु वेदेभ्यः पादं पादमदूदुहत् तदित्य् ऋचो ऽस्याः सावित्र्याः परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः
2.e: Out of the three Vedas again, the Supreme Prajāpati milked each foot of the Sāvitrī verse beginning with ‘tat.’

2.s: etadakṣarametāṃ ca japan vyāhṛtipūrvikām saṃdhyayorvedavidvipro vedapuṇyena yujyate
2.d: एतदक्षरमेतां च जपन् व्याहृतिपूर्विकाम् संध्ययोर्वेदविद्विप्रो वेदपुण्येन युज्यते
2.e: Reciting, at the two twilights, this syllable and this verse, preceded by the Vyāhṛtis, the Brāhmaṇa, learned in the Veda, becomes endowed with Vedic merit.

2.s: sahasrakṛtvastvabhyasya bahiretat trikaṃ dvijaḥ mahato 'pyenaso māsāt tvacaivāhirvimucyate
2.d: सहस्रकृत्वस्त्वभ्यस्य बहिरेतत् त्रिकं द्विजः महतो ऽप्येनसो मासात् त्वचैवाहिर्विमुच्यते
2.e: Repeating this Triad a thousand times in open air, the twice-born person becomes freed, in a month, from even great sin, as the snake from its slough.

2.s: etayāṛcā visaṃyuktaḥ kāle ca kriyayā svayā brahmakṣatriyaviśyonirgarhaṇāṃ yāti sādhuṣu
2.d: एतयाऋचा विसंयुक्तः काले च क्रियया स्वया ब्रह्मक्षत्रियविश्योनिर्गर्हणां याति साधुषु
2.e: Bereft of this verse, and of the timely performance of his own duty, a person of Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya or Vaiśya birth incurs the odium of good men.

2.s: oṃkārapūrvikāstisro mahāvyāhṛtayo 'vyayāḥ oṅkāra tripadā caiva sāvitrī vijñeyaṃ brahmaṇo mukham
2.d: ओंकारपूर्विकास्तिस्रो महाव्याहृतयो ऽव्ययाः ओङ्कार त्रिपदा चैव सावित्री विज्ञेयं ब्रह्मणो मुखम्
2.e: The three imperishable Mahāvyāhṛtis preceded by the syllable ‘oṃ,’ and the three-footed Sāvitrī,—these should be regarded as the ‘Mouth of Brahman.’

2.s: yo 'dhīte 'hanyahanyetāṃ trīṇi varṣāṇyatandritaḥ sa brahma paramabhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān
2.d: यो ऽधीते ऽहन्यहन्येतां त्रीणि वर्षाण्यतन्द्रितः स ब्रह्म परमभ्येति वायुभूतः खमूर्तिमान्
2.e: He who, untired, recites this, day after day, for three years, turns into air, and becoming transfigured into Ākāśa, reaches the supreme brahman.

2.s: ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaḥ paraṃ tapaḥ sāvitryāstu paraṃ nāsti maunāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate
2.d: एकाक्षरं परं ब्रह्म प्राणायामः परं तपः सावित्र्यास्तु परं नास्ति मौनात् सत्यं विशिष्यते
2.e: The mono-syllable is the highest Brahman; Breath-suspensions are the highest austerity; nothing is higher than the Sāvitrī verse; truth is better than Silence.

2.s: kṣaranti sarvā vaidikyo juhotiyajatikriyāḥ akṣaraṃ duṣkaraṃ jñeyaṃ brahma caiva prajāpatiḥ akṣaraṃ tvakṣaraṃ jñeyaṃ
2.d: क्षरन्ति सर्वा वैदिक्यो जुहोतियजतिक्रियाः अक्षरं दुष्करं ज्ञेयं ब्रह्म चैव प्रजापतिः अक्षरं त्वक्षरं ज्ञेयं
2.e: All vedic acts of oblation and sacrifice pass away; while this syllable (om) is to be regarded as imperishable; and it is Brahman, and also Prajāpati

2.s: vidhiyajñāj japayajño viśiṣṭo daśabhirguṇaiḥ upāṃśuḥ syātśataguṇaḥ sāhasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ
2.d: विधियज्ञाज् जपयज्ञो विशिष्टो दशभिर्गुणैः उपांशुः स्यात्शतगुणः साहस्रो मानसः स्मृतः
2.e: The offering that consists in the repeating of mantras excels the enjoined (ritualistic) offering ten times; the inaudible (repeating) excels this latter a hundred times; and the Mental (repeating) excels it a thousandfold.

2.s: ye pākayajñāḥ catvāro vidhiyajñasamanvitāḥ sarve te japayajñasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm
2.d: ये पाकयज्ञाः चत्वारो विधियज्ञसमन्विताः सर्वे ते जपयज्ञस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्
2.e: The four cooked offerings, along with the enjoined sacrifices,—all these are not worth the sixteenth part of the offering that consists in the repeating of mantras.

2.s: japyenaiva tu saṃsidhyedbrāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ kuryādanyanna vā kuryān maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate
2.d: जप्येनैव तु संसिध्येद्ब्राह्मणो नात्र संशयः कुर्यादन्यन्न वा कुर्यान् मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते
2.e: It is by means of repeating mantras that the Brāhmaṇa succeeds;—there is no doubt in this. he may, or may not, do anything else, one comes to be called a Brāhmaṇa if he is of a friendly disposition.

2.s: indriyāṇāṃ vicaratāṃ viṣayeṣvapahāriṣu saṃyame yatnamātiṣṭhedvidvān yantaiva vājinām
2.d: इन्द्रियाणां विचरतां विषयेष्वपहारिषु संयमे यत्नमातिष्ठेद्विद्वान् यन्तैव वाजिनाम्
2.e: The wise man should put forth an effort to restrain his organs roaming among alluring objects; just as the driver restrains the horses.

2.s: ekādaśaindriyāṇyāhuryāni pūrve manīṣiṇaḥ tāni samyak pravakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ
2.d: एकादशैन्द्रियाण्याहुर्यानि पूर्वे मनीषिणः तानि सम्यक् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः
2.e: Those eleven organs which the ancient sages have named I shall now fully describe in due order.

2.s: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā caiva pañcamī pāyūpasthaṃ hastapādaṃ vāk caiva daśamī smṛtā
2.d: श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुषी जिह्वा नासिका चैव पञ्चमी पायूपस्थं हस्तपादं वाक् चैव दशमी स्मृता
2.e: (They are) the Ear, the Skin, the Eyes, the Tongue and the Nose as the fifth; the Anus, the Generative Organ, the Hands and Feet, and Speech described as the tenth.

2.s: buddhīndriyāṇi pañcaiṣāṃ śrotrādīnyanupūrvaśaḥ karmaindriyāṇi pañcaiṣāṃ pāyuādīni pracakṣate
2.d: बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि पञ्चैषां श्रोत्रादीन्यनुपूर्वशः कर्मैन्द्रियाणि पञ्चैषां पायुआदीनि प्रचक्षते
2.e: Of these the five beginning with the Ear in due order they call “Organs of Sensation’; and five of these, beginning with the Anus, “Organs of Action.”

2.s: ekādaśaṃ mano jñeyaṃ svaguṇenaubhayātmakam yasmin jite jitāvetau bhavataḥ pañcakau gaṇau
2.d: एकादशं मनो ज्ञेयं स्वगुणेनौभयात्मकम् यस्मिन् जिते जितावेतौ भवतः पञ्चकौ गणौ
2.e: The Mind is to be regarded as the eleventh, which, by its own quality, is of two-fold nature; and on this being subdued, both the aforesaid five-mentioned groups become subdued.

2.s: indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena doṣaṃ ṛcchatyasaṃśayam saṃniyamya tu tānyeva tataḥ siddhiṃ nigacchati
2.d: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन दोषं ऋच्छत्यसंशयम् संनियम्य तु तान्येव ततः सिद्धिं निगच्छति
2.e: By attachment to the organs one incurs evil, without doubt; while by subjugating those same he attains success.

2.s: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmaiva bhūya evābhivardhate
2.d: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मैव भूय एवाभिवर्धते
2.e: Never is desire appeased by the enjoyment of desires; it only waxes stronger, like fire by clarified butter.

2.s: yaścaitān prāpnuyāt sarvān yaścaitān kevalāṃstyajet prāpaṇāt sarvakāmānāṃ parityāgo viśiṣyate
2.d: यश्चैतान् प्राप्नुयात् सर्वान् यश्चैतान् केवलांस्त्यजेत् प्रापणात् सर्वकामानां परित्यागो विशिष्यते
2.e: As between one who would attain all these, and another who would renounce them all, the renunciation of desires surf asses the attainment of

2.s: na tathaitāni śakyante saṃniyantumasevayā viṣayeṣu prajuṣṭāni yathā jñānena nityaśaḥ
2.d: न तथैतानि शक्यन्ते संनियन्तुमसेवया विषयेषु प्रजुष्टानि यथा ज्ञानेन नित्यशः
2.e: These (organs), being contaminated with objects, are not capable of being subjugated by mere abstinence, as they are by ever present knowledge.

2.s: vedāstyāgaśca yajñāśca niyamāśca tapāṃsi ca na vipraduṣṭabhāvasya siddhiṃ gacchati karhi cit
2.d: वेदास्त्यागश्च यज्ञाश्च नियमाश्च तपांसि च न विप्रदुष्टभावस्य सिद्धिं गच्छति कर्हि चित्
2.e: The Vedas, Renunciation, Sacrifices, Restraints and Austerities never attain fulfilment for one whose disposition is vitiated.

2.s: śrutvā spṛṣṭvā ca dṛṣṭvā ca bhuktvā ghrātvā ca yo naraḥ na hṛṣyati glāyati vā sa vijñeyo jitaindriyaḥ
2.d: श्रुत्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च दृष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा घ्रात्वा च यो नरः न हृष्यति ग्लायति वा स विज्ञेयो जितैन्द्रियः
2.e: That man is to be known as having subjugated his sense-organs, who, on having heard, or touched, or seen, or tasted, or smelt, anything, neither rejoices nor grieves.

2.s: indriyāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ yadyekaṃ kṣaratīndriyam tenāsya kṣarati prajñā dṛteḥ pādādivaudakam
2.d: इन्द्रियाणां तु सर्वेषां यद्येकं क्षरतीन्द्रियम् तेनास्य क्षरति प्रज्ञा दृतेः पादादिवौदकम्
2.e: From among all the organs, if one happens to ooze out, then thereby his wisdom oozes out, just like water from one part of the leathern bag.

2.s: vaśe kṛtvaindriyagrāmaṃ saṃyamya ca manastathā sarvān saṃsādhayedarthānakṣiṇvan yogatastanum
2.d: वशे कृत्वैन्द्रियग्रामं संयम्य च मनस्तथा सर्वान् संसाधयेदर्थानक्षिण्वन् योगतस्तनुम्
2.e: Having brought the host of organs under control, and having also subdued the mind, one should accomplish all his purposes, taking care not to injure his body.

2.s: pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japāṃstiṣṭhet sāvitrīmā 'rkadarśanāt paścimāṃ tu samāsīnaḥ samyag ṛkṣavibhāvanāt paścimāṃ tu sadāsīta
2.d: पूर्वां संध्यां जपांस्तिष्ठेत् सावित्रीमा ऽर्कदर्शनात् पश्चिमां तु समासीनः सम्यग् ऋक्षविभावनात् पश्चिमां तु सदासीत
2.e: Everyday during the earlier twilight one should stand repeating the Sāvitrī, till the sun becomes distinctly visible; and during the later twilight he should sit till the stars ark clearly seen.

2.s: pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhannaiśameno vyapohati paścimāṃ tu samāsīno malaṃ hanti divākṛtam
2.d: पूर्वां संध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठन्नैशमेनो व्यपोहति पश्चिमां तु समासीनो मलं हन्ति दिवाकृतम्
2.e: One who, during the morning-twilight, repeats (the Sāvitrī) standing, removes the sin of the (preceding) night; while he who, during the evening-Twilight, repeats it seated, destroys the sin committed during the day.

2.s: na tiṣṭhati tu yaḥ pūrvāṃ naupāste yaśca paścimām sa śūdravadbahiṣkāryaḥ sarvasmāddvijakarmaṇaḥ
2.d: न तिष्ठति तु यः पूर्वां नौपास्ते यश्च पश्चिमाम् स शूद्रवद्बहिष्कार्यः सर्वस्माद्द्विजकर्मणः
2.e: But he who does not stand during the morning-twilight, and who does not sit through the evening-twilight, should be excluded, like the Sśūdra, from all that is due to twice-born persons.

2.s: apāṃ samīpe niyato naityakaṃ vidhimāsthitaḥ sāvitrīmapyadhīyīta gatvā 'raṇyaṃ samāhitaḥ
