2.d: अपां समीपे नियतो नैत्यकं विधिमास्थितः सावित्रीमप्यधीयीत गत्वा ऽरण्यं समाहितः
2.e: Convinced of the necessary character of the injunction, and retiring to the forest on a spot near water, one may even recite the Sāvitrī only, with a clean body and a collected mind.

2.s: vedaupakaraṇe caiva svādhyāye caiva naityake nānurodho 'styanadhyāye homamantreṣu caiva hi
2.d: वेदौपकरणे चैव स्वाध्याये चैव नैत्यके नानुरोधो ऽस्त्यनध्याये होममन्त्रेषु चैव हि
2.e: There is no regard for (observance of) days forbidden for study in connection with the appurtenances to the Veda, and with the mantras recited during oblations.

2.s: naityake nāstyanadhyāyo brahmasattraṃ hi tat smṛtam brahmāhutihutaṃ puṇyamanadhyāyavaṣaṭkṛtam
2.d: नैत्यके नास्त्यनध्यायो ब्रह्मसत्त्रं हि तत् स्मृतम् ब्रह्माहुतिहुतं पुण्यमनध्यायवषट्कृतम्
2.e: There is no “day forbidden for study” in regard to the daily recitation; since this has been called “Brahmasatra”; it is meritorious, being offered with the offering of study, and being maintained by the syllable “vaṣaṭ” in the shape of the recitation made on forbidden days.

2.s: yaḥ svādhyāyamadhīte 'bdaṃ vidhinā niyataḥ śuciḥ tasya nityaṃ kṣaratyeṣa payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ madhu
2.d: यः स्वाध्यायमधीते ऽब्दं विधिना नियतः शुचिः तस्य नित्यं क्षरत्येष पयो दधि घृतं मधु
2.e: He who, clean and self-controlled, recites the Veda, in due form, for one year,—for him this constantly fours out milk, curd, clarified butter and honey.

2.s: agnīndhanaṃ bhaikṣacaryāmadhaḥśayyāṃ gurorhitam ā samāvartanāt kuryāt kṛtaupanayano dvijaḥ
2.d: अग्नीन्धनं भैक्षचर्यामधःशय्यां गुरोर्हितम् आ समावर्तनात् कुर्यात् कृतौपनयनो द्विजः
2.e: The twice-born person, whose Initiation has been performed, should continue to do, till the final Bath of “Return” (Samāvartana), tub kindling of fire, the begging of food, the sleeping on the ground and the acting for the teacher’s well- being.

2.s: ācāryaputraḥ śuśrūṣurjñānado dhārmikaḥ śuciḥ āptaḥ śakto 'rthadaḥ sādhuḥ svo 'dhyāpyā daśa dharmataḥ
2.d: आचार्यपुत्रः शुश्रूषुर्ज्ञानदो धार्मिकः शुचिः आप्तः शक्तो ऽर्थदः साधुः स्वो ऽध्याप्या दश धर्मतः
2.e: The teacher’s son, one who is eager to do service, one who imparts knowledge, one who is righteous, one who is clean, a near relative, one who is competent, one who gives monet, one who is gentle, and one’s own (son)—these ten should be taught for the sake of merit.

2.s: nāpṛṣṭaḥ kasya cidbrūyānna cānyāyena pṛcchataḥ jānannapi hi medhāvī jaḍavalloka ācaret
2.d: नापृष्टः कस्य चिद्ब्रूयान्न चान्यायेन पृच्छतः जानन्नपि हि मेधावी जडवल्लोक आचरेत्
2.e: One should not instruct any one unless he is asked; nor any one who asks in an improper manner. even though knowing (the truth), the wise man should behave, among men, as if ignorant.

2.s: adharmeṇa ca yaḥ prāha yaścādharmeṇa pṛcchati tayoranyataraḥ praiti vidveṣaṃ vā 'dhigacchati
2.d: अधर्मेण च यः प्राह यश्चाधर्मेण पृच्छति तयोरन्यतरः प्रैति विद्वेषं वा ऽधिगच्छति
2.e: He who instructs in an unlawful manner, and he who asks in an unlawful manner,—of those two one or the other either dies (untimely), or incurs the ill-will (of the people).

2.s: dharmārthau yatra na syātāṃ śuśrūṣā vā 'pi tadvidhā tatra vidyā na vaptavyā śubhaṃ bījamivauṣare
2.d: धर्मार्थौ यत्र न स्यातां शुश्रूषा वा ऽपि तद्विधा तत्र विद्या न वप्तव्या शुभं बीजमिवौषरे
2.e: Where merit and wealth are not possible, nor is there an adequate desire to serve, there knowledge should not be imparted; just as healthy seed (is not sown) on barren land.

2.s: vidyayaiva samaṃ kāmaṃ martavyaṃ brahmavādinā āpadyapi hi ghorāyāṃ na tvenāmiriṇe vapet
2.d: विद्ययैव समं कामं मर्तव्यं ब्रह्मवादिना आपद्यपि हि घोरायां न त्वेनामिरिणे वपेत्
2.e: The expounder of the Veda may rather perish along with his knowledge; hut he should never sow it on barren soil, even in dike distress.

2.s: vidyā brāhmaṇametyāha śevadhiste 'smi rakṣa mām śevadhiṣ ṭe asūyakāya māṃ mādāstathā syāṃ vīryavattamā
2.d: विद्या ब्राह्मणमेत्याह शेवधिस्ते ऽस्मि रक्ष माम् शेवधिष् टे असूयकाय मां मादास्तथा स्यां वीर्यवत्तमा
2.e: Learning having approached the Brāhmaṇa said to him—“I am thy wealth, guard me; impart me not unto a scorner; thus may I become extremely powerful.”

2.s: yameva tu śuciṃ vidyānniyatabrahmacāriṇam vidyā niyataṃ brahmacāriṇam tasmai māṃ brūhi viprāya nidhipāyāpramādine
2.d: यमेव तु शुचिं विद्यान्नियतब्रह्मचारिणम् विद्या नियतं ब्रह्मचारिणम् तस्मै मां ब्रूहि विप्राय निधिपायाप्रमादिने
2.e: “Expound me unto the Brāhmaṇa who guards his treasures and is never careless,—and whom thou knowest to be pure, self-controlled and a duly qualified student.”

2.s: brahma yastvananujñātamadhīyānādavāpnuyāt sa brahmasteyasaṃyukto narakaṃ pratipadyate
2.d: ब्रह्म यस्त्वननुज्ञातमधीयानादवाप्नुयात् स ब्रह्मस्तेयसंयुक्तो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते
2.e: He, who may acquire Veda, without his permission, from one who is reciting it, becomes corrupted with the sin of stealing the Veda, and falls into hell.

2.s: laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vā 'pi tathā 'dhyātmikameva vā ādadīta yato jñānaṃ taṃ pūrvamabhivādayet
2.d: लौकिकं वैदिकं वा ऽपि तथा ऽध्यात्मिकमेव वा आददीत यतो ज्ञानं तं पूर्वमभिवादयेत्
2.e: One should first salute him from whom he receives knowledge, either temporal or scriptural or spiritual.

2.s: sāvitrīmātrasāro 'pi varaṃ vipraḥ suyantritaḥ nāyantritastrivedo 'pi sarvāśī sarvavikrayī
2.d: सावित्रीमात्रसारो ऽपि वरं विप्रः सुयन्त्रितः नायन्त्रितस्त्रिवेदो ऽपि सर्वाशी सर्वविक्रयी
2.e: Better the Brāhmaṇa knowing the Sāvitrī alone, if he is thoroughly self-controlled,—and not he who knows all the three Vedas, but is not self-controlled, and eats all things and sells all things.

2.s: śayyā ''sane 'dhyācarite śreyasā na samāviśet śayyā ''sanasthaścaivainaṃ pratyutthāyābhivādayet
2.d: शय्या 'ऽसने ऽध्याचरिते श्रेयसा न समाविशेत् शय्या 'ऽसनस्थश्चैवैनं प्रत्युत्थायाभिवादयेत्
2.e: One should not sit with a superior upon the couch or seat prepared for him. and if he himself should happen to be seated on a couch or skat, he should rise to meet (the superior) and salute him.

2.s: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hyutkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastān pratipadyate
2.d: ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्युत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान् प्रतिपद्यते
2.e: On the elder approaching, the vital breaths of the younger rush outward; and he recovers them by the acts of rising to meet and salute him.

2.s: abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhaupasevinaḥ catvāri tasya vardhante āyurdharmo yaśo balam catvāri saṃpravardhante
2.d: अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धौपसेविनः चत्वारि तस्य वर्धन्ते आयुर्धर्मो यशो बलम् चत्वारि संप्रवर्धन्ते
2.e: For one who is in the habit of saluting and constantly revering elders,—four things prosper:viz., longevity, merit, fame and strength.

2.s: abhivādāt paraṃ vipro jyāyāṃsamabhivādayan asau nāmāhamasmīti svaṃ nāma parikīrtayet
2.d: अभिवादात् परं विप्रो ज्यायांसमभिवादयन् असौ नामाहमस्मीति स्वं नाम परिकीर्तयेत्
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa, when greeting an elder, should, after the accosting, pronounce his name, (saying) “this here, I am named so and so,”

2.s: nāmadheyasya ye ke cidabhivādaṃ na jānate tān prājño 'hamiti brūyāt striyaḥ sarvāstathaiva ca
2.d: नामधेयस्य ये के चिदभिवादं न जानते तान् प्राज्ञो ऽहमिति ब्रूयात् स्त्रियः सर्वास्तथैव च
2.e: To those persons who do not comprehend the (significance of the) name (pronounced) in the words of greeting, the wise one should say ‘I’; similarly to all, women.

2.s: bhoḥśabdaṃ kīrtayedante svasya nāmno 'bhivādane nāmnāṃ svarūpabhāvo hi bhobhāva ṛṣibhiḥ smṛtaḥ
2.d: भोःशब्दं कीर्तयेदन्ते स्वस्य नाम्नो ऽभिवादने नाम्नां स्वरूपभावो हि भोभाव ऋषिभिः स्मृतः
2.e: In saluting, one should pronounce the term “Oh, Sir” at the end op his own name; since it has been declared by the sages that the form “Oh, Sir” represents the form of all names.

2.s: āyuṣmān bhava saumyaiti vācyo vipro 'bhivādane akāraścāsya nāmno 'nte vācyaḥ pūrvākṣaraḥ plutaḥ
2.d: आयुष्मान् भव सौम्यैति वाच्यो विप्रो ऽभिवादने अकारश्चास्य नाम्नो ऽन्ते वाच्यः पूर्वाक्षरः प्लुतः
2.e: On saluting, the Brāhmaṇa should he answered with the words ‘Be long lived, O Gentle One’; and at the end of his name the vowel “a,” which occurs at the end of the consonant, should be pronounced ultra long.

2.s: yo na vettyabhivādasya vipraḥ pratyabhivādanam nābhivādyaḥ sa viduṣā yathā śūdrastathaiva saḥ
2.d: यो न वेत्त्यभिवादस्य विप्रः प्रत्यभिवादनम् नाभिवाद्यः स विदुषा यथा शूद्रस्तथैव सः
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa who knows not the return-greeting of the greeting of salutation does not deserve to be saluted by the learned; he is exactly as the śūdra is.

2.s: brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchet kṣatrabandhumanāmayam vaiśyaṃ kṣemaṃ samāgamya śūdramārogyameva ca
2.d: ब्राह्मणं कुशलं पृच्छेत् क्षत्रबन्धुमनामयम् वैश्यं क्षेमं समागम्य शूद्रमारोग्यमेव च
2.e: Having met a Brāhmaṇa, one should ask him his “welfare,” a Kṣatriya his “freedom from distemper,” a Vaiśya his “prosperity,” and a Shudra his “freedom from disease.”

2.s: avācyo dīkṣito nāmnā yavīyānapi yo bhavet bhobhavatpūrvakaṃ tvenamabhibhāṣeta dharmavit
2.d: अवाच्यो दीक्षितो नाम्ना यवीयानपि यो भवेत् भोभवत्पूर्वकं त्वेनमभिभाषेत धर्मवित्
2.e: A person who has been initiated (for a rite), even though he be younger, should not be addressed by name; one who knows the law should address him beginning with such terms as “sir” and “your worship.”

2.s: parapatnī tu yā strī syādasaṃbandhā ca yonitaḥ tāṃ brūyādbhavatītyevaṃ subhage bhaginīti ca
2.d: परपत्नी तु या स्त्री स्यादसंबन्धा च योनितः तां ब्रूयाद्भवतीत्येवं सुभगे भगिनीति च
2.e: A female who is the wife of another person, and is not related to one by birth, should be addressed as “Lady,” and also “blessed,” or “sister.”

2.s: mātulāṃśca pitṛvyāṃśca śvaśurān ṛtvijo gurūn asāvahamiti brūyāt pratyutthāya yavīyasaḥ
2.d: मातुलांश्च पितृव्यांश्च श्वशुरान् ऋत्विजो गुरून् असावहमिति ब्रूयात् प्रत्युत्थाय यवीयसः
2.e: One should rise and say ‘here (so and so) I am,’ to such maternal uncles, paternal uncles, fathers-in-law and superiors as happen to be younger.

2.s: mātṛśvasā mātulānī śvaśrūratha pitṛśvasā saṃpūjyā gurupatnīvat samāstā gurubhāryayā
2.d: मातृश्वसा मातुलानी श्वश्रूरथ पितृश्वसा संपूज्या गुरुपत्नीवत् समास्ता गुरुभार्यया
2.e: Mother’s sister, maternal uncle’s wife, mother-in-law, and father’s sister deserve to re honoured like the teacher’s wife; all these are equal to the wife of the Teacher.

2.s: bhrāturbhāryaupasaṅgrāhyā savarṇā 'hanyahanyapi viproṣya tūpasaṅgrāhyā jñātisaṃbandhiyoṣitaḥ
2.d: भ्रातुर्भार्यौपसङ्ग्राह्या सवर्णा ऽहन्यहन्यपि विप्रोष्य तूपसङ्ग्राह्या ज्ञातिसंबन्धियोषितः
2.e: The brother’s wife, if of the same caste, should be clasped in the feet day by day; but the wives of other paternal, maternal and other relatives should be so clasped only when one has gone on a journey.

2.s: piturbhaginyāṃ mātuśca jyāyasyāṃ ca svasaryapi mātṛvadvṛttimātiṣṭhen mātā tābhyo garīyasī
2.d: पितुर्भगिन्यां मातुश्च ज्यायस्यां च स्वसर्यपि मातृवद्वृत्तिमातिष्ठेन् माता ताभ्यो गरीयसी
2.e: Towards his father’s sister, his mother’s sister, and his own elder sister, one should adopt the same behaviour as towards his mother; but the mother is more venerable than these.

2.s: daśābdākhyaṃ paurasakhyaṃ pañcābdākhyaṃ kalābhṛtām tryabdapūrvaṃ śrotriyāṇāṃ svalpenāpi svayoniṣu
2.d: दशाब्दाख्यं पौरसख्यं पञ्चाब्दाख्यं कलाभृताम् त्र्यब्दपूर्वं श्रोत्रियाणां स्वल्पेनापि स्वयोनिषु
2.e: Among citizens friendship and equality are regarded as ranging within ten years (of age-difference); among artists, it is regarded as ranging within five years; among learned men, it proceeds up to three years; and among blood-relations, it ranges only within a very short period of time.

2.s: brāhmaṇaṃ daśavarṣaṃ tu śatavarṣaṃ tu bhūmipam pitāputrau vijānīyādbrāhmaṇastu tayoḥ pitā
2.d: ब्राह्मणं दशवर्षं तु शतवर्षं तु भूमिपम् पितापुत्रौ विजानीयाद्ब्राह्मणस्तु तयोः पिता
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa or ten years and the Kṣatriya or a hundred years should be known as father and son; and of the two this Brāhmaṇa is the father.

2.s: vittaṃ bandhurvayaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī etāni mānyasthānāni garīyo yadyaduttaram mānasthānāni
2.d: वित्तं बन्धुर्वयः कर्म विद्या भवति पञ्चमी एतानि मान्यस्थानानि गरीयो यद्यदुत्तरम् मानस्थानानि
2.e: Wealth, Relation, Age, Action and Learning, as the fifth,—these are the grounds of respect; (among them) that which follows is weightier (than that which goes before it).

2.s: pañcānāṃ triṣu varṇeṣu bhūyāṃsi guṇavanti ca yatra syuḥ so 'tra mānārhaḥ śūdro 'pi daśamīṃ gataḥ
2.d: पञ्चानां त्रिषु वर्णेषु भूयांसि गुणवन्ति च यत्र स्युः सो ऽत्र मानार्हः शूद्रो ऽपि दशमीं गतः
2.e: Among the three (higher) castes, he, in whom there are present most op these five, and of high degree, deserves (greater) respect; as also the Śūdra who has reached the tenth stage (of life).

2.s: cakriṇo daśamīsthasya rogiṇo bhāriṇaḥ striyāḥ snātakasya ca rājñaśca panthā deyo varasya ca
2.d: चक्रिणो दशमीस्थस्य रोगिणो भारिणः स्त्रियाः स्नातकस्य च राज्ञश्च पन्था देयो वरस्य च
2.e: Way should be made for one in a chariot, for one who is in the tenth stage of life, for one suffering from disease, for one carrying a burden, for a woman, for the person who has just passed out of studentship, for the king and for the bridegroom.

2.s: teṣāṃ tu samāvetānāṃ mānyau snātakapārthivau rājasnātakayoścaiva snātako nṛpamānabhāk
2.d: तेषां तु समावेतानां मान्यौ स्नातकपार्थिवौ राजस्नातकयोश्चैव स्नातको नृपमानभाक्
2.e: Among these, when they come together, the man who has just passed his studentship and the King deserve to be honoured; and between the person just passed his studentship and the King, the person just passed his studentship receives the respects op the King.

2.s: upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyaṃ vedamadhyāpayeddvijaḥ sakalpaṃ sarahasyaṃ ca tamācāryaṃ pracakṣate
2.d: उपनीय तु यः शिष्यं वेदमध्यापयेद्द्विजः सकल्पं सरहस्यं च तमाचार्यं प्रचक्षते
2.e: The Brāhmana who, having initiated a pupil, teaches him the Veda along with the Ritualistic and esoteric treatises,—him they call, ‘Ācārya,’ ‘Preceptor’

2.s: ekadeśaṃ tu vedasya vedāṅgānyapi vā punaḥ yo 'dhyāpayati vṛttyarthamupādhyāyaḥ sa ucyate
2.d: एकदेशं तु वेदस्य वेदाङ्गान्यपि वा पुनः यो ऽध्यापयति वृत्त्यर्थमुपाध्यायः स उच्यते
2.e: He is called “Upādhyāya,” “Sub-teacher,” who teaches, for a living, only a part of the Veda, or only the Vedic subsidiary sciences.

2.s: niṣekādīni karmāṇi yaḥ karoti yathāvidhi saṃbhāvayati cānnena sa vipro gururucyate
2.d: निषेकादीनि कर्माणि यः करोति यथाविधि संभावयति चान्नेन स विप्रो गुरुरुच्यते
2.e: That Brāhmaṇa, who performs, in the prescribed manner, one’s sacramental rites beginning with the rites of impregnation, and supports him with food, is called the “Guru,” “Mentor.”

2.s: agnyādheyaṃ pākayajñānagniṣṭomādikān makhān yaḥ karoti vṛto yasya sa tasyaṛtvigihaucyate
2.d: अग्न्याधेयं पाकयज्ञानग्निष्टोमादिकान् मखान् यः करोति वृतो यस्य स तस्यऋत्विगिहौच्यते
2.e: He who, being duly appointed, performs, for one the Fire-laying rite, the Cooked Sacrifices and the Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices,—is called his “officiating priest.”

2.s: ya āvṛṇotyavitathaṃ brahmaṇā śravaṇāvubhau sa mātā sa pitā jñeyastaṃ na druhyet kadā cana
2.d: य आवृणोत्यवितथं ब्रह्मणा श्रवणावुभौ स माता स पिता ज्ञेयस्तं न द्रुह्येत् कदा चन
2.e: He who rightly fills one’s both ears with the Veda should be regarded as his Father and Mother; one should not, at any time, do him harm.

2.s: upādhyāyān daśācārya ācāryāṇāṃ śataṃ pitā sahasraṃ tu pitr̥̄n mātā gauraveṇātiricyate
2.d: उपाध्यायान् दशाचार्य आचार्याणां शतं पिता सहस्रं तु पित्र्̥̄न् माता गौरवेणातिरिच्यते
2.e: In veneration, the Preceptor excels ten Sub-teachers; the Father a hundred preceptors, and the Mother a thousand Fathers.

2.s: utpādakabrahmadātrorgarīyān brahmadaḥ pitā brahmajanma hi viprasya pretya caiha ca śāśvatam
2.d: उत्पादकब्रह्मदात्रोर्गरीयान् ब्रह्मदः पिता ब्रह्मजन्म हि विप्रस्य प्रेत्य चैह च शाश्वतम्
2.e: Between the progenitor and the imparter of the veda, the imparter op the veda is the more venerable father; for the brāhmaṇa’s “birth” is the veda, eternally,—here as well as after death.

2.s: kāmān mātā pitā cainaṃ yadutpādayato mithaḥ saṃbhūtiṃ tasya tāṃ vidyādyadyonāvabhijāyate
2.d: कामान् माता पिता चैनं यदुत्पादयतो मिथः संभूतिं तस्य तां विद्याद्यद्योनावभिजायते
2.e: When the Father and Mother beget one through mutual desire,—this that he is born in the womb is to be regarded as his “production.”

2.s: ācāryastvasya yāṃ jātiṃ vidhivadvedapāragaḥ utpādayati sāvitryā sā satyā sā 'jarā 'marā
2.d: आचार्यस्त्वस्य यां जातिं विधिवद्वेदपारगः उत्पादयति सावित्र्या सा सत्या सा ऽजरा ऽमरा
2.e: But the “birth” which the Preceptor, well-versed in the Veda, brings about for him, in the lawful manner, by means of the Sāvitrī,—that is real, imperishable, immortal.

2.s: alpaṃ vā bahu vā yasya śrutasyaupakaroti yaḥ tamapīha guruṃ vidyātśrutaupakriyayā tayā
2.d: अल्पं वा बहु वा यस्य श्रुतस्यौपकरोति यः तमपीह गुरुं विद्यात्श्रुतौपक्रियया तया
2.e: If one benefits him by means of knowledge, more or less,—him also one should regard herb as the “mentor,” by virtue of that benefit of knowledge.

2.s: brāhmasya janmanaḥ kartā svadharmasya ca śāsitā bālo 'pi vipro vṛddhasya pitā bhavati dharmataḥ
2.d: ब्राह्मस्य जन्मनः कर्ता स्वधर्मस्य च शासिता बालो ऽपि विप्रो वृद्धस्य पिता भवति धर्मतः
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa, who brings about his Vedic birth, and teaches him his duty,—even though he be a mere child,—becomes in law the father of the old man (whom he teaches).

2.s: adhyāpayāmāsa pitr̥̄n śiśurāṅgirasaḥ kaviḥ putrakā iti hauvāca jñānena parigṛhya tān
2.d: अध्यापयामास पित्र्̥̄न् शिशुराङ्गिरसः कविः पुत्रका इति हौवाच ज्ञानेन परिगृह्य तान्
2.e: The child Kavi, the son of Aṅgiras, taught his fathers; and having received and trained them by knowledge, he called them “little sons.”

2.s: te tamarthamapṛcchanta devānāgatamanyavaḥ devāścaitān sametyaucurnyāyyaṃ vaḥ śiśuruktavān
2.d: ते तमर्थमपृच्छन्त देवानागतमन्यवः देवाश्चैतान् समेत्यौचुर्न्याय्यं वः शिशुरुक्तवान्
2.e: They, having their anger aroused, questioned the gods about this matter; and the gods, having met together, said to them—“the child has addressed you in the lawful manner.”

2.s: ajño bhavati vai bālaḥ pitā bhavati mantradaḥ ajñaṃ hi bālamityāhuḥ pitaityeva tu mantradam
2.d: अज्ञो भवति वै बालः पिता भवति मन्त्रदः अज्ञं हि बालमित्याहुः पितैत्येव तु मन्त्रदम्
2.e: The ignorant person is verily a “child,” while the imparted of mantras is the “father.” They have called the ignorant man “child,” and the imparter of mantras, “father.”

2.s: na hāyanairna palitairna vittena na bandhubhiḥ ṛṣayaścakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān
2.d: न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्मं यो ऽनूचानः स नो महान्
2.e: Neither by years, nor by grey hair, nor by wealth, nor by relatives (is greatness attained); since the sages have made the law that ‘he who teaches is the greatest among us.’

2.s: viprāṇāṃ jñānato jyaiṣṭhyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu vīryataḥ vaiśyānāṃ dhānyadhanataḥ śūdrāṇāmeva janmataḥ
2.d: विप्राणां ज्ञानतो ज्यैष्ठ्यं क्षत्रियाणां तु वीर्यतः वैश्यानां धान्यधनतः शूद्राणामेव जन्मतः
2.e: Among Brāhmaṇas seniority is by knowledge; among Kṣatriyas by valour; and among Vaiśyas by grains and riches; among Shudras alone it is by age.

2.s: na tena vṛddho bhavati yenāsya palitaṃ śiraḥ yo vai yuvā 'pyadhīyānastaṃ devāḥ sthaviraṃ viduḥ
2.d: न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः यो वै युवा ऽप्यधीयानस्तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः
2.e: One does not become venerable by the fact that his hair has turned grey; the gods know him to be venerable who, though young, continues to study.

2.s: yathā kāṣṭhamayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ yaśca vipro 'nadhīyānastrayaste nāma bibhrati
2.d: यथा काष्ठमयो हस्ती यथा चर्ममयो मृगः यश्च विप्रो ऽनधीयानस्त्रयस्ते नाम बिभ्रति
2.e: As the elephant made of wood, as the deer made of leather, so the non-learning Brāhmaṇa,—these three merely bear their names.

2.s: yathā ṣaṇḍho 'phalaḥ strīṣu yathā gaurgavi cāphalā yathā cājñe 'phalaṃ dānaṃ tathā vipro 'nṛco 'phalaḥ
2.d: यथा षण्ढो ऽफलः स्त्रीषु यथा गौर्गवि चाफला यथा चाज्ञे ऽफलं दानं तथा विप्रो ऽनृचो ऽफलः
2.e: As the eunuch is useless among women, as the cow is useless among cows, as a gift to the ignorant person is useless, even so is the Bbrāhmaṇa useless who is devoid of the Veda.

2.s: ahiṃsayaiva bhūtānāṃ kāryaṃ śreyo 'nuśāsanam vāk caiva madhurā ślakṣṇā prayojyā dharmamicchatā
2.d: अहिंसयैव भूतानां कार्यं श्रेयो ऽनुशासनम् वाक् चैव मधुरा श्लक्ष्णा प्रयोज्या धर्ममिच्छता
2.e: Teaching for good should be imparted to living beings, without injury to them; and sweet and soft words should be employed by one who seeks for merit.

2.s: yasya vācmanasī śuddhe samyaggupte ca sarvadā sa vai sarvamavāpnoti vedāntaupagataṃ phalam
2.d: यस्य वाच्मनसी शुद्धे सम्यग्गुप्ते च सर्वदा स वै सर्वमवाप्नोति वेदान्तौपगतं फलम्
2.e: He, whose speech and mind are pure and ever properly guarded, obtains the whole reward recognised by the canons of the Veda.

2.s: nāruṃtudaḥ syādārto 'pi na paradrohakarmadhīḥ yayā 'syaudvijate vācā nālokyāṃ tāmudīrayet
2.d: नारुंतुदः स्यादार्तो ऽपि न परद्रोहकर्मधीः यया ऽस्यौद्विजते वाचा नालोक्यां तामुदीरयेत्
2.e: Even though pained, one should not (use such words as) cut to the quick; he should not do, or think of, injury to others; he should not utter words by which others are pained, and which (therefore) will obstruct his passage to (higher) regions.

2.s: sammānādbrāhmaṇo nityamudvijeta viṣādiva amṛtasyaiva cākāṅkṣedavamānasya sarvadā
2.d: सम्मानाद्ब्राह्मणो नित्यमुद्विजेत विषादिव अमृतस्यैव चाकाङ्क्षेदवमानस्य सर्वदा
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa should ever shrink from reverence, as from poison; and he should always seek for disrespect, as for nectar.

2.s: sukhaṃ hyavamataḥ śete sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate sukhaṃ carati loke 'sminnavamantā vinaśyati
2.d: सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते सुखं च प्रतिबुध्यते सुखं चरति लोके ऽस्मिन्नवमन्ता विनश्यति
2.e: One who is scorned sleeps in comport and wakes up in comfort and goes about in the world in comport; it is the scorner that perishes.

2.s: anena kramayogena saṃskṛtātmā dvijaḥ śanaiḥ gurau vasan sañcinuyādbrahmādhigamikaṃ tapaḥ
2.d: अनेन क्रमयोगेन संस्कृतात्मा द्विजः शनैः गुरौ वसन् सञ्चिनुयाद्ब्रह्माधिगमिकं तपः
2.e: Sanctified in self, the twice-born man, while dwelling with his Teacher, should, by the adoption of this course, generally accumulate sanctity for the learning of the Veda.

2.s: tapoviśeṣairvividhairvrataiśca vidhicoditaiḥ vedaḥ kṛtsno 'dhigantavyaḥ sarahasyo dvijanmanā
2.d: तपोविशेषैर्विविधैर्व्रतैश्च विधिचोदितैः वेदः कृत्स्नो ऽधिगन्तव्यः सरहस्यो द्विजन्मना
2.e: The entire Veda, along with the Esoteric Treatises, should be learnt by the twice-born person,—by means of various kinds of austerities and observances prescribed by rule.

2.s: vedameva sadā 'bhyasyet tapastapsyan dvijottamaḥ vedābhyāso hi viprasya tapaḥ paramihaucyate
2.d: वेदमेव सदा ऽभ्यस्येत् तपस्तप्स्यन् द्विजोत्तमः वेदाभ्यासो हि विप्रस्य तपः परमिहौच्यते
2.e: The best of Brāhmaṇas, desiring to acquire piety, should constantly repeat the Veda; because for the Brāhmaṇa, Veda-repeating is declared to be the highest penance on earth.

2.s: ā haiva sa nakhāgrebhyaḥ paramaṃ tapyate tapaḥ yaḥ sragvyapi dvijo 'dhīte svādhyāyaṃ śaktito 'nvaham
2.d: आ हैव स नखाग्रेभ्यः परमं तप्यते तपः यः स्रग्व्यपि द्विजो ऽधीते स्वाध्यायं शक्तितो ऽन्वहम्
2.e: It is said that that twice-born man, who, even though garlanded, recites the Veda daily to the best of his capacity, undergoes the highest penance to his very nail-tips.

2.s: yo 'nadhītya dvijo vedamanyatra kurute śramam sa jīvanneva śūdratvamāśu gacchati sānvayaḥ
2.d: यो ऽनधीत्य द्विजो वेदमन्यत्र कुरुते श्रमम् स जीवन्नेव शूद्रत्वमाशु गच्छति सान्वयः
2.e: The twice-born man, who, not having learnt the veda, labours over other things, soon falls, along with his descendants, even while living, to the state of the śūdra.

2.s: māturagre 'dhijananaṃ dvitīyaṃ mauñjibandhane tṛtīyaṃ yajñadīkṣāyāṃ dvijasya śruticodanāt
2.d: मातुरग्रे ऽधिजननं द्वितीयं मौञ्जिबन्धने तृतीयं यज्ञदीक्षायां द्विजस्य श्रुतिचोदनात्
2.e: According to the directions of the Revealed Word, the first birth of the twice-born man is from the mother, the second, after the Ggirdle-tying ceremony, and the third, after sacrificial initiation.

2.s: tatra yadbrahmajanmāsya mauñjībandhanacihnitam tatrāsya mātā sāvitrī pitā tvācārya ucyate
2.d: तत्र यद्ब्रह्मजन्मास्य मौञ्जीबन्धनचिह्नितम् तत्रास्य माता सावित्री पिता त्वाचार्य उच्यते
2.e: Among these, at that Brahmic birth which is. marked by the tying of the girdle, the Sāvitrī has been declared to be his “Mother,” and the Teacher his “Father.”

2.s: vedapradānādācāryaṃ pitaraṃ paricakṣate na hyasmin yujyate karma kiñcidā mauñjibandhanāt
2.d: वेदप्रदानादाचार्यं पितरं परिचक्षते न ह्यस्मिन् युज्यते कर्म किञ्चिदा मौञ्जिबन्धनात्
2.e: They call the Teacher “father,” on account of his imparting the Veda. Before the tying of the girdle, the performance of no religious act is proper for him.

2.s: nābhivyāhārayedbrahma svadhāninayanādṛte śūdreṇa hi samastāvadyāvadvede na jāyate
2.d: नाभिव्याहारयेद्ब्रह्म स्वधानिनयनादृते शूद्रेण हि समस्तावद्यावद्वेदे न जायते
2.e: He should hot pronounce Vedic texts, apart from the Svadhā-offering; because so long as he is not born in the Veda, he is equal to a śūdra.

2.s: kṛtaupanayanasyāsya vratādeśanamiṣyate brahmaṇo grahaṇaṃ caiva krameṇa vidhipūrvakam
2.d: कृतौपनयनस्यास्य व्रतादेशनमिष्यते ब्रह्मणो ग्रहणं चैव क्रमेण विधिपूर्वकम्
2.e: For the boy whose initiatory rite has been performed, instruction regarding; observances is considered desirable; as also the getting up of the Veda, in due course, according to the prescribed rule.

2.s: yadyasya vihitaṃ carma yat sūtraṃ yā ca mekhalā yo daṇḍo yatca vasanaṃ tat tadasya vrateṣvapi
2.d: यद्यस्य विहितं चर्म यत् सूत्रं या च मेखला यो दण्डो यत्च वसनं तत् तदस्य व्रतेष्वपि
2.e: That skin, that sac red thread, that girdle, that staff and that garment, which has been prescribed for one, stand during the observances also.

2.s: sevetaimāṃstu niyamān brahmacārī gurau vasan sanniyamyaindriyagrāmaṃ tapovṛddhiarthamātmanaḥ
2.d: सेवेतैमांस्तु नियमान् ब्रह्मचारी गुरौ वसन् सन्नियम्यैन्द्रियग्रामं तपोवृद्धिअर्थमात्मनः
2.e: With a view to enhancing his own piety, the Rreligious Student should, while living with his Teacher, observe all these rules,—having fully subjugated all his organs.

2.s: nityaṃ snātvā śuciḥ kuryāddevaṛṣipitṛtarpaṇam devatābhyarcanaṃ caiva samidādhānameva ca
2.d: नित्यं स्नात्वा शुचिः कुर्याद्देवऋषिपितृतर्पणम् देवताभ्यर्चनं चैव समिदाधानमेव च
2.e: Every day, having bathed and become clean, he should make offerings to deities, Sages and Fathers, and do the worshipping of the deities and the placing of fuel.

2.s: varjayen madhu māṃsaṃ ca gandhaṃ mālyaṃ rasān striyaḥ śuktāni yāni sarvāṇi prāṇināṃ caiva hiṃsanam
2.d: वर्जयेन् मधु मांसं च गन्धं माल्यं रसान् स्त्रियः शुक्तानि यानि सर्वाणि प्राणिनां चैव हिंसनम्
2.e: He should abstain from honey, meat, scent, garland, flavours, women, all fermented acids and also the killing of living creatures.

2.s: abhyaṅgamañjanaṃ cākṣṇorupānahchatradhāraṇam kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca nartanaṃ gītavādanam
2.d: अभ्यङ्गमञ्जनं चाक्ष्णोरुपानह्छत्रधारणम् कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च नर्तनं गीतवादनम्
2.e: From anointing, applying collyrium to the eyes, shoes, holding the umbrella, attachment, anger, avarice, dancing, singing and playing on musical instruments.

2.s: dyūtaṃ ca janavādaṃ ca parivādaṃ tathā 'nṛtam strīṇāṃ ca prekṣaṇālambhamupaghātaṃ parasya ca ālambhā
2.d: द्यूतं च जनवादं च परिवादं तथा ऽनृतम् स्त्रीणां च प्रेक्षणालम्भमुपघातं परस्य च आलम्भा
2.e: From gambling, quarelling with people, calumniating, and also lying; prom gazing at and touching of women, and prom the injuring op others.

2.s: ekaḥ śayīta sarvatra na retaḥ skandayet kva cit kāmāddhi skandayan reto hinasti vratamātmanaḥ
2.d: एकः शयीत सर्वत्र न रेतः स्कन्दयेत् क्व चित् कामाद्धि स्कन्दयन् रेतो हिनस्ति व्रतमात्मनः
2.e: He should always sleep alone; nowhere should he allow his manhood to run out; by intentionally allowing his manhood to run out, hr breaks his vow.

2.s: svapne siktvā brahmacārī dvijaḥ śukramakāmataḥ snātvā 'rkamarcayitvā triḥ punarmāmity ṛcaṃ japet
2.d: स्वप्ने सिक्त्वा ब्रह्मचारी द्विजः शुक्रमकामतः स्नात्वा ऽर्कमर्चयित्वा त्रिः पुनर्मामित्य् ऋचं जपेत्
2.e: The twice-born religious student, haying unintentionally dropped his manhood during a dream, should thrice recite the three vedic verses beginning with “punarmām,” after having bathed and worshipped the sun.

2.s: udakumbhaṃ sumanaso gośakṛtmṛttikākuśān āharedyāvadarthāni bhaikṣaṃ cāhar 'haścaret
2.d: उदकुम्भं सुमनसो गोशकृत्मृत्तिकाकुशान् आहरेद्यावदर्थानि भैक्षं चाहर् ऽहश्चरेत्
2.e: He should fetch the jar of water, flowers, cowdung, earth and kuśa-grass,—as much as may be required; and day by day he should beg for alms.

2.s: vedayajñairahīnānāṃ praśastānāṃ svakarmasu brahmacāryāharedbhaikṣaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ prayato 'nvaham
2.d: वेदयज्ञैरहीनानां प्रशस्तानां स्वकर्मसु ब्रह्मचार्याहरेद्भैक्षं गृहेभ्यः प्रयतो ऽन्वहम्
2.e: The Religious Student, being pure, should fetch alms daily from the houses of persons who are not devoid of Veda and sacrifices, and who are famed for their deeds.

2.s: guroḥ kule na bhikṣeta na jñātikulabandhuṣu alābhe tvanyagehānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ vivarjayet
2.d: गुरोः कुले न भिक्षेत न ज्ञातिकुलबन्धुषु अलाभे त्वन्यगेहानां पूर्वं पूर्वं विवर्जयेत्
2.e: He should not beg for food from his Teacher’s family; nor from the family of his paternal or maternal relations. But when other houses are not available, he should avoid the preceding in preference to the succeeding.

2.s: sarvaṃ vāpi caredgrāmaṃ pūrvauktānāmasaṃbhave niyamya prayato vācamabhiśastāṃstu varjayet
2.d: सर्वं वापि चरेद्ग्रामं पूर्वौक्तानामसंभवे नियम्य प्रयतो वाचमभिशस्तांस्तु वर्जयेत्
2.e: In the event of al the afouesaid being not available, he may wander over the whole village, remaining pure and having his speech well-controlled; but he should avoid persons of ill-repute.

2.s: dūrādāhṛtya samidhaḥ sannidadhyādvihāyasi sāyaṃprātaśca juhuyāt tābhiragnimatandritaḥ
2.d: दूरादाहृत्य समिधः सन्निदध्याद्विहायसि सायंप्रातश्च जुहुयात् ताभिरग्निमतन्द्रितः
2.e: Having fetched fuel-sticks from a distance, he should place them in the air; and with these he should, without fail, make offerings to the fire, morning and evening.

2.s: akṛtvā bhaikṣacaraṇamasamidhya ca pāvakam anāturaḥ saptarātramavakīrṇivrataṃ caret
2.d: अकृत्वा भैक्षचरणमसमिध्य च पावकम् अनातुरः सप्तरात्रमवकीर्णिव्रतं चरेत्
2.e: He who, without being ill, omits for seven days, to beg alms and to offer fuel to the fire, shall perform the rites prescribed for the Avakīrṇin.

2.s: bhaikṣeṇa vartayennityaṃ naikānnādī bhavedvratī bhaikṣeṇa vratino vṛttirupavāsasamā smṛtā
2.d: भैक्षेण वर्तयेन्नित्यं नैकान्नादी भवेद्व्रती भैक्षेण व्रतिनो वृत्तिरुपवाससमा स्मृता
2.e: The avowed student should subsist on alms; he should not (habitually) eat the food given by one person. for the student, subsisting on alms has been declared to be equal to fasting.

2.s: vratavaddevadaivatye pitrye karmaṇyathaṛṣivat kāmamabhyarthito 'śnīyādvratamasya na lupyate
2.d: व्रतवद्देवदैवत्ये पित्र्ये कर्मण्यथऋषिवत् काममभ्यर्थितो ऽश्नीयाद्व्रतमस्य न लुप्यते
2.e: During a performance in honour of gods and in honour of ancestors, he may, when invited, eat freely, like an ascetic, in due accordance with his observances. by this his observances do not suffer.

2.s: brāhmaṇasyaiva karmaitadupadiṣṭaṃ manīṣibhiḥ rājanyavaiśyayostvevaṃ naitat karma vidhīyate
2.d: ब्राह्मणस्यैव कर्मैतदुपदिष्टं मनीषिभिः राजन्यवैश्ययोस्त्वेवं नैतत् कर्म विधीयते
2.e: This duty has been prescribed by the sages for the Brāhmaṇa only; this duty has not been so ordained for the Kṣatriya and the Vaiśya.

2.s: codito guruṇā nityamapracodita eva vā kuryādadhyayane yatnamācāryasya hiteṣu ca 'dhyayane yogam
2.d: चोदितो गुरुणा नित्यमप्रचोदित एव वा कुर्यादध्ययने यत्नमाचार्यस्य हितेषु च ऽध्ययने योगम्
2.e: Prompted by the Teacher, or even when not prompted, he should put forth his exertion to study, and also to doing what is helpful to the teacher.

2.s: śarīraṃ caiva vācaṃ ca buddhīndriyamanāṃsi ca niyamya prāñjalistiṣṭhedvīkṣamāṇo gurormukham
2.d: शरीरं चैव वाचं च बुद्धीन्द्रियमनांसि च नियम्य प्राञ्जलिस्तिष्ठेद्वीक्षमाणो गुरोर्मुखम्
2.e: Having under control his body and his speech, as also his organs of sensation and his hind, he should stand with joined palms, looking at the face of his Teacher.

2.s: nityamuddhṛtapāṇiḥ syāt sādhuācāraḥ susaṃvṛtaḥ āsyatāmiti cauktaḥ sannāsītābhimukhaṃ guroḥ
2.d: नित्यमुद्धृतपाणिः स्यात् साधुआचारः सुसंवृतः आस्यतामिति चौक्तः सन्नासीताभिमुखं गुरोः
2.e: He should always have his arm raised, remain well behaved, and well-guarded; when addressed with the words “be seated,” he should sit facing his teacher.

2.s: hīnānnavastraveṣaḥ syāt sarvadā gurusannidhau uttiṣṭhet prathamaṃ cāsya caramaṃ caiva saṃviśet
2.d: हीनान्नवस्त्रवेषः स्यात् सर्वदा गुरुसन्निधौ उत्तिष्ठेत् प्रथमं चास्य चरमं चैव संविशेत्
2.e: In the peesenge of his Teacher, he should always have inferior food, dress and apparel; he should rise before him, and go to sleep later.

2.s: pratiśrāvaṇasaṃbhāṣe śayāno na samācaret nāsīno na ca bhuñjāno na tiṣṭhanna parālgmukhaḥ
2.d: प्रतिश्रावणसंभाषे शयानो न समाचरेत् नासीनो न च भुञ्जानो न तिष्ठन्न पराल्ग्मुखः
2.e: He should not listen to and converse with (his Teacher), while lying down; nor while seated, nor while eating, nor while standing, nor with his face turned away.

2.s: āsīnasya sthitaḥ kuryādabhigacchaṃstu tiṣṭhataḥ pratyudgamya tvāvrajataḥ paścāddhāvaṃstu dhāvataḥ
2.d: आसीनस्य स्थितः कुर्यादभिगच्छंस्तु तिष्ठतः प्रत्युद्गम्य त्वाव्रजतः पश्चाद्धावंस्तु धावतः
2.e: He should do (these) standing, when the teacher is seated; advancing towards him, when he is standing; going forward to him, when he advances; and running after him, when he runs;

2.s: parālgmukhasyābhimukho dūrasthasyaitya cāntikam praṇamya tu śayānasya nideśe caiva tiṣṭhataḥ
2.d: पराल्ग्मुखस्याभिमुखो दूरस्थस्यैत्य चान्तिकम् प्रणम्य तु शयानस्य निदेशे चैव तिष्ठतः
2.e: Facing him, when the teacher has his pace averted; going near him, when the teacher is at a distance; bowing low, when the teacher is lying down, as also if he is standing close by.

2.s: nīcaṃ śayyā ''sanaṃ cāsya nityaṃ syādgurusannidhau gurostu cakṣurviṣaye na yathaiṣṭāsano bhavet
2.d: नीचं शय्या 'ऽसनं चास्य नित्यं स्याद्गुरुसन्निधौ गुरोस्तु चक्षुर्विषये न यथैष्टासनो भवेत्
2.e: When near his Teacher, his bed or seat should always be low; and within sight op his Teacher, he should not sit at ease.

2.s: naudāharedasya nāma parokṣamapi kevalam na caivāsyānukurvīta gatibhāṣitaceṣṭitam
2.d: नौदाहरेदस्य नाम परोक्षमपि केवलम् न चैवास्यानुकुर्वीत गतिभाषितचेष्टितम्
2.e: Even behind the Teacher’s back, he should not pronounce his mere name; nor should he mimic his gait, speech or deportment.

2.s: guroryatra parivādo nindā vā 'pi pravartate karṇau tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato 'nyataḥ
2.d: गुरोर्यत्र परिवादो निन्दा वा ऽपि प्रवर्तते कर्णौ तत्र पिधातव्यौ गन्तव्यं वा ततो ऽन्यतः
2.e: Where the censuring or defaming of his Teacher is going on, there he should either close his ears, or go away thence to another place.

2.s: parīvādāt kharo bhavati śvā vai bhavati nindakaḥ paribhoktā kṛmirbhavati kīṭo bhavati matsarī
2.d: परीवादात् खरो भवति श्वा वै भवति निन्दकः परिभोक्ता कृमिर्भवति कीटो भवति मत्सरी
2.e: Through censure one becomes an ass, and the defamer becomes a dog; he who lives on him becomes a worm, and he who is jealous becomes an insect.

2.s: dūrastho nārcayedenaṃ na kruddho nāntike striyāḥ yānāsanasthaścaivainamavaruhyābhivādayet
2.d: दूरस्थो नार्चयेदेनं न क्रुद्धो नान्तिके स्त्रियाः यानासनस्थश्चैवैनमवरुह्याभिवादयेत्
2.e: He should not offer his worship to the teacher while at a distance from him; nor when angry, nor near a woman. If seated upon a conveyance or a seat, he should come down and then salute him.

2.s: prativāte 'nuvāte ca nāsīta guruṇā saha prativātānuvāte asaṃśrave caiva gurorna kiṃ cidapi kīrtayet
2.d: प्रतिवाते ऽनुवाते च नासीत गुरुणा सह प्रतिवातानुवाते असंश्रवे चैव गुरोर्न किं चिदपि कीर्तयेत्
2.e: When sitting in the company of his teacher, uk should not sit either to the lee-ward or to the wind-ward of him; nor should he say anything beyond the hearing of his teacher.

2.s: go 'śvauṣṭrayānaprāsādaprastareṣu kaṭeṣu ca āsīta guruṇā sārdhaṃ śilāphalakanauṣu ca
2.d: गो ऽश्वौष्ट्रयानप्रासादप्रस्तरेषु कटेषु च आसीत गुरुणा सार्धं शिलाफलकनौषु च
2.e: He may sit with the teacher on carts drawn by oxen, horses and camels, on terraces and on grass-mats; as also on reedmats, rocks, benches and boats.

2.s: gurorgurau sannihite guruvadvṛttimācaret na cānisṛṣṭo guruṇā svān gurūnabhivādayet
2.d: गुरोर्गुरौ सन्निहिते गुरुवद्वृत्तिमाचरेत् न चानिसृष्टो गुरुणा स्वान् गुरूनभिवादयेत्
2.e: When the Teacher’s teacher happens to be close by, he should adopt towards him the same behaviour as towards his own teacher; but until permitted by his teacher, he should not pay respects to his own elders.

2.s: vidyāguruṣvevameva nityā vṛttiḥ svayoniṣu pratiṣedhatsu cādharmāddhitaṃ caupadiśatsvapi
2.d: विद्यागुरुष्वेवमेव नित्या वृत्तिः स्वयोनिषु प्रतिषेधत्सु चाधर्माद्धितं चौपदिशत्स्वपि
2.e: This same shall be his constant behaviour towards his intellectual teachers, towards his blood-relations, towards persons restraining him from sin and towards those who give him salutary advice.

2.s: śreyaḥsu guruvadvṛttiṃ nityameva samācaret guruputreṣu cāryeṣu guroścaiva svabandhuṣu guruputre tathācārye
2.d: श्रेयःसु गुरुवद्वृत्तिं नित्यमेव समाचरेत् गुरुपुत्रेषु चार्येषु गुरोश्चैव स्वबन्धुषु गुरुपुत्रे तथाचार्ये
2.e: Towards superiors he should always behave as towards the Teacher, as also towards the Teacher’s son who has acquired the position of the Teacher, and towards the Teacher’s own blood-relations.

2.s: bālaḥ samānajanmā vā śiṣyo vā yajñakarmaṇi adhyāpayan gurusuto guruvatmānamarhati
2.d: बालः समानजन्मा वा शिष्यो वा यज्ञकर्मणि अध्यापयन् गुरुसुतो गुरुवत्मानमर्हति
2.e: Whether he be younger, or of equal age, or a student of sacrificial ritual,—the Teacher’s son, imparting instruction, dfserves the same honour as the Teacher.

2.s: utsādanaṃ ca gātrāṇāṃ snāpanaucchiṣṭabhojane na kuryādguruputrasya pādayoścāvanejanam
2.d: उत्सादनं च गात्राणां स्नापनौच्छिष्टभोजने न कुर्याद्गुरुपुत्रस्य पादयोश्चावनेजनम्
2.e: He shall not shampoo the limbs of his teacher’s son, nor assist him in bathing, nor eat of the food left by him; nor should he wash his feet.

2.s: guruvat pratipūjyāḥ syuḥ savarṇā guruyoṣitaḥ asavarṇāstu sampūjyāḥ pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ
2.d: गुरुवत् प्रतिपूज्याः स्युः सवर्णा गुरुयोषितः असवर्णास्तु सम्पूज्याः प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादनैः
2.e: The teacher’s ladies belonging to the same caste should be honoured like the teacher himself; those not belonging to the same caste should be honoured with rising and salutations.

2.s: abhyañjanaṃ snāpanaṃ ca gātrautsādanameva ca gurupatnyā na kāryāṇi keśānāṃ ca prasādhanam
2.d: अभ्यञ्जनं स्नापनं च गात्रौत्सादनमेव च गुरुपत्न्या न कार्याणि केशानां च प्रसाधनम्
2.e: Annointing, assisting at bath, shampooing of limbs and dressing of the hair should not be done for the teacher’s wife.

2.s: gurupatnī tu yuvatirnābhivādyaiha pādayoḥ pūrṇaviṃśativarṣeṇa guṇadoṣau vijānatā
2.d: गुरुपत्नी तु युवतिर्नाभिवाद्यैह पादयोः पूर्णविंशतिवर्षेण गुणदोषौ विजानता
2.e: The teacher’s wife, when young, shall not be saluted at her feet by a pupil who is full twenty years old, and who is conscious of what is good and what is bad.

2.s: svabhāva eṣa nārīṇāṃ narāṇāmiha dūṣaṇam ato 'rthānna pramādyanti pramadāsu vipaścitaḥ
2.d: स्वभाव एष नारीणां नराणामिह दूषणम् अतो ऽर्थान्न प्रमाद्यन्ति प्रमदासु विपश्चितः
2.e: It is the very nature of women to corrupt men. It is for this reason that the wise are never unguarded regarding women.

2.s: avidvāṃsamalaṃ loke vidvāṃsamapi vā punaḥ pramadā hyutpathaṃ netuṃ kāmakrodhavaśānugam
2.d: अविद्वांसमलं लोके विद्वांसमपि वा पुनः प्रमदा ह्युत्पथं नेतुं कामक्रोधवशानुगम्
2.e: In this world women are capable op leading astray the ignorant, as well as the learned, who becomes a servile follower of desire and passion.

2.s: mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā na viviktāsano bhavet balavānindriyagrāmo vidvāṃsamapi karṣati
2.d: मात्रा स्वस्रा दुहित्रा वा न विविक्तासनो भवेत् बलवानिन्द्रियग्रामो विद्वांसमपि कर्षति
2.e: One should not sit alone with his mother, sister or daughter. The powerful host of sense-organs overpowers even the learned.

2.s: kāmaṃ tu gurupatnīnāṃ yuvatīnāṃ yuvā bhuvi vidhivadvandanaṃ kuryādasāvahamiti bruvan
2.d: कामं तु गुरुपत्नीनां युवतीनां युवा भुवि विधिवद्वन्दनं कुर्यादसावहमिति ब्रुवन्
2.e: The young man may perform the proper salutation on the ground to the young wives of his Teacher,—saying “here i am.”

2.s: viproṣya pādagrahaṇamanvahaṃ cābhivādanam gurudāreṣu kurvīta satāṃ dharmamanusmaran
2.d: विप्रोष्य पादग्रहणमन्वहं चाभिवादनम् गुरुदारेषु कुर्वीत सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन्
2.e: Having returned from a journey, he should clasp the feet of his Teacher’s wife, and daily he should salute her, bearing in mind the duty of the righteous.

2.s: yathā khanan khanitreṇa naro vāryadhigacchati tathā gurugatāṃ vidyāṃ śuśrūṣuradhigacchati
2.d: यथा खनन् खनित्रेण नरो वार्यधिगच्छति तथा गुरुगतां विद्यां शुश्रूषुरधिगच्छति
2.e: Just as a man digging with the spade obtains water,—even so one who is eager to serve acquires the learning that is in the Teacher.

2.s: muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā syādatha vā syātśikhājaṭaḥ nainaṃ grāme 'bhinimlocet sūryo nābhyudiyāt kva cit
2.d: मुण्डो वा जटिलो वा स्यादथ वा स्यात्शिखाजटः नैनं ग्रामे ऽभिनिम्लोचेत् सूर्यो नाभ्युदियात् क्व चित्
2.e: He may have his head shaved, or wear his hair in braids, or have only the top-hair braided. The sun should never set, nor should it rise, while he is still in the village.

2.s: taṃ cedabhyudiyāt sūryaḥ śayānaṃ kāmacārataḥ nimlocedvā 'pyavijñānāj japannupavaseddinam
2.d: तं चेदभ्युदियात् सूर्यः शयानं कामचारतः निम्लोचेद्वा ऽप्यविज्ञानाज् जपन्नुपवसेद्दिनम्
2.e: If the sun should rise or set while he is still sleeping, either intentionally or unintentionally, he should fast during the day, reciting. (the Sāvitrī).

2.s: sūryeṇa hyabhinirmuktaḥ śayāno 'bhyuditaśca yaḥ 'bhinimluktaḥ prāyaścittamakurvāṇo yuktaḥ syān mahatainasā
2.d: सूर्येण ह्यभिनिर्मुक्तः शयानो ऽभ्युदितश्च यः ऽभिनिम्लुक्तः प्रायश्चित्तमकुर्वाणो युक्तः स्यान् महतैनसा
2.e: If during one’s sleep the sun has set, and if during one’s sleep the sun has risen,—if he does not perform the Expiatory Rite, he becomes tainted by grievous sin.

2.s: ācamya prayato nityamubhe saṃdhye samāhitaḥ śucau deśe japañjapyamupāsīta yathāvidhi
2.d: आचम्य प्रयतो नित्यमुभे संध्ये समाहितः शुचौ देशे जपञ्जप्यमुपासीत यथाविधि
2.e: Having sipped water, with calm and collected mind, he shall daily attend upon the two twilights, in a clean place, reciting the mantras to be recited, according to rule.

2.s: yadi strī yadyavarajaḥ śreyaḥ kiṃ cit samācaret tat sarvamācaredyukto yatra cāsya ramen manaḥ
2.d: यदि स्त्री यद्यवरजः श्रेयः किं चित् समाचरेत् तत् सर्वमाचरेद्युक्तो यत्र चास्य रमेन् मनः
2.e: If either a woman; or a junior person, do something good, he should faithfully perform all that; as also that in which his mind finds satisfaction.

2.s: dharmārthāvucyate śreyaḥ kāmārthau dharma eva ca artha evaiha vā śreyastrivarga iti tu sthitiḥ
2.d: धर्मार्थावुच्यते श्रेयः कामार्थौ धर्म एव च अर्थ एवैह वा श्रेयस्त्रिवर्ग इति तु स्थितिः
2.e: Spiritual merit and wealth are called “good”; or pleasure and wealth; or spiritual merit alone, or wealth alone is “good”; but the truth is that it is the aggregate of the three.

2.s: ācāryaśca pitā caiva mātā bhrātā ca pūrvajaḥ nārtenāpyavamantavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ
2.d: आचार्यश्च पिता चैव माता भ्राता च पूर्वजः नार्तेनाप्यवमन्तव्या ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः
2.e: The preceptor, the father, the mother and the elder brother should not be treated with disrespect, especially by a Brāhmaṇa,—even though he be distressed

2.s: ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ mātā pṛthivyā mūrtistu bhrātā svo mūrtirātmanaḥ
2.d: आचार्यो ब्रह्मणो मूर्तिः पिता मूर्तिः प्रजापतेः माता पृथिव्या मूर्तिस्तु भ्राता स्वो मूर्तिरात्मनः
2.e: The preceptor is the embodiment of Brahman; the father is the embodiment of Prajāpati; the Mother is the embodiment of the earth, and one’s own brother is the embodiment of the self.

2.s: yaṃ mātāpitarau kleśaṃ sahete saṃbhave nṛṇām na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi
2.d: यं मातापितरौ क्लेशं सहेते संभवे नृणाम् न तस्य निष्कृतिः शक्या कर्तुं वर्षशतैरपि
2.e: The trouble that the parents undergo in the birth of children,—for that there can be no compensation even in a hundred years.

2.s: tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryādācāryasya ca sarvadā teṣveva triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ sarvaṃ samāpyate
2.d: तयोर्नित्यं प्रियं कुर्यादाचार्यस्य च सर्वदा तेष्वेव त्रिषु तुष्टेषु तपः सर्वं समाप्यते
2.e: He should always do what is pleasing to those two and to the preceptor; on these three being satisfied, all austerity becomes completed.

2.s: teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate na tairanabhyanujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācaret
2.d: तेषां त्रयाणां शुश्रूषा परमं तप उच्यते न तैरनभ्यनुज्ञातो धर्ममन्यं समाचरेत्
2.e: The service of these three is declared to be the highest austerity; until permitted by them, one should not perform any other meritorious act.

2.s: ta eva hi trayo lokāsta eva traya āśramāḥ ta eva hi trayo vedāsta evauktāstrayo 'gnayaḥ
2.d: त एव हि त्रयो लोकास्त एव त्रय आश्रमाः त एव हि त्रयो वेदास्त एवौक्तास्त्रयो ऽग्नयः
2.e: These have been declared to be the three regions, these the three life-stages, these the three Vedas and these the three fires.

2.s: pitā vai gārhapatyo 'gnirmātā 'gnirdakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ gururāhavanīyastu sā 'gnitretā garīyasī
2.d: पिता वै गार्हपत्यो ऽग्निर्माता ऽग्निर्दक्षिणः स्मृतः गुरुराहवनीयस्तु सा ऽग्नित्रेता गरीयसी
2.e: The Father has been declared to be the Gārhapatya Fire, the Mother the Dakṣiṇa Fire, and the Preceptor the Āhavanīya fire; and this Triad of fires is highly important.

2.s: triṣvapramādyanneteṣu trīn lokān vijayedgṛhī dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā devavaddivi modate
2.d: त्रिष्वप्रमाद्यन्नेतेषु त्रीन् लोकान् विजयेद्गृही दीप्यमानः स्ववपुषा देववद्दिवि मोदते
2.e: The Householder who fails not towards these three would win the three regions, and rejoice in heaven, radiant in body, like a God.

2.s: imaṃ lokaṃ mātṛbhaktyā pitṛbhaktyā tu madhyamam guruśuśrūṣayā tvevaṃ brahmalokaṃ samaśnute
2.d: इमं लोकं मातृभक्त्या पितृभक्त्या तु मध्यमम् गुरुशुश्रूषया त्वेवं ब्रह्मलोकं समश्नुते
2.e: He acquires this region by devotion to his Mother, the middle region by devotion to his Father, and the region of Brahman by serving his Preceptor.

2.s: sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ anādṛtāstu yasyaite sarvāstasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ
2.d: सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः
2.e: All the duties have been honoured by him who has honoured these three; and all acts remain fruitless for him who does not honour them.

2.s: yāvat trayaste jīveyustāvatnānyaṃ samācaret teṣveva nityaṃ śuśrūṣāṃ kuryāt priyahite rataḥ
2.d: यावत् त्रयस्ते जीवेयुस्तावत्नान्यं समाचरेत् तेष्वेव नित्यं शुश्रूषां कुर्यात् प्रियहिते रतः
2.e: So long as these three live, he should not do anything else; he should always bender service unto them, rejoicing in what is pleasing and beneficial to them.

2.s: teṣāmanuparodhena pāratryaṃ yadyadācaret tat tannivedayet tebhyo manovacanakarmabhiḥ
2.d: तेषामनुपरोधेन पारत्र्यं यद्यदाचरेत् तत् तन्निवेदयेत् तेभ्यो मनोवचनकर्मभिः
2.e: He should communicate to them by thought, word or deed whatever he may do without injury to them, for the sake of the next life.

2.s: triṣveteṣvitikṛtyaṃ hi puruṣasya samāpyate eṣa dharmaḥ paraḥ sākṣādupadharmo 'nya ucyate
2.d: त्रिष्वेतेष्वितिकृत्यं हि पुरुषस्य समाप्यते एष धर्मः परः साक्षादुपधर्मो ऽन्य उच्यते
2.e: All that ought to be done by man is finished on these three; this is the highest direct duty; every other is a subordinate duty.

2.s: śraddadhānaḥ śubhāṃ vidyāmādadītāvarādapi anyādapi paraṃ dharmaṃ strīratnaṃ duṣkulādapi
2.d: श्रद्दधानः शुभां विद्यामाददीतावरादपि अन्यादपि परं धर्मं स्त्रीरत्नं दुष्कुलादपि
2.e: One imbued with faith may acquire excellent learning even from a lowly person, special law even from the lowest, and the gem of a wife even from a base family.

2.s: viṣādapyamṛtaṃ grāhyaṃ bālādapi subhāṣitam amitrādapi sadvṛttamamedhyādapi kāñcanam
2.d: विषादप्यमृतं ग्राह्यं बालादपि सुभाषितम् अमित्रादपि सद्वृत्तममेध्यादपि काञ्चनम्
2.e: Nectar mat be taken even from poison, good advice even prom a child; good conduct (may be learnt) even from a foe; and gold (mat be taken) even from an impure source.

2.s: striyo ratnānyatho vidyā dharmaḥ śaucaṃ subhāṣitam vividhāni ca śīlpāni samādeyāni sarvataḥ
2.d: स्त्रियो रत्नान्यथो विद्या धर्मः शौचं सुभाषितम् विविधानि च शील्पानि समादेयानि सर्वतः
2.e: Wives, gems, learning, virtue, purity, wise saying and the various arts may be obtained from all sources.

2.s: abrāhmaṇādadhyāyanamāpatkāle vidhīyate anuvrajyā ca śuśrūṣā yāvadadhyāyanaṃ guroḥ
2.d: अब्राह्मणादध्यायनमापत्काले विधीयते अनुव्रज्या च शुश्रूषा यावदध्यायनं गुरोः
2.e: In abnormal times of difficulty learning from a non-Brāhmaṇa has been enjoined, as also the serving of such a teacher, in the shape of following him, during the course of study.

2.s: nābrāhmaṇe gurau śiṣyo vāsamātyantikaṃ vaset brāhmaṇe vā 'nanūcāne kāṅkṣan gatimanuttamām
2.d: नाब्राह्मणे गुरौ शिष्यो वासमात्यन्तिकं वसेत् ब्राह्मणे वा ऽननूचाने काङ्क्षन् गतिमनुत्तमाम्
2.e: A pupil, desiring an unsurpassable state, shall not be in life-long residence with a non-Brāhhaṇa teacher; or with a Brāhmaṇa-teacher who is not an expounder.

2.s: yadi tvātyantikaṃ vāsaṃ rocayeta guroḥ kule yuktaḥ paricaredenamā śarīravimokṣaṇāt
2.d: यदि त्वात्यन्तिकं वासं रोचयेत गुरोः कुले युक्तः परिचरेदेनमा शरीरविमोक्षणात्
2.e: If one likes to live in life-long residence in the teacher’s house, he should, intently serve him till he becomes freed from his body.

2.s: ā samāpteḥ śarīrasya yastu śuśrūṣate gurum sa gacchatyañjasā vipro brahmaṇaḥ sadma śāśvatam
2.d: आ समाप्तेः शरीरस्य यस्तु शुश्रूषते गुरुम् स गच्छत्यञ्जसा विप्रो ब्रह्मणः सद्म शाश्वतम्
2.e: The Brāhmaṇa who, till the dissolution of his body, serves his teacher, goes forthwith to the eternal abode of brahman.

2.s: na pūrvaṃ gurave kiṃ cidupakurvīta dharmavit snāsyaṃstu guruṇā 'jñaptaḥ śaktyā guruarthamāharet
2.d: न पूर्वं गुरवे किं चिदुपकुर्वीत धर्मवित् स्नास्यंस्तु गुरुणा ऽज्ञप्तः शक्त्या गुरुअर्थमाहरेत्
2.e: At first the pupil, knowing his duties, should not give anything to his teacher; but when going to take the final bath, he should, on being ordered by the teacher, present something for him, to the best of his capacity;

2.s: kṣetraṃ hiraṇyaṃ gāmaśvaṃ chatraupānahamāsanam chatropānahamantataḥ dhānyaṃ śākaṃ ca vāsāṃsi gurave prītimāvahet dhānyaṃ vāsāṃsi śākaṃ vā gurave prītimāharan
2.d: क्षेत्रं हिरण्यं गामश्वं छत्रौपानहमासनम् छत्रोपानहमन्ततः धान्यं शाकं च वासांसि गुरवे प्रीतिमावहेत् धान्यं वासांसि शाकं वा गुरवे प्रीतिमाहरन्
2.e: Joyfully bringing to the teacher, a field, or gold, or a cow, or a horse, or at least an umbrella and a fair of shoes, grain, vegetables or clothes.

2.s: ācārye tu khalu prete guruputre guṇānvite gurudāre sapiṇḍe vā guruvadvṛttimācaret
2.d: आचार्ये तु खलु प्रेते गुरुपुत्रे गुणान्विते गुरुदारे सपिण्डे वा गुरुवद्वृत्तिमाचरेत्
2.e: The Preceptor having died, he should serve, in the same manner as the Preceptor, the qualified son of the Preceptor, or the Preceptor’s wife, or his Sapiṇḍa.

2.s: eteṣvavidyamāneṣu sthānāsanavihāravān prayuñjāno 'gniśuśrūṣāṃ sādhayeddehamātmanaḥ
2.d: एतेष्वविद्यमानेषु स्थानासनविहारवान् प्रयुञ्जानो ऽग्निशुश्रूषां साधयेद्देहमात्मनः
2.e: When all these are non-existent, he should perfect his body, while he carries on the tending of the Fire, with only such diversions as standing and sitting.

2.s: evaṃ carati yo vipro brahmacaryamaviplutaḥ sa gacchatyuttamasthānaṃ na caiha jāyate punaḥ
2.d: एवं चरति यो विप्रो ब्रह्मचर्यमविप्लुतः स गच्छत्युत्तमस्थानं न चैह जायते पुनः

3.s: ṣaṭtriṃśadābdikaṃ caryaṃ gurau traivedikaṃ vratam tadardhikaṃ pādikaṃ vā grahaṇāntikameva vā
3.d: षट्त्रिंशदाब्दिकं चर्यं गुरौ त्रैवेदिकं व्रतम् तदर्धिकं पादिकं वा ग्रहणान्तिकमेव वा
3.e: Duties relating to the Three Vedas should be observed under the Preceptor for thirty-six years, or for half that period, or for a quarter, or precisely till they have been got up.

3.s: vedānadhītya vedau vā vedaṃ vā 'pi yathākramam aviplutabrahmacaryo gṛhasthāśramamāvaset
3.d: वेदानधीत्य वेदौ वा वेदं वा ऽपि यथाक्रमम् अविप्लुतब्रह्मचर्यो गृहस्थाश्रममावसेत्
3.e: Having learnt, in due course, three Vedas, or two Vedas, or one Veda, he should enter upon the state of the householder, having never deviated from the vows of studentship.

3.s: taṃ pratītaṃ svadharmeṇa brahmadāyaharaṃ pituḥ sragviṇaṃ talpa āsīnamarhayet prathamaṃ gavā
3.d: तं प्रतीतं स्वधर्मेण ब्रह्मदायहरं पितुः स्रग्विणं तल्प आसीनमर्हयेत् प्रथमं गवा
3.e: When, by the due observance of his duties, he has acquired the Veda and his heritage from his father, and is so inclined,—his father shall first honour him, adorned with garlands and seated upon a couch, with the “Cow.”

3.s: guruṇānumataḥ snātvā samāvṛtto yathāvidhi udvaheta dvijo bhāryāṃ savarṇāṃ lakṣaṇānvitām
3.d: गुरुणानुमतः स्नात्वा समावृत्तो यथाविधि उद्वहेत द्विजो भार्यां सवर्णां लक्षणान्विताम्
3.e: The twice-born person, having, on being permitted by the Preceptor, “bathed” and “returned” according to rule, shall take a wife of the same caste as himself, who is endowed with signs.

3.s: asapiṇḍā ca yā māturasagotrā ca yā pituḥ sā praśastā dvijātīnāṃ dārakarmaṇi maithune 'maithinī
3.d: असपिण्डा च या मातुरसगोत्रा च या पितुः सा प्रशस्ता द्विजातीनां दारकर्मणि मैथुने ऽमैथिनी
3.e: She who is not a “sapiṇḍa” of one’s mother, not of the same “Gotra” as his Father, and who is not born of (unlawful) intercourse—has been recommended for marriage.

3.s: mahāntyapi samṛddhāni go 'jāvidhanadhānyataḥ strīsaṃbandhe daśaitāni kulāni parivarjayet
3.d: महान्त्यपि समृद्धानि गो ऽजाविधनधान्यतः स्त्रीसंबन्धे दशैतानि कुलानि परिवर्जयेत्
3.e: In female connection one should avoid these (following) ten families,—even though they be great and rich in the possession of cattle, goat and sheep and grain.

3.s: hīnakriyaṃ niṣpuruṣaṃ niśchando romaśārśasam kṣayāmayāvy 'pasmāriśvitrikuṣṭhikulāni ca
3.d: हीनक्रियं निष्पुरुषं निश्छन्दो रोमशार्शसम् क्षयामयाव्य् ऽपस्मारिश्वित्रिकुष्ठिकुलानि च
3.e: Such families as—(1) that in which the sacred rites have been abandoned, (2) which is male-less, (3) which is devoid of the Veda, (4) members of which are woolly and subject to (5) piles, (6) phthisis, (7) dyspepsia, (8) epilepsy, (9) leucoderma, and (10) leprosy.

3.s: naudvahet kapilāṃ kanyāṃ nādhikāṅgīṃ na rogiṇīm nālomikāṃ nātilomāṃ na vācāṭāṃ na piṅgalām vācālāṃ
3.d: नौद्वहेत् कपिलां कन्यां नाधिकाङ्गीं न रोगिणीम् नालोमिकां नातिलोमां न वाचाटां न पिङ्गलाम् वाचालां
3.e: He should hot marry a maiden with tawny hair, nor one with superfluous limbs, nor one who has disease, nor one who has either no hair or too much hair, nor one who is garrulous, nor one with reddish eyes.

3.s: naṛkṣavṛkṣanadīnāmnīṃ nāntyaparvatanāmikām na pakṣiahipreṣyanāmnīṃ na ca bhīṣananāmikām
3.d: नऋक्षवृक्षनदीनाम्नीं नान्त्यपर्वतनामिकाम् न पक्षिअहिप्रेष्यनाम्नीं न च भीषननामिकाम्
3.e: Nor one bearing the name of an asterism, or a tree, or a river; nob one having her hame after a low caste or a mountain; nor one named after a bird, a serpent or a slave; nor one with a hame inspiring terror.

3.s: avyaṅgāṅgīṃ saumyanāmnīṃ haṃsavāraṇagāminīm tanulomakeśadaśanāṃ mṛdv 'ṅgīmudvahet striyam
3.d: अव्यङ्गाङ्गीं सौम्यनाम्नीं हंसवारणगामिनीम् तनुलोमकेशदशनां मृद्व् ऽङ्गीमुद्वहेत् स्त्रियम्
3.e: One should marry a female with a faultless body, bearing an agreeable name, having her gait like that of the swan or the elephant, having fine hair on the body and the head, and fine teeth, and with tender limbs.

3.s: yasyāstu na bhavedbhrātā na vijñāyeta vā pitā vai(vā pitā naupayaccheta tāṃ prājñaḥ putrikā 'dharmaśaṅkayā
3.d: यस्यास्तु न भवेद्भ्राता न विज्ञायेत वा पिता वै(वा पिता नौपयच्छेत तां प्राज्ञः पुत्रिका ऽधर्मशङ्कया
3.e: The wise man shall not mabry one who has no brother, or whose father is not known; for fear of her having the character of the “appointed daughter.”

3.s: savarṇā 'gre dvijātīnāṃ praśastā dārakarmaṇi kāmatastu pravṛttānāmimāḥ syuḥ kramaśo 'varāḥ
3.d: सवर्णा ऽग्रे द्विजातीनां प्रशस्ता दारकर्मणि कामतस्तु प्रवृत्तानामिमाः स्युः क्रमशो ऽवराः
3.e: For ‘twice-born men’ a girl of equal caste has been recommended for the first marriage-sacrament. For those, however, who take to it through mere desire, these (following) should be regarded as preferable in due order.

3.s: śūdraiva bhāryā śūdrasya sā ca svā ca viśaḥ smṛte te ca svā caiva rājñaśca tāśca svā cāgrajanmanaḥ
3.d: शूद्रैव भार्या शूद्रस्य सा च स्वा च विशः स्मृते ते च स्वा चैव राज्ञश्च ताश्च स्वा चाग्रजन्मनः
3.e: For the Śūdra, the Śūdra girl. alone has been ordained to be the wife; for the Vaiśya, she as also the girl of his own caste; for the Kṣatriya, those two as also the girl of his own caste; and for the Brāhmaṇa those three as also the girl of his own caste

3.s: na brāhmaṇakṣatriyayorāpadyapi hi tiṣṭhatoḥ kasmiṃścidapi vṛttānte śūdrā bhāryaupadiśyate
3.d: न ब्राह्मणक्षत्रिययोरापद्यपि हि तिष्ठतोः कस्मिंश्चिदपि वृत्तान्ते शूद्रा भार्यौपदिश्यते
3.e: Under no circumstance whatsoever has a Śūdra wife been ordained for the Brāhmaṇa and the Kṣatriya,—even though these be placed in peril.

3.s: hīnajātistriyaṃ mohādudvahanto dvijātayaḥ kulānyeva nayantyāśu sasantānāni śūdratām
3.d: हीनजातिस्त्रियं मोहादुद्वहन्तो द्विजातयः कुलान्येव नयन्त्याशु ससन्तानानि शूद्रताम्
3.e: Twice-born men, marrying, through infatuation, a girl of the low caste, quickly reduce their families, along with their offspring, to the position of the Śūdra.

3.s: śūdrāvedī patatyatrerutathyatanayasya ca śaunakasya sutautpattyā tadapatyatayā bhṛgoḥ
3.d: शूद्रावेदी पतत्यत्रेरुतथ्यतनयस्य च शौनकस्य सुतौत्पत्त्या तदपत्यतया भृगोः
3.e: One who marries a Śūdra girl becomes an outcastk,—according to atri and to the son of Utathya; according to Śaunaka, by the birth of a son; and according to Bhṛgu, by having children from her (alone).

3.s: śūdrāṃ śayanamāropya brāhmaṇo yātyadhogatim janayitvā sutaṃ tasyāṃ brāhmaṇyādeva hīyate
3.d: शूद्रां शयनमारोप्य ब्राह्मणो यात्यधोगतिम् जनयित्वा सुतं तस्यां ब्राह्मण्यादेव हीयते
3.e: Having placed a Śūdrā woman on his bed, the Brāhmaṇa goes to perdition; and having begotten a son by her, he falls from Brāhmaṇahood itself.

3.s: daivapitryātitheyāni tatpradhānāni yasya tu nāśnanti pitṛdevāstanna ca svargaṃ sa gacchati
3.d: दैवपित्र्यातिथेयानि तत्प्रधानानि यस्य तु नाश्नन्ति पितृदेवास्तन्न च स्वर्गं स गच्छति
3.e: If the rites performed by one in honour of deities, Pitṛs and Guests are dominated by her (his Śūdra wife), then the Pitṛs and the Gods do not eat of them; and the man does not go to heaven.

3.s: vṛṣalīphenapītasya niḥśvāsaupahatasya ca tasyāṃ caiva prasūtasya niṣkṛtirna vidhīyate
3.d: वृषलीफेनपीतस्य निःश्वासौपहतस्य च तस्यां चैव प्रसूतस्य निष्कृतिर्न विधीयते
3.e: There is ho expiation for him who has drunk the moisture of the mouth of a Śūdra woman, who has been tainted by her breath, and who has begotten children on her.

3.s: caturṇāmapi varṇānaṃ pretya caiha hitāhitān aṣṭāvimān samāsena strīvivāhānnibodhata
3.d: चतुर्णामपि वर्णानं प्रेत्य चैह हिताहितान् अष्टाविमान् समासेन स्त्रीविवाहान्निबोधत
3.e: Understand briefly these (following) eight forms of marriage of girls, among the four castes,—which are beneficial and not-beneficial here (in this life) and also after death.

3.s: brāhmo daivastathaivārṣaḥ prājāpatyastathā 'suraḥ gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva paiśācaścāṣṭamo 'dhamaḥ
3.d: ब्राह्मो दैवस्तथैवार्षः प्राजापत्यस्तथा ऽसुरः गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव पैशाचश्चाष्टमो ऽधमः
3.e: (1) The Brāhma, (2) the Daiva, (3) the Ārṣa, (1) the Prājāpatya, (5) the Āsura, (6) the Gāndharva, (7) the Rākṣasa and (8) the Paiśāca, which is the eighth and the lowest.

3.s: yo yasya dharmyo varṇasya guṇadoṣau ca yasya yau tadvaḥ sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi prasave ca guṇāguṇān
3.d: यो यस्य धर्म्यो वर्णस्य गुणदोषौ च यस्य यौ तद्वः सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रसवे च गुणागुणान्
3.e: Which (of these) is lawful for which caste, what are the good and bad points of each, the good and bad effects of each upon the offspring,—all this I shall explain to you.

3.s: ṣaḍānupūrvyā viprasya kṣatrasya caturo 'varān viśśūdrayostu tāneva vidyāddharmyānarākṣasān dharmyānna rākṣasān
3.d: षडानुपूर्व्या विप्रस्य क्षत्रस्य चतुरो ऽवरान् विश्शूद्रयोस्तु तानेव विद्याद्धर्म्यानराक्षसान् धर्म्यान्न राक्षसान्
3.e: One should know the first six in the order stated as lawful for the Brāhmaṇa, the last four for the Kṣatriya and those same, excepting the “Rākṣasa,” for the Vaiśya and the Śūdra.

3.s: caturo brāhmaṇasyādyān praśastān kavayo viduḥ rākṣasaṃ kṣatriyasyaikamāsuraṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ
3.d: चतुरो ब्राह्मणस्याद्यान् प्रशस्तान् कवयो विदुः राक्षसं क्षत्रियस्यैकमासुरं वैश्यशूद्रयोः
3.e: The wise ones have regarded the first four as commended for the Brāhmaṇa, the Rākṣasa alone for the Kṣatriya and the Āsura for the Vaiśva and the Śūdra.

3.s: pañcānāṃ tu trayo dharmyā dvāvadharmyau smṛtāviha paiśācaścāsuraścaiva na kartavyau kadā cana
3.d: पञ्चानां तु त्रयो धर्म्या द्वावधर्म्यौ स्मृताविह पैशाचश्चासुरश्चैव न कर्तव्यौ कदा चन
3.e: Of the five, three have been declared to be lawful and two unlawful, in this treatise; the Paiśāca and the Āsura forms should never be adopted.’

3.s: pṛthak pṛthag vā miśrau vā vivāhau pūrvacoditau gāndharvo rākṣasaścaiva dharmyau kṣatrasya tau smṛtau
3.d: पृथक् पृथग् वा मिश्रौ वा विवाहौ पूर्वचोदितौ गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव धर्म्यौ क्षत्रस्य तौ स्मृतौ
3.e: The two forms of marriage mentioned before—i.e., the Gāndharva and the Rākṣasa—have been declared, whether separately or mixed, to be lawful for the Kṣatriya.

3.s: ācchādya cārcayitvā ca śrutaśīlavate svayam āhūya dānaṃ kanyāyā brāhmo dharmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
3.d: आच्छाद्य चार्चयित्वा च श्रुतशीलवते स्वयम् आहूय दानं कन्याया ब्राह्मो धर्मः प्रकीर्तितः
3.e: When one himself invites a man endowed with learning and character and gives to him his daughter, after having dressed and worshipped (them),—this is called the “Brāhma” form.

3.s: yajñe tu vitate samyag ṛtvije karma kurvate alaṅkṛtya sutādānaṃ daivaṃ dharmaṃ pracakṣate
3.d: यज्ञे तु वितते सम्यग् ऋत्विजे कर्म कुर्वते अलङ्कृत्य सुतादानं दैवं धर्मं प्रचक्षते
3.e: While a sacrifice is being performed, if one gives away his daughter, after having decked her, to the priest who is officiating at it,—this they call the “Daiva” form.

3.s: ekaṃ gomithunaṃ dve vā varādādāya dharmataḥ kanyāpradānaṃ vidhivadārṣo dharmaḥ sa ucyate
3.d: एकं गोमिथुनं द्वे वा वरादादाय धर्मतः कन्याप्रदानं विधिवदार्षो धर्मः स उच्यते
3.e: ‘When the maiden is given away in due accordance with rule, after taking, in odedience to law, from the bridegroom, one or two pairs of cow and bull,—this is called the “Ārṣa” form.’

3.s: sahaubhau caratāṃ dharmamiti vācā 'nubhāṣya ca kanyāpradānamabhyarcya prājāpatyo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
3.d: सहौभौ चरतां धर्ममिति वाचा ऽनुभाष्य च कन्याप्रदानमभ्यर्च्य प्राजापत्यो विधिः स्मृतः
3.e: When the Father, having decked them, gives away the daughter with the words, “may you both together perform your duty,” making them also repeat them,—this is called the “Prājāpatya” form.

3.s: jñātibhyo draviṇaṃ dattvā kanyāyai caiva śaktitaḥ kanyāpradānaṃ svācchandyādāsuro dharma ucyate
3.d: ज्ञातिभ्यो द्रविणं दत्त्वा कन्यायै चैव शक्तितः कन्याप्रदानं स्वाच्छन्द्यादासुरो धर्म उच्यते
3.e: When one carries away the maiden, after having given, of his own will, as much wealth as the (he?) can to the kinsmen, as well as to the bride herself, this is called the “Āsura” form.

3.s: icchayā 'nyonyasaṃyogaḥ kanyāyāśca varasya ca gāndharvaḥ sa tu vijñeyo maithunyaḥ kāmasaṃbhavaḥ
3.d: इच्छया ऽन्योन्यसंयोगः कन्यायाश्च वरस्य च गान्धर्वः स तु विज्ञेयो मैथुन्यः कामसंभवः
3.e: The mutual union of the bride and bridegroom, through love is to be known as the “Gāndharva” form; it has sexual intercourse for its end and it has its source in lust.

3.s: hatvā chittvā ca bhittvā ca krośantīṃ rudantīṃ gṛhāt prasahya kanyāharaṇaṃ rākṣaso vidhirucyate
3.d: हत्वा छित्त्वा च भित्त्वा च क्रोशन्तीं रुदन्तीं गृहात् प्रसह्य कन्याहरणं राक्षसो विधिरुच्यते
3.e: The forcible abduction of the maiden from her home, while she is crying out and weeping, after having beaten and wounded and pierced,—is called the “Rākṣasa” form.

3.s: suptāṃ mattāṃ pramattāṃ vā raho yatraupagacchati sa pāpiṣṭho vivāhānāṃ paiśācaścāṣṭamo 'dhamaḥ paiśācaḥ prathito 'dhamaḥ
3.d: सुप्तां मत्तां प्रमत्तां वा रहो यत्रौपगच्छति स पापिष्ठो विवाहानां पैशाचश्चाष्टमो ऽधमः पैशाचः प्रथितो ऽधमः
3.e: When the man approaches the girl by stealth, while she is asleep, or intoxicated or unconscious,—it is the “Paiśāca” form, the wickedest and the basest of marriages.

3.s: adbhireva dvijāgryāṇāṃ kanyādānaṃ viśiṣyate itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāmitaretarakāmyayā
3.d: अद्भिरेव द्विजाग्र्याणां कन्यादानं विशिष्यते इतरेषां तु वर्णानामितरेतरकाम्यया
3.e: ‘For the chief of twice-born men the giving away of one’s daughter with water alone is commended; but for the other castes it is with mutual desire.’

3.s: yo yasyaiṣāṃ vivāhānāṃ manunā kīrtito guṇaḥ sarvaṃ śṛṇuta taṃ viprāḥ sarvaṃ kīrtayato mama samyak kīrtayato
3.d: यो यस्यैषां विवाहानां मनुना कीर्तितो गुणः सर्वं शृणुत तं विप्राः सर्वं कीर्तयतो मम सम्यक् कीर्तयतो
3.e: The quality that has been ascribed by Manu to each of these forms of marriage—listen to all that, O Brāhmaṇas, from me, as I proceed to describe them correctly.

3.s: daśa pūrvān parān vaṃśyānātmānaṃ caikaviṃśakam brāhmīputraḥ sukṛtakṛtmocayatyenasaḥ pitr̥̄n
3.d: दश पूर्वान् परान् वंश्यानात्मानं चैकविंशकम् ब्राह्मीपुत्रः सुकृतकृत्मोचयत्येनसः पित्र्̥̄न्
3.e: The son born of the wife married by the Brāhma form is a performer of righteous acts, absolves from sins ten Pitṛs on the ascending side and ten on the descending side of his family, as also himself as the twenty-first.

3.s: daivauḍhājaḥ sutaścaiva sapta sapta parāvarān ārṣauḍhājaḥ sutastrīṃstrīn ṣaṭ ṣaṭ kāyauḍhajaḥ sutaḥ
3.d: दैवौढाजः सुतश्चैव सप्त सप्त परावरान् आर्षौढाजः सुतस्त्रींस्त्रीन् षट् षट् कायौढजः सुतः
3.e: The son born of the wife married by the Daiva form (absolves from sin) seven ancestors and seven des cendants; the son born of the wife married by the Ārṣa form three of each; and the son born of the wife married by the Prājāpatya form six of each.

3.s: brāhmādiṣu vivāheṣu caturṣvevānupūrvaśaḥ brahmavarcasvinaḥ putrā jāyante śiṣṭasammatāḥ brahmavarcasinaḥ
3.d: ब्राह्मादिषु विवाहेषु चतुर्ष्वेवानुपूर्वशः ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनः पुत्रा जायन्ते शिष्टसम्मताः ब्रह्मवर्चसिनः
3.e: Only from the four marriages mentioned successively, beginning with the Brāhma, are born sons endowed with Brahmic glory and respected by cultured persons.

3.s: rūpasattvaguṇaupetā dhanavanto yaśasvinaḥ paryāptabhogā dharmiṣṭhā jīvanti ca śataṃ samāḥ
3.d: रूपसत्त्वगुणौपेता धनवन्तो यशस्विनः पर्याप्तभोगा धर्मिष्ठा जीवन्ति च शतं समाः
3.e: Endowed with beauty and the quality of goodness, possessing wealth, and fame, with full enjoyment and righteous, they live for a hundred years.

3.s: itareṣu tu śiṣṭeṣu nṛśaṃsā 'nṛtavādinaḥ jāyante durvivāheṣu brahmadharmadviṣaḥ sutāḥ
3.d: इतरेषु तु शिष्टेषु नृशंसा ऽनृतवादिनः जायन्ते दुर्विवाहेषु ब्रह्मधर्मद्विषः सुताः
3.e: From the other remaining inferior marriages are born sons, addicted to saying harsh and untrue words, and despisers of the Vedic Dharma.

3.s: aninditaiḥ strīvivāhairanindyā bhavati prajā ninditairninditā nr̥̄ṇāṃ tasmānnindyān vivarjayet
3.d: अनिन्दितैः स्त्रीविवाहैरनिन्द्या भवति प्रजा निन्दितैर्निन्दिता न्र्̥̄णां तस्मान्निन्द्यान् विवर्जयेत्
3.e: From unblamable marriages unblamable offspring is born to men; and from blameworthy marriages blameworthy child. One should therefore avoid the blamable marriages.

3.s: pāṇigrahaṇasaṃskāraḥ savarṇāsūpadiśyate asavarṇāsvayaṃ jñeyo vidhirudvāhakarmaṇi
3.d: पाणिग्रहणसंस्कारः सवर्णासूपदिश्यते असवर्णास्वयं ज्ञेयो विधिरुद्वाहकर्मणि
3.e: In the case of girls of the same caste (as the bridegroom) the sacramental rite of “taking the hand” has been prescribed; and in that of the marriage of girls of different castes, this (following) should be known as the right procedure.

3.s: śaraḥ kṣatriyayā grāhyaḥ pratodo vaiśyakanyayā vasanasya daśā grāhyā śūdrayautkṛṣṭavedane
3.d: शरः क्षत्रियया ग्राह्यः प्रतोदो वैश्यकन्यया वसनस्य दशा ग्राह्या शूद्रयौत्कृष्टवेदने
3.e: When being married to a man of higher caste, the Kṣatriya girl should take hold of the arrow, the Vaiśya girl of the goad and the Śūdra girl of the hem of the garment.

3.s: ṛtukālābhigāmī syāt svadāranirataḥ sadā parvavarjaṃ vrajeccaināṃ tadvrato ratikāmyayā
3.d: ऋतुकालाभिगामी स्यात् स्वदारनिरतः सदा पर्ववर्जं व्रजेच्चैनां तद्व्रतो रतिकाम्यया
3.e: One should observe the rule of approaching (one’s wife) during the period of her season,—ever attached to his own wife. In consideration of her he may approach her with a desire for sexual intercourse, except on the sacred days.

3.s: ṛtuḥ svābhāvikaḥ strīṇāṃ rātrayaḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ caturbhiritaraiḥ sārdhamahobhiḥ sadvigarhitaiḥ
3.d: ऋतुः स्वाभाविकः स्त्रीणां रात्रयः षोडश स्मृताः चतुर्भिरितरैः सार्धमहोभिः सद्विगर्हितैः
3.e: Sixteen days, including the four days that are censured by good men, have been declared to be the normal “season” for women.

3.s: tāsāmādyāścatasrastu ninditaikādaśī ca yā trayodaśī ca śeṣāstu praśastā daśarātrayaḥ
3.d: तासामाद्याश्चतस्रस्तु निन्दितैकादशी च या त्रयोदशी च शेषास्तु प्रशस्ता दशरात्रयः
3.e: Of these the first four days have been deprecated, as also the eleventh and the thirteenth, the remaining ten days have been recommended.

3.s: yugmāsu putrā jāyante striyo 'yugmāsu rātriṣu tasmādyugmāsu putrārthī saṃviśedārtave striyam
3.d: युग्मासु पुत्रा जायन्ते स्त्रियो ऽयुग्मासु रात्रिषु तस्माद्युग्मासु पुत्रार्थी संविशेदार्तवे स्त्रियम्
3.e: On the even days male children are conceived, and female ones on the uneven days; therefore one who desires a son should have recourse to ones wife on the even days of her “season.”

3.s: pumān puṃso 'dhike śukre strī bhavatyadhike striyāḥ same 'pumān puṃstriyau vā kṣīṇe 'lpe ca viparyayaḥ
3.d: पुमान् पुंसो ऽधिके शुक्रे स्त्री भवत्यधिके स्त्रियाः समे ऽपुमान् पुंस्त्रियौ वा क्षीणे ऽल्पे च विपर्ययः
3.e: A male child is born when the man’s seed is in excess, and a female child when the woman’s (is in excess); when the two are equal, there is born either a non-male or a boy and a girl; when it is weak and small in quantity, there is failure.

3.s: nindyāsvaṣṭāsu cānyāsu striyo rātriṣu varjayan brahmacāryeva bhavati yatra tatrāśrame vasan
3.d: निन्द्यास्वष्टासु चान्यासु स्त्रियो रात्रिषु वर्जयन् ब्रह्मचार्येव भवति यत्र तत्राश्रमे वसन्
3.e: ‘By avoiding women on the forbidden days and also on the eight other days, one remains a “religious student” (observing the vow of continence), in whatever stage of life he may happen to be.”

3.s: na kanyāyāḥ pitā vidvān gṛhṇīyātśulkamaṇuapi gṛhṇaṃśulkaṃ hi lobhena syānnaro 'patyavikrayī
3.d: न कन्यायाः पिता विद्वान् गृह्णीयात्शुल्कमणुअपि गृह्णंशुल्कं हि लोभेन स्यान्नरो ऽपत्यविक्रयी
3.e: The girl’s father, if wise, should not accept even a small consideration; by accepting a consideration, through greed, the man becomes a child-seller.

3.s: strīdhanāni tu ye mohādupajīvanti bāndhavāḥ nārī yānāni vastraṃ vā te pāpā yāntyadhogatim
3.d: स्त्रीधनानि तु ये मोहादुपजीवन्ति बान्धवाः नारी यानानि वस्त्रं वा ते पापा यान्त्यधोगतिम्
3.e: Those relations who, through folly, live upon the bride’s properties—even the bride’s conveyances and clothes—are sinners and fall into the lowest state.

3.s: ārṣe gomithunaṃ śulkaṃ ke cidāhurmṛṣaiva tat alpo 'pyevaṃ mahān vā 'pi vikrayastāvadeva saḥ tāvāneva sa vikrayaḥ
3.d: आर्षे गोमिथुनं शुल्कं के चिदाहुर्मृषैव तत् अल्पो ऽप्येवं महान् वा ऽपि विक्रयस्तावदेव सः तावानेव स विक्रयः
3.e: Some people declare that the bovine pair are the “consideration” (to be accepted) in the Ārṣa form of marriage. This is not true; for small or large, the act becomes a ‘selling’ all the same.

3.s: yāsāṃ nādadate śulkaṃ jñātayo na sa vikrayaḥ arhaṇaṃ tat kumārīṇāmānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca kevalam na kevalam
3.d: यासां नाददते शुल्कं ज्ञातयो न स विक्रयः अर्हणं तत् कुमारीणामानृशंस्यं च केवलम् न केवलम्
3.e: In the case of girls whose relations do not appropriate the bride’s gift, it is not “selling;” It is only a means of honouring the maidens and is entirely harmless.

3.s: pitṛbhirbhrātṛbhiścaitāḥ patibhirdevaraistathā pūjyā bhūṣayitavyāśca bahukalyāṇamīpsubhiḥ
3.d: पितृभिर्भ्रातृभिश्चैताः पतिभिर्देवरैस्तथा पूज्या भूषयितव्याश्च बहुकल्याणमीप्सुभिः
3.e: These shall be honoured and adorned by their fathers and brothers, husbands and brothers-in-law, who are desirous of their own welfare.

3.s: yatra nāryastu pūjyante ramante tatra devatāḥ yatraitāstu na pūjyante sarvāstatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ
3.d: यत्र नार्यस्तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः यत्रैतास्तु न पूज्यन्ते सर्वास्तत्राफलाः क्रियाः
3.e: Where women are honoured, there the gods rejoice; where, on the other hand, they are not honoured, there all rites are fruitless.

3.s: śocanti jāmayo yatra vinaśyatyāśu tat kulam na śocanti tu yatraitā vardhate taddhi sarvadā
3.d: शोचन्ति जामयो यत्र विनश्यत्याशु तत् कुलम् न शोचन्ति तु यत्रैता वर्धते तद्धि सर्वदा
3.e: Where the female relations live in grief, the family soon wholly perishes; but that family where they are not unhappy ever prospers.

3.s: jāmayo yāni gehāni śapantyapratipūjitāḥ tāni kṛtyāhatānīva vinaśyanti samantataḥ
3.d: जामयो यानि गेहानि शपन्त्यप्रतिपूजिताः तानि कृत्याहतानीव विनश्यन्ति समन्ततः
3.e: The houses on which female relations, not being duly honoured, pronounce a curse, perish completely, as if destroyed by magic.

3.s: tasmādetāḥ sadā pūjyā bhūṣaṇācchādanāśanaiḥ bhūtikāmairnarairnityaṃ satkareṣūtsaveṣu ca
3.d: तस्मादेताः सदा पूज्या भूषणाच्छादनाशनैः भूतिकामैर्नरैर्नित्यं सत्करेषूत्सवेषु च
3.e: Hence men who seek (their own) welfare, should always honour women on holidays and festivals with (gifts of) ornaments, clothes, and (dainty) food.

3.s: saṃtuṣṭo bhāryayā bhartā bhartrā bhāryā tathaiva ca yasminneva kule nityaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tatra vai dhruvam
3.d: संतुष्टो भार्यया भर्ता भर्त्रा भार्या तथैव च यस्मिन्नेव कुले नित्यं कल्याणं तत्र वै ध्रुवम्
3.e: In that family, where the husband is pleased with his wife and the wife with her husband, happiness will assuredly be lasting.

3.s: yadi hi strī na roceta pumāṃsaṃ na pramodayet apramodāt punaḥ puṃsaḥ prajanaṃ na pravartate
3.d: यदि हि स्त्री न रोचेत पुमांसं न प्रमोदयेत् अप्रमोदात् पुनः पुंसः प्रजनं न प्रवर्तते
3.e: For if the wife is not radiant with beauty, she will not attract her husband; but if she has no attractions for him, no children will be born.

3.s: striyāṃ tu rocamānāyāṃ sarvaṃ tadrocate kulam tasyāṃ tvarocamānāyāṃ sarvameva na rocate
3.d: स्त्रियां तु रोचमानायां सर्वं तद्रोचते कुलम् तस्यां त्वरोचमानायां सर्वमेव न रोचते
3.e: If the wife is radiant with beauty, the whole house is bright; but if she is destitute of beauty, all will appear dismal.

3.s: kuvivāhaiḥ kriyālopairvedānadhyayanena ca kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca
3.d: कुविवाहैः क्रियालोपैर्वेदानध्ययनेन च कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च
3.e: By low marriages, by omitting (the performance of) sacred rites, by neglecting the study of the Veda, and by irreverence towards Brahmanas, (great) families sink low.

3.s: śilpena vyavahāreṇa śūdrāpatyaiśca kevalaiḥ gobhiraśvaiśca yānaiśca kṛṣyā rājaupasevayā
3.d: शिल्पेन व्यवहारेण शूद्रापत्यैश्च केवलैः गोभिरश्वैश्च यानैश्च कृष्या राजौपसेवया
3.e: By (practising) handicrafts, by pecuniary transactions, by (begetting) children on Sudra females only, by (trading in) cows, horses, and carriages, by (the pursuit of) agriculture and by taking service under a king.

3.s: ayājyayājanaiścaiva nāstikyena ca karmaṇām kulānyāśu vinaśyanti yāni hīnāni mantrataḥ
3.d: अयाज्ययाजनैश्चैव नास्तिक्येन च कर्मणाम् कुलान्याशु विनश्यन्ति यानि हीनानि मन्त्रतः
3.e: By sacrificing for men unworthy to offer sacrifices and by denying (the future rewards for good) works, families, deficient in the (knowledge of the) Veda, quickly perish.

3.s: mantratastu samṛddhāni kulānyalpadhanānyapi kulasaṅkhyāṃ ca gacchanti karṣanti ca mahadyaśaḥ
3.d: मन्त्रतस्तु समृद्धानि कुलान्यल्पधनान्यपि कुलसङ्ख्यां च गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च महद्यशः
3.e: But families that are rich in the knowledge of the Veda, though possessing little wealth, are numbered among the great, and acquire great fame.

3.s: vaivāhike 'gnau kurvīta gṛhyaṃ karma yathāvidhi pañcayajñavidhānaṃ ca paktiṃ cānvāhikīṃ gṛhī
3.d: वैवाहिके ऽग्नौ कुर्वीत गृह्यं कर्म यथाविधि पञ्चयज्ञविधानं च पक्तिं चान्वाहिकीं गृही
3.e: In the marriage-fire the householder should perform the ‘gṛhya’ rites; as also the rite of the ‘five sacrifices’ and the daily cooking.

3.s: pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya cullī peṣaṇyupaskaraḥ kaṇḍanī caudakumbhaśca badhyate yāstu vāhayan vadhyate
3.d: पञ्च सूना गृहस्थस्य चुल्ली पेषण्युपस्करः कण्डनी चौदकुम्भश्च बध्यते यास्तु वाहयन् वध्यते
3.e: For the householder there are five slaughter-houses: the hearth, the grinding-stone, household implements, mortar and pestle and water-jar;—by using which he becomes stricken.

3.s: tāsāṃ krameṇa sarvāsāṃ niṣkṛtyarthaṃ maharṣibhiḥ pañca kḷptā mahāyajñāḥ pratyahaṃ gṛhamedhinām
3.d: तासां क्रमेण सर्वासां निष्कृत्यर्थं महर्षिभिः पञ्च कॢप्ता महायज्ञाः प्रत्यहं गृहमेधिनाम्
3.e: For the purpose of expiating all these in their course, the five great sacrifices have been ordained by the great sages, for householders (to be performed) daily.

3.s: adhyāpanaṃ brahmayajñaḥ pitṛyajñastu tarpaṇam homo daivo balirbhauto nṛyajño 'tithipūjanam
3.d: अध्यापनं ब्रह्मयज्ञः पितृयज्ञस्तु तर्पणम् होमो दैवो बलिर्भौतो नृयज्ञो ऽतिथिपूजनम्
3.e: Teaching is the ‘offering to Brahma;’ the Tarpaṇa is the ‘offering to Pitṛs;’ the Homa is ‘offering to Gods;’ the Bali is ‘offering to elementals;’ and the honouring of Guests is ‘offering to men.’

3.s: pañcaitān yo mahā 'yajñānna hāpayati śaktitaḥ sa gṛhe 'pi vasannityaṃ sūnādoṣairna lipyate
3.d: पञ्चैतान् यो महा ऽयज्ञान्न हापयति शक्तितः स गृहे ऽपि वसन्नित्यं सूनादोषैर्न लिप्यते
3.e: He who omits not these sacrifices, to the best of his capacity, on any day, does not become tainted by the sin of the ‘slaughter-house,’ even though living in the house.

3.s: devatā 'tithibhṛtyānāṃ pitr̥̄ṇāmātmanaśca yaḥ na nirvapati pañcānāmucchvasanna sa jīvati
3.d: देवता ऽतिथिभृत्यानां पित्र्̥̄णामात्मनश्च यः न निर्वपति पञ्चानामुच्छ्वसन्न स जीवति
3.e: He who does not make offerings to the five—viz., gods, guests, dependents, Pitṛs and himself,—does not live, even though breathing.

3.s: ahutaṃ ca hutaṃ caiva tathā prahutameva ca brāhmyaṃ hutaṃ prāśitaṃ ca pañcayajñān pracakṣate
3.d: अहुतं च हुतं चैव तथा प्रहुतमेव च ब्राह्म्यं हुतं प्राशितं च पञ्चयज्ञान् प्रचक्षते
3.e: ‘They also call these five sacrifices—(1) “Ahuta,” (2) “Huta,” (3) “Prahuta,” (4) “Brāhmya-huta,” and (5) “Prāśita.”’

3.s: japo 'huto huto homaḥ prahuto bhautiko baliḥ brāhmyaṃ hutaṃ dvijāgryārcā prāśitaṃ pitṛtarpaṇam
3.d: जपो ऽहुतो हुतो होमः प्रहुतो भौतिको बलिः ब्राह्म्यं हुतं द्विजाग्र्यार्चा प्राशितं पितृतर्पणम्
3.e: (1) Japa is ‘Ahuta,’ (2) Offering into fire is ‘Huta,’ (3) Offering to elementals is ‘Prahuta,’ (4) The honouring of Brāhmaṇas is ‘Brāhmya-huta,’ and (5) Water-offering to Pitṛs is ‘Prāśita.’

3.s: svādhyāye nityayuktaḥ syāddaive caivaiha karmaṇi daivakarmaṇi yukto hi bibhartīdaṃ carācaram
3.d: स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्याद्दैवे चैवैह कर्मणि दैवकर्मणि युक्तो हि बिभर्तीदं चराचरम्
3.e: One should be constantly engaged in Vedic Study, as also in acts in honour of the gods; one who is engaged in acts in honour of the gods upholds the world, moveable as well as immoveable.

3.s: agnau prāstā 'hutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate ādityāj jāyate vṛṣtirvṛṣterannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ
3.d: अग्नौ प्रास्ता ऽहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते आदित्याज् जायते वृष्तिर्वृष्तेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः
3.e: An oblation duly thrown into the fire reaches the sun; from the sun proceeds rain from, rain food, and from food, the creatures.

3.s: yathā vāyuṃ samāśritya vartante sarvajantavaḥ sarve jīvanti jantavaḥ tathā gṛhasthamāśritya vartante sarva āśramāḥ vartanta itarāśramaḥ
3.d: यथा वायुं समाश्रित्य वर्तन्ते सर्वजन्तवः सर्वे जीवन्ति जन्तवः तथा गृहस्थमाश्रित्य वर्तन्ते सर्व आश्रमाः वर्तन्त इतराश्रमः
3.e: Just as all Creatures subsist by deriving support from air, so do the other states subsist by deriving support from the Housohelder.
