3.s: yasmāt trayo 'pyāśramiṇo jñānenānnena cānvaham gṛhasthenaiva dhāryante tasmāj jyeṣṭhāśramo gṛhī gṛhaṃ
3.d: यस्मात् त्रयो ऽप्याश्रमिणो ज्ञानेनान्नेन चान्वहम् गृहस्थेनैव धार्यन्ते तस्माज् ज्येष्ठाश्रमो गृही गृहं
3.e: Because men in all the three states are sustained by householders only, with knowledge and food, therefore the householder’s is the highest state.

3.s: sa saṃdhāryaḥ prayatnena svargamakṣayamicchatā sukhaṃ caihaichhatā 'tyantaṃ yo 'dhāryo durbalaindriyaiḥ
3.d: स संधार्यः प्रयत्नेन स्वर्गमक्षयमिच्छता सुखं चैहैछ्हता ऽत्यन्तं यो ऽधार्यो दुर्बलैन्द्रियैः
3.e: That state, which cannot be maintained by men with weak organs, should be kept up with care by one desiring imperishable heaven and also undying happiness in this world.

3.s: ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā bhūtānyatithayastathā āśāsate kuṭumbibhyastebhyaḥ kāryaṃ vijānatā
3.d: ऋषयः पितरो देवा भूतान्यतिथयस्तथा आशासते कुटुम्बिभ्यस्तेभ्यः कार्यं विजानता
3.e: Sages, Pitṛs, gods, elementals and guests have expectations from family-men; one who knows should fulfil (one’s duty) towards them.’

3.s: svādhyāyenārcayetaṛṣīn homairdevān yathāvidhi pitr̥̄ṃśrāddhaiśca nr̥̄nannairbhūtāni balikarmaṇā
3.d: स्वाध्यायेनार्चयेतऋषीन् होमैर्देवान् यथाविधि पित्र्̥̄ंश्राद्धैश्च न्र्̥̄नन्नैर्भूतानि बलिकर्मणा
3.e: One should worship, according to law, the Sages by Vedic Study, the Gods by Homa-offerings, the Pitṛs by Śrāddha offerings, the Men by food and the Elementals by the offering of Bali.’

3.s: kuryādahar 'haḥ śrāddhamannādyenaudakena vā dadyādahar 'haḥ payomūlaphalairvā 'pi pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāvahan
3.d: कुर्यादहर् ऽहः श्राद्धमन्नाद्येनौदकेन वा दद्यादहर् ऽहः पयोमूलफलैर्वा ऽपि पितृभ्यः प्रीतिमावहन्
3.e: One should daily offer Śrāddha with food, or with water, or with milk, roots and fruits,—(thereby) bringing pleasure to the Pitṛs.

3.s: ekamapyāśayedvipraṃ pitryarthe pāñcayajñike pitryarthaṃ na caivātrāśayet kiṃ cidvaiśvadevaṃ prati dvijam
3.d: एकमप्याशयेद्विप्रं पित्र्यर्थे पाञ्चयज्ञिके पित्र्यर्थं न चैवात्राशयेत् किं चिद्वैश्वदेवं प्रति द्विजम्
3.e: At that (Śrāddha) which forms part of the Five Sacrifices, one should feed even one Brāhmaṇa in honour of the pitṛs; and on this occasion he shall not feed any Brāhmaṇa in honour of the Viśve-devas.

3.s: vaiśvadevasya siddhasya gṛhye 'gnau vidhipūrvakam ābhyaḥ kuryāddevatābhyo brāhmaṇo homamanvaham
3.d: वैश्वदेवस्य सिद्धस्य गृह्ये ऽग्नौ विधिपूर्वकम् आभ्यः कुर्याद्देवताभ्यो ब्राह्मणो होममन्वहम्
3.e: Out of the food cooked in the domestic fire, for the Viśvedevas, the Brāhmaṇa shall every day offer, according to rule, Homa to these deities,’

3.s: agneḥ somasya caivādau tayoścaiva samastayoḥ viśvebhyaścaiva devebhyo dhanvantaraya eva ca
3.d: अग्नेः सोमस्य चैवादौ तयोश्चैव समस्तयोः विश्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यो धन्वन्तरय एव च
3.e: First to Agni and to Soma, then to both these together, then to the Viśve-devas and to Dhanvantari.

3.s: kuhvai caivānumatyai ca prajāpataya eva ca saha dyāvāpṛthivyośca tathā sviṣṭakṛte 'ntataḥ
3.d: कुह्वै चैवानुमत्यै च प्रजापतय एव च सह द्यावापृथिव्योश्च तथा स्विष्टकृते ऽन्ततः
3.e: To Kuhū, to Anumati, and to Prajāpati; then to Dyauḥ—Pṛthivī jointly, and finally to Sviṣṭakṛt,’

3.s: evaṃ samyagg havirhutvā sarvadikṣu pradakṣiṇam indrāntakāppatīndubhyaḥ sānugebhyo baliṃ haret
3.d: एवं सम्यग्ग् हविर्हुत्वा सर्वदिक्षु प्रदक्षिणम् इन्द्रान्तकाप्पतीन्दुभ्यः सानुगेभ्यो बलिं हरेत्
3.e: Having thus duly offered the oblation into fire, he should place Bali-offerings in all directions, proceeding towards his right to Indra, Antaka, Ap-pati and Indu, along with their followers.

3.s: marudbhya iti tu dvāri kṣipedapsvadbhya ityapi vanaspatibhya ityevaṃ musalaulūkhale haret
3.d: मरुद्भ्य इति तु द्वारि क्षिपेदप्स्वद्भ्य इत्यपि वनस्पतिभ्य इत्येवं मुसलौलूखले हरेत्
3.e: Saying “this to the Maruts,” he should make an offering at the door; also one in water, saying, “this to the Apas;” and he should hake an offering on the pestle and mortar, saying, “this to the Vanaspatis.”

3.s: ucchīrṣake śriyai kuryādbhadrakālyai ca pādataḥ brahmavāstoṣpatibhyāṃ tu vāstumadhye baliṃ haret
3.d: उच्छीर्षके श्रियै कुर्याद्भद्रकाल्यै च पादतः ब्रह्मवास्तोष्पतिभ्यां तु वास्तुमध्ये बलिं हरेत्
3.e: He should hake an offering to Śrī on the “head” and to Bhadrakālī on the “feet;” for Brahman and Vāstoṣpati, he should place an offering in the centre of the homestead.

3.s: viśvebhyaścaiva devebhyo balimākāśa utkṣipet divācarebhyo bhūtebhyo naktañcāribhya eva ca
3.d: विश्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यो बलिमाकाश उत्क्षिपेत् दिवाचरेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो नक्तञ्चारिभ्य एव च
3.e: The offering to the Viśvedevas he should throw into the sky; as also to the Elementals roaming in the day and to those roaming at night.

3.s: pṛṣṭhavāstuni kurvīta baliṃ sarvātmabhūtaye sarvānnabhūtaye pitṛbhyo baliśeṣaṃ tu sarvaṃ dakṣiṇato haret
3.d: पृष्ठवास्तुनि कुर्वीत बलिं सर्वात्मभूतये सर्वान्नभूतये पितृभ्यो बलिशेषं तु सर्वं दक्षिणतो हरेत्
3.e: These offerings one should make in the upper dwelling, for the purpose of acquiring all kinds of food. The entire remnant of the offerings he should offer towards the South, to the pitṛs.

3.s: śūnāṃ ca patitānāṃ ca śvapacāṃ pāparogiṇām vayasānāṃ kṛmīṇāṃ ca śanakairnirvapedbhuvi vayasāṃ ca
3.d: शूनां च पतितानां च श्वपचां पापरोगिणाम् वयसानां कृमीणां च शनकैर्निर्वपेद्भुवि वयसां च
3.e: He should gently place on the ground food for dogs, outcasts, Cāṇḍālas, persons afflicted with filthy diseases, birds and insects.

3.s: evaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūtāni brāhmaṇo nityamarcati sa gacchati paraṃ sthānaṃ tejomūrtiḥ pathāṛjunā
3.d: एवं यः सर्वभूतानि ब्राह्मणो नित्यमर्चति स गच्छति परं स्थानं तेजोमूर्तिः पथाऋजुना
3.e: The Brāhmaṇa who thus daily honours all beings, becomes endowed with a body of light, and goes to the highest place, by the straight path.

3.s: kṛtvaitadbalikarmaivamatithiṃ pūrvamāśayet bhikṣāṃ ca bhikṣave dadyādvidhivadbrahmacāriṇe
3.d: कृत्वैतद्बलिकर्मैवमतिथिं पूर्वमाशयेत् भिक्षां च भिक्षवे दद्याद्विधिवद्ब्रह्मचारिणे
3.e: Having performed this rite of offerings, he should first feed his guest and then give alms in the proper form, to one who is mendicant and a ‘Brahmacārin’

3.s: yat puṇyaphalamāpnoti gāṃ dattvā vidhivadguroḥ tat puṇyaphalamāpnoti bhikṣāṃ dattvā dvijo gṛhī
3.d: यत् पुण्यफलमाप्नोति गां दत्त्वा विधिवद्गुरोः तत् पुण्यफलमाप्नोति भिक्षां दत्त्वा द्विजो गृही
3.e: The twice-born householder, giving alms, obtains the same reward for merit which reward for merit one obtains by giving a cow, in the proper form, to his Teacher.

3.s: bhikṣāmapyudapātraṃ vā satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam vedatattvārthaviduṣe brāhmaṇāyaupapādayet
3.d: भिक्षामप्युदपात्रं वा सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् वेदतत्त्वार्थविदुषे ब्राह्मणायौपपादयेत्
3.e: In accordance with scriptural injunctions, one should make over to the Brāhmaṇa knowing the true meaning of the Veda even alms and a water-put, after having honoured him.

3.s: naśyanti havyakavyāni narāṇāmavijānatām bhasmībhūteṣu vipreṣu mohāddattāni dātṛbhiḥ bhasmabhūteṣu
3.d: नश्यन्ति हव्यकव्यानि नराणामविजानताम् भस्मीभूतेषु विप्रेषु मोहाद्दत्तानि दातृभिः भस्मभूतेषु
3.e: Rites in honour of the gods and those in honour of the Pitṛs performed by ignorant men become lost, when they are presented by the givers, through folly, to ash-like Brāhmaṇas.

3.s: vidyātapassamṛddheṣu hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu nistārayati durgācca mahataścaiva kilbiṣāt
3.d: विद्यातपस्समृद्धेषु हुतं विप्रमुखाग्निषु निस्तारयति दुर्गाच्च महतश्चैव किल्बिषात्
3.e: An oblation thrown into the mouth-fire of Brāhmaṇas, effulgent with learning and austerities, saves from trouble, and also from great sin.

3.s: saṃprāptāya tvatithaye pradadyādāsanaudake annaṃ caiva yathāśakti satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam saṃskṛtya
3.d: संप्राप्ताय त्वतिथये प्रदद्यादासनौदके अन्नं चैव यथाशक्ति सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् संस्कृत्य
3.e: To the guest that has happened to come, he should offer; according to rule, water and seat, and also food prepared to the best of his abilitv.

3.s: śilānapyuñchato nityaṃ pañcāgnīnapi juhvataḥ sarvaṃ sukṛtamādatte brāhmaṇo 'narcito vasan
3.d: शिलानप्युञ्छतो नित्यं पञ्चाग्नीनपि जुह्वतः सर्वं सुकृतमादत्ते ब्राह्मणो ऽनर्चितो वसन्
3.e: A Brāhmaṇa staying unhonoured (in one’s house) takes away all his merit, even though he be one who subsists by gathering harvest-droppings, or offers oblations into the five fires.

3.s: tṛṇāni bhūmirudakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā etānyapi satāṃ gehe naucchidyante kadā cana
3.d: तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक् चतुर्थी च सूनृता एतान्यपि सतां गेहे नौच्छिद्यन्ते कदा चन
3.e: Grasses, place, water and kind word as the fourth,—even these never fail in the house of good people.

3.s: ekarātraṃ tu nivasannatithirbrāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ anityaṃ hi sthito yasmāt tasmādatithirucyate
3.d: एकरात्रं तु निवसन्नतिथिर्ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः अनित्यं हि स्थितो यस्मात् तस्मादतिथिरुच्यते
3.e: A Brāhmaṇa staying for a single night has been declared to be a “guest” (Atithi). Because his stay is not long, therefore he is called “Atithi” (guest).

3.s: naikagrāmīṇamatithiṃ vipraṃ sāṅgatikaṃ tathā upasthitaṃ gṛhe vidyādbhāryā yatrāgnayo 'pi vā
3.d: नैकग्रामीणमतिथिं विप्रं साङ्गतिकं तथा उपस्थितं गृहे विद्याद्भार्या यत्राग्नयो ऽपि वा
3.e: One should not regard as “guest” a Brāhmaṇa who lives in the same village or who is a companion. He should regard him as such when he arrives at his house, or where the wife and the fires are at the time.

3.s: upāsate ye gṛhasthāḥ parapākamabuddhayaḥ tena te pretya paśutāṃ vrajantyannādidāyinaḥ
3.d: उपासते ये गृहस्थाः परपाकमबुद्धयः तेन ते प्रेत्य पशुतां व्रजन्त्यन्नादिदायिनः
3.e: Those foolish householders who wait upon the food cooked by others, become, after death, on that account, cattle belonging to the givers of food.

3.s: apraṇodyo 'tithiḥ sāyaṃ sūryauḍho gṛhamedhinā kāle prāptastvakāle vā nāsyānaśnan gṛhe vaset
3.d: अप्रणोद्यो ऽतिथिः सायं सूर्यौढो गृहमेधिना काले प्राप्तस्त्वकाले वा नास्यानश्नन् गृहे वसेत्
3.e: The guest brought by the sun in the evening should not be driven away by the house-holder. Arrived in time, or not in time, he shall not stay in his house without taking food.

3.s: na vai svayaṃ tadaśnīyādatithiṃ yanna bhojayet dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ vā 'tithipūjanam
3.d: न वै स्वयं तदश्नीयादतिथिं यन्न भोजयेत् धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वर्ग्यं वा ऽतिथिपूजनम्
3.e: He himself should not eat what he does not offer to his guest. The honouring of guests is conducive to wealth, fame, longevity and heaven.

3.s: āsanāvasathau śayyāmanuvrajyāmupāsanām uttameṣūttamaṃ kuryāddhīine hīnaṃ same samam
3.d: आसनावसथौ शय्यामनुव्रज्यामुपासनाम् उत्तमेषूत्तमं कुर्याद्धीइने हीनं समे समम्
3.e: He should offer seat, room, bed, foliowing and attendance of the best kind to superiors, of the inferior kind to inferiors and of the equal (ordinary) kind to equals.

3.s: vaiśvadeve tu nirvṛtte yadyanyo 'tithirāvrajet tasyāpyannaṃ yathāśakti pradadyānna baliṃ haret
3.d: वैश्वदेवे तु निर्वृत्ते यद्यन्यो ऽतिथिराव्रजेत् तस्याप्यन्नं यथाशक्ति प्रदद्यान्न बलिं हरेत्
3.e: On the Vaiśvadeva having been finished, if another guest should happen to arrive,—for him also he should provide food to the best of his ability; but he shall not make any offering (out of that food).

3.s: na bhojanārthaṃ sve vipraḥ kulagotre nivedayet bhojanārthaṃ hi te śaṃsan vāntāśīityucyate budhaiḥ
3.d: न भोजनार्थं स्वे विप्रः कुलगोत्रे निवेदयेत् भोजनार्थं हि ते शंसन् वान्ताशीइत्युच्यते बुधैः
3.e: A Brāhmaṇa should not advertise his family and Gotra for the purpose of obtaining a meal. Bragging about these, for the purpose of obtaining a meal, he comes to be called a “feeder on filth” by the wise.

3.s: na brāhmaṇasya tvatithirgṛhe rājanya ucyate vaiśyaśūdrau sakhā caiva jñātayo gurureva ca
3.d: न ब्राह्मणस्य त्वतिथिर्गृहे राजन्य उच्यते वैश्यशूद्रौ सखा चैव ज्ञातयो गुरुरेव च
3.e: In a Brāhmaṇa’s house, the Kṣatriya is not called a ‘guest;’ nor the Vaiśya or the Śūdra, nor his friends or relations, or his Teacher.

3.s: yadi tvatithidharmeṇa kṣatriyo gṛhamāvrajet bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu kāmaṃ tamapi bhojayet
3.d: यदि त्वतिथिधर्मेण क्षत्रियो गृहमाव्रजेत् भुक्तवत्सु च विप्रेषु कामं तमपि भोजयेत्
3.e: If a Kṣatriya should happen to come to one’s house in the character of a guest, one may feed him also, after the Brāhmaṇas have eaten.

3.s: vaiśyaśūdrāvapi prāptau kuṭumbe 'tithidharmiṇau bhojayet saha bhṛtyaistāvānṛśaṃsyaṃ prayojayan
3.d: वैश्यशूद्रावपि प्राप्तौ कुटुम्बे ऽतिथिधर्मिणौ भोजयेत् सह भृत्यैस्तावानृशंस्यं प्रयोजयन्
3.e: The Vaiśya and the Śūdra also, when arrived in the family in the character of guests, he should feed, along with his servants,—showing his compassionate disposition.

3.s: itarānapi sakhiādīn samprītyā gṛhamāgatān prakṛtyānnaṃ yathāśakti bhojayet saha bhāryayā
3.d: इतरानपि सखिआदीन् सम्प्रीत्या गृहमागतान् प्रकृत्यान्नं यथाशक्ति भोजयेत् सह भार्यया
3.e: Others also, friends and the rest, that may come to his house out of affection, he should feed on food specially prepared, to the best of his ability, together with his wife.

3.s: suvāsinīḥ kumārīśca rogiṇo garbhiṇīḥ striyaḥ atithibhyo 'gra evaitān bhojayedavicārayan 'tithibhyo 'nvagevaitān
3.d: सुवासिनीः कुमारीश्च रोगिणो गर्भिणीः स्त्रियः अतिथिभ्यो ऽग्र एवैतान् भोजयेदविचारयन् ऽतिथिभ्यो ऽन्वगेवैतान्
3.e: Newly married girls, maidens, sick persons and pregnant women,—these he should, without hesitation, feed immediately after the guests.

3.s: adattvā tu ya etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṅkte 'vicakṣaṇaḥ sa bhuñjāno na jānāti śvagṛdhrairjagdhimātmanaḥ
3.d: अदत्त्वा तु य एतेभ्यः पूर्वं भुङ्क्ते ऽविचक्षणः स भुञ्जानो न जानाति श्वगृध्रैर्जग्धिमात्मनः
3.e: The foolish man, who eats before giving food to these, does not understand, that, in thus eating, he is himself devoured by dogs and vultures.

3.s: bhuktavatsvatha vipreṣu sveṣu bhṛtyeṣu caiva hi bhuñjīyātāṃ tataḥ paścādavaśiṣṭaṃ tu dampatī
3.d: भुक्तवत्स्वथ विप्रेषु स्वेषु भृत्येषु चैव हि भुञ्जीयातां ततः पश्चादवशिष्टं तु दम्पती
3.e: After the Brāhmaṇas, his own people and servants have dined,—the husband and wife should afterwards eat what is left.

3.s: devān ṛṣīn manuṣyāṃśca pitr̥̄n gṛhyāśca devatāḥ pūjayitvā tataḥ paścādgṛhasthaḥ śeṣabhug bhavet
3.d: देवान् ऋषीन् मनुष्यांश्च पित्र्̥̄न् गृह्याश्च देवताः पूजयित्वा ततः पश्चाद्गृहस्थः शेषभुग् भवेत्
3.e: Having worshipped the gods, sages, men, the Pitṛs and the household deities, the Householder shall eat afterwards what remains.

3.s: aghaṃ sa kevalaṃ bhuṅkte yaḥ pacatyātmakāraṇāt yajñaśiṣṭāśanaṃ hyetat satāmannaṃ vidhīyate
3.d: अघं स केवलं भुङ्क्ते यः पचत्यात्मकारणात् यज्ञशिष्टाशनं ह्येतत् सतामन्नं विधीयते
3.e: He who cooks for himself eats only sin; for the eating of good mem has been described as the eating of the remains of sacrifices.

3.s: rājaṛtvijsnātakagurūn priyaśvaśuramātulān arhayen madhuparkeṇa parisaṃvatsarāt punaḥ
3.d: राजऋत्विज्स्नातकगुरून् प्रियश्वशुरमातुलान् अर्हयेन् मधुपर्केण परिसंवत्सरात् पुनः
3.e: He should receive, with the “honey-mixture,” the king, the priest, the accomplished Student, the Teacher, the Son-in-law, the Father-in-law and the Maternal uncle,—coming again after a year.

3.s: rājā ca śrotriyaścaiva yajñakarmaṇyupasthitau upasthite madhuparkeṇa saṃpūjyau na tvayajña iti sthitiḥ
3.d: राजा च श्रोत्रियश्चैव यज्ञकर्मण्युपस्थितौ उपस्थिते मधुपर्केण संपूज्यौ न त्वयज्ञ इति स्थितिः
3.e: The king and the Learned Man should be honoured with the Honey-mixture, at the approach of a sacrificial performance,—not if there is no sacrifice (going to be performed).

3.s: sāyaṃ tvannasya siddhasya patnyamantraṃ baliṃ haret vaiśvadevaṃ hi nāmaitat sāyaṃ prātarvidhīyate
3.d: सायं त्वन्नस्य सिद्धस्य पत्न्यमन्त्रं बलिं हरेत् वैश्वदेवं हि नामैतत् सायं प्रातर्विधीयते
3.e: Out of the food cooked in the evening the wife should offer the Bali-oblation, without sacred formulas. This is the “Vaiśvadeva” rite which has been enjoined for both Morning and evening.

3.s: pitṛyajñaṃ tu nirvartya vipraścandrakṣaye 'gnimān caindukṣaye piṇḍānvāhāryakaṃ śrāddhaṃ kuryān māsānumāsikam
3.d: पितृयज्ञं तु निर्वर्त्य विप्रश्चन्द्रक्षये ऽग्निमान् चैन्दुक्षये पिण्डान्वाहार्यकं श्राद्धं कुर्यान् मासानुमासिकम्
3.e: Month after Month, on the moonless day, the Brāhmaṇa with the Fire shall, after having performed the Pitṛyajña, offer the “Piṇḍānvāhāryaka.”

3.s: pitr̥̄ṇāṃ māsikaṃ śrāddhamanvāhāryaṃ vidurbudhāḥ taccāmiṣeṇā kartavyaṃ praśastena prayatnataḥ
3.d: पित्र्̥̄णां मासिकं श्राद्धमन्वाहार्यं विदुर्बुधाः तच्चामिषेणा कर्तव्यं प्रशस्तेन प्रयत्नतः
3.e: The monthly śrāddha to the Pitṛs the wise call “anvāhārya;” and it should be carefully performed with such meat as has been commended.

3.s: tatra ye bhojanīyāḥ syurye ca varjyā dvijottamāḥ yāvantaścaiva yaiścānnaistān pravakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ
3.d: तत्र ये भोजनीयाः स्युर्ये च वर्ज्या द्विजोत्तमाः यावन्तश्चैव यैश्चान्नैस्तान् प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः
3.e: I am now going to describe fully which and how many Brāhmaṇas should be fed at it, and on what food,—as also those that should be avoided.

3.s: dvau daive pitṛkārye trīnekaikamubhayatra vā pitṛkṛtye bhojayet susamṛddho 'pi na prasajjeta vistare na pravarteta
3.d: द्वौ दैवे पितृकार्ये त्रीनेकैकमुभयत्र वा पितृकृत्ये भोजयेत् सुसमृद्धो ऽपि न प्रसज्जेत विस्तरे न प्रवर्तेत
3.e: Even though wealthy, one should feed two at the rite performed in honour of the gods, and three at that in honour of the Pitṛs; or one only at each of the two rites he should not indulge in large company.

3.s: satkriyāṃ deśakālau ca śaucaṃ brāhmaṇasaṃpadaḥ pañcaitān vistaro hanti tasmānnaiheta vistaram
3.d: सत्क्रियां देशकालौ च शौचं ब्राह्मणसंपदः पञ्चैतान् विस्तरो हन्ति तस्मान्नैहेत विस्तरम्
3.e: Respectful treatment, place and time, purity and the qualities of Brāhmaṇas,—a large company hampers these five; therefore one shall not seek a large company.

3.s: prathitā pretakṛtyaiṣā pitryaṃ nāma vidhukṣaye tasmin yuktasyaiti nityaṃ pretakṛtyaiva laukikī
3.d: प्रथिता प्रेतकृत्यैषा पित्र्यं नाम विधुक्षये तस्मिन् युक्तस्यैति नित्यं प्रेतकृत्यैव लौकिकी
3.e: This rite named “Pitrya,” performed on the Moonless Day is known as beneficial to the dead. To him who is intent on performing it, there always accrues benefit after death, offered according to human ordinances.

3.s: śrotriyāyaiva deyāni havyakavyāni dātṛbhiḥ arhattamāya viprāya tasmai dattaṃ mahāphalam
3.d: श्रोत्रियायैव देयानि हव्यकव्यानि दातृभिः अर्हत्तमाय विप्राय तस्मै दत्तं महाफलम्
3.e: Food offered to the gods and that offered in the Pitṛs are to be given to the most deserving; Brāhmaṇa learned in the Vedas. What is given to him is conducive to great results.

3.s: ekaikamapi vidvāṃsaṃ daive pitrye ca bhojayet bhojayan puṣkalaṃ phalamāpnoti nāmantrajñān bahūnapi
3.d: एकैकमपि विद्वांसं दैवे पित्र्ये च भोजयेत् भोजयन् पुष्कलं फलमाप्नोति नामन्त्रज्ञान् बहूनपि
3.e: By feeding at least one learned brāhmaṇa each at the rite performed in honour of the gods and that performed in honour of the ancestors,—one obtains a full reward; and not by feeding even many men ignorant of the Veda.’

3.s: dūrādeva parīkṣeta brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam tīrthaṃ taddhavyakavyānāṃ pradāne so 'tithiḥ smṛtaḥ
3.d: दूरादेव परीक्षेत ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम् तीर्थं तद्धव्यकव्यानां प्रदाने सो ऽतिथिः स्मृतः
3.e: From far off one should examine the Brāhmaṇa thoroughly versed in the Veda; such a one is the proper channel for offerings to gods and Pitṛ and in the matter of gifts he has been declared to be the guest.

3.s: sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇāmanṛcāṃ yatra bhuñjate ekastān mantravit prītaḥ sarvānarhati dharmataḥ
3.d: सहस्रं हि सहस्राणामनृचां यत्र भुञ्जते एकस्तान् मन्त्रवित् प्रीतः सर्वानर्हति धर्मतः
3.e: Where one thousand persons ignorant of the Veda eat, all those a single man learned in the Veda, on being satisfied, absorbs, in point of merit.

3.s: jñānautkṛṣṭāya deyāni kavyāni ca havīṃṣi ca na hi hastāvasṛgdigdhau rudhireṇaiva śudhyataḥ
3.d: ज्ञानौत्कृष्टाय देयानि कव्यानि च हवींषि च न हि हस्तावसृग्दिग्धौ रुधिरेणैव शुध्यतः
3.e: Offerings for gods and Pitṛs should be given to one who is distinguished by knowledge; for hands smeared with blood are not cleansed by blood.

3.s: yāvato grasate grāsān havyakavyeṣvamantravit tāvato grasate preto dīptaśūlaṛṣṭiayoguḍān
3.d: यावतो ग्रसते ग्रासान् हव्यकव्येष्वमन्त्रवित् तावतो ग्रसते प्रेतो दीप्तशूलऋष्टिअयोगुडान्
3.e: As many mouthfuls as the person ignorant of the Veda swallows out of the offerings to gods and Pitṛs, so many flaming spikes, spears and iron-balls does the man swallow after death.

3.s: jñānaniṣṭhā dvijāḥ ke cit taponiṣṭhāstathā 'pare tapassvādhyāyaniṣṭhāśca karmaniṣṭhāstathā 'pare
3.d: ज्ञाननिष्ठा द्विजाः के चित् तपोनिष्ठास्तथा ऽपरे तपस्स्वाध्यायनिष्ठाश्च कर्मनिष्ठास्तथा ऽपरे
3.e: Some twice-born persons excel in learning; others excel in austerities; some others excel in austerities and Vedic study, and others again excel in rites.

3.s: jñānaniṣṭheṣu kavyāni pratiṣṭhāpyāni yatnataḥ havyāni tu yathānyāyaṃ sarveṣveva caturṣvapi
3.d: ज्ञाननिष्ठेषु कव्यानि प्रतिष्ठाप्यानि यत्नतः हव्यानि तु यथान्यायं सर्वेष्वेव चतुर्ष्वपि
3.e: The offerings to the pitṛs should be carefully presented to those excelling in learning; and the offerings to gods to all the four, according to law.

3.s: aśrotriyaḥ pitā yasya putraḥ syādvedapāragaḥ aśrotriyo vā putraḥ syāt pitā syādvedapāragaḥ
3.d: अश्रोत्रियः पिता यस्य पुत्रः स्याद्वेदपारगः अश्रोत्रियो वा पुत्रः स्यात् पिता स्याद्वेदपारगः
3.e: If a father happen to be ignorant of the Veda, whose son is thoroughly versed in the Veda,—and if the son happen to be ignorant of the Veda and the father is t horoughly versed in the Veda;

3.s: jyāyāṃsamanayorvidyādyasya syātśrotriyaḥ pitā mantrasaṃpūjanārthaṃ tu satkāramitaro 'rhati
3.d: ज्यायांसमनयोर्विद्याद्यस्य स्यात्श्रोत्रियः पिता मन्त्रसंपूजनार्थं तु सत्कारमितरो ऽर्हति
3.e: ‘Of these two one should regard him as superior whose father is learned in the Veda; while the other deserves honour for the sake of the veneration due to the Veda.

3.s: na śrāddhe bhojayen mitraṃ dhanaiḥ kāryo 'sya saṅgrahaḥ nāriṃ na mitraṃ yaṃ vidyāt taṃ śrāddhe bhojayeddvijam
3.d: न श्राद्धे भोजयेन् मित्रं धनैः कार्यो ऽस्य सङ्ग्रहः नारिं न मित्रं यं विद्यात् तं श्राद्धे भोजयेद्द्विजम्
3.e: At a Śrāddha one should not feed a friend; his acquisition shall be made by means of riches. At a Śrāddha one should feed him whom he regards neither as friend nor as foe.

3.s: yasya mitrapradhānāni śrāddhāni ca havīṃṣi ca tasya pretya phalaṃ nāsti śrāddheṣu ca haviḥṣu ca
3.d: यस्य मित्रप्रधानानि श्राद्धानि च हवींषि च तस्य प्रेत्य फलं नास्ति श्राद्धेषु च हविःषु च
3.e: He at whose Śrāddhas and sacrifices, the friend forms the principal factor,—for him, after death, there is no reward, either for Śrāddhas or for sacrifices.

3.s: yaḥ saṅgatāni kurute mohātśrāddhena mānavaḥ sa svargāccyavate lokātśrāddhamitro dvijādhamaḥ
3.d: यः सङ्गतानि कुरुते मोहात्श्राद्धेन मानवः स स्वर्गाच्च्यवते लोकात्श्राद्धमित्रो द्विजाधमः
3.e: The man who, through folly, makes friendships by means of Śrāddhas,—that meanest of twice-born men, having the Śrāddha for his friend, falls from the regions of heaven.

3.s: saṃbhojāni sā 'bhihitā paiśācī dakṣiṇā dvijaiḥ ihaivāste tu sā loke gaurandhaivaikaveśmani
3.d: संभोजानि सा ऽभिहिता पैशाची दक्षिणा द्विजैः इहैवास्ते तु सा लोके गौरन्धैवैकवेश्मनि
3.e: This convivial dinner has been called by twice-born people the “gift of devils.” It remains in this world alone, like the blind cow tied in a single room.

3.s: yathairiṇe bījamuptvā na vaptā labhate phalam tathā 'nṛce havirdattvā na dātā labhate phalam
3.d: यथैरिणे बीजमुप्त्वा न वप्ता लभते फलम् तथा ऽनृचे हविर्दत्त्वा न दाता लभते फलम्
3.e: Just as having sown the seed in barren soil, the sower reaps no harvest,—even so, having given the offerings to one ignorant of the Veda, the giver obtains no reward.

3.s: dātr̥̄n pratigrahītr̥̄ṃśca kurute phalabhāginaḥ viduṣe dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā vidhivat pretya caiha ca
3.d: दात्र्̥̄न् प्रतिग्रहीत्र्̥̄ंश्च कुरुते फलभागिनः विदुषे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा विधिवत् प्रेत्य चैह च
3.e: The presenting of the gift, according to rule, to the learned makes the givers and receivers partakers of reward, here as well as after death.

3.s: kāmaṃ śrāddhe 'rcayen mitraṃ nābhirūpamapi tvarim dviṣatā hi havirbhuktaṃ bhavati pretya niṣphalam
3.d: कामं श्राद्धे ऽर्चयेन् मित्रं नाभिरूपमपि त्वरिम् द्विषता हि हविर्भुक्तं भवति प्रेत्य निष्फलम्
3.e: One may entertain a friend at Śrāddhas, but never a foe, even though qualified. The offering eaten by the enemy becomes futile after death.

3.s: yatnena bhojayetśrāddhe bahvṛcaṃ vedapāragam śākhāntagamathādhvaryuṃ chandogaṃ tu samāptikam
3.d: यत्नेन भोजयेत्श्राद्धे बह्वृचं वेदपारगम् शाखान्तगमथाध्वर्युं छन्दोगं तु समाप्तिकम्
3.e: With great care one should feed at a Śrāddha the adherent of the Ṛgveda who is thoroughly versed in his Veda, or the adherent of the Yajurveda who has finished the entire recensional text, or the adherent of the Sāmaveda who has reached the end of it.

3.s: eṣāmanyatamo yasya bhuñjīta śrāddhamarcitaḥ pitr̥̄ṇāṃ tasya tṛptiḥ syātśāśvatī sāptapauruṣī
3.d: एषामन्यतमो यस्य भुञ्जीत श्राद्धमर्चितः पित्र्̥̄णां तस्य तृप्तिः स्यात्शाश्वती साप्तपौरुषी
3.e: If any one of these should dine, duly honoured, at the Śrāddha performed by a certain person, there would be ever-lasting satisfaction for his ancestors, lasting till the seventh degree (of descendants).

3.s: eṣa vai prathamaḥ kalpaḥ pradāne havyakavyayoḥ anukalpastvayaṃ jñeyaḥ sadā sadbhiranuṣṭhitaḥ
3.d: एष वै प्रथमः कल्पः प्रदाने हव्यकव्ययोः अनुकल्पस्त्वयं ज्ञेयः सदा सद्भिरनुष्ठितः
3.e: This is the first course to be adopted in the presenting of the offerings made to Gods and Pitṛs. This (following) is to be regarded as the secondary course always adopted by the good.’

3.s: mātāmahaṃ mātulaṃ ca svasrīyaṃ śvaśuraṃ gurum dauhitraṃ viṭpatiṃ bandhuṃ ṛtvig yājyau ca bhojayet
3.d: मातामहं मातुलं च स्वस्रीयं श्वशुरं गुरुम् दौहित्रं विट्पतिं बन्धुं ऋत्विग् याज्यौ च भोजयेत्
3.e: One may feed the maternal grandfather, the maternal uncle, the sister’s son, father-in-law, the teacher, the daughter’s son, the son-in-law, a relative, the priest and him at whose sacrifices the performer officiates.

3.s: na brāhmaṇaṃ parīkṣeta daive karmaṇi dharmavit pitrye karmaṇi tu prāpte parīkṣeta prayatnataḥ
3.d: न ब्राह्मणं परीक्षेत दैवे कर्मणि धर्मवित् पित्र्ये कर्मणि तु प्राप्ते परीक्षेत प्रयत्नतः
3.e: At the rite in honour of the gods, the man knowing the law shall not examine the Brāhmaṇa. But when the rite in honour of the Pitṛs comes to be performed, he shall examine him carefullv.

3.s: ye stenapatitaklībā ye ca nāstikavṛttayaḥ tān havyakavyayorviprānanarhān manurabravīt
3.d: ये स्तेनपतितक्लीबा ये च नास्तिकवृत्तयः तान् हव्यकव्ययोर्विप्राननर्हान् मनुरब्रवीत्
3.e: Manu has declared those Brāhmaṇas undeserving of (receiving) the offerings to gods and Pitṛs who are thieves, outcasts and eunuchs, as also those that have the behaviour of atheists.

3.s: jaṭilaṃ cānadhīyānaṃ durbālaṃ kitavaṃ tathā yājayanti ca ye pūgāṃstāṃśca śrāddhe na bhojayet
3.d: जटिलं चानधीयानं दुर्बालं कितवं तथा याजयन्ति च ये पूगांस्तांश्च श्राद्धे न भोजयेत्
3.e: One should not feed, at a Śrāddha, one with braided hair, who is not learned, one who is hairless, the gambler, and those who sacrifice for hosts.

3.s: cikitsakān devalakān māṃsavikrayiṇastathā cikitsakādevalakāmāṃsavikrayiṇastathā vipaṇena ca jīvanto varjyāḥ syurhavyakavyayoḥ
3.d: चिकित्सकान् देवलकान् मांसविक्रयिणस्तथा चिकित्सकादेवलकामांसविक्रयिणस्तथा विपणेन च जीवन्तो वर्ज्याः स्युर्हव्यकव्ययोः
3.e: Healers, temple-attendants, meat-sellers and those living by trade,—these should be avoided at rites performed in honour of gods and Pitṛs.

3.s: preṣyo grāmasya rājñaśca kunakhī śyāvadantakaḥ pratiroddhā guroścaiva tyaktāgnirvārdhuṣistathā
3.d: प्रेष्यो ग्रामस्य राज्ञश्च कुनखी श्यावदन्तकः प्रतिरोद्धा गुरोश्चैव त्यक्ताग्निर्वार्धुषिस्तथा
3.e: The servant of a village and of the king, one with deformed nails, one with black teeth, the opposer of his superior, one who has forsaken the Fire and the usurer.

3.s: yakṣmī ca paśupālaśca parivettā nirākṛtiḥ brahmadviṣparivittiśca gaṇābhyantara eva ca
3.d: यक्ष्मी च पशुपालश्च परिवेत्ता निराकृतिः ब्रह्मद्विष्परिवित्तिश्च गणाभ्यन्तर एव च
3.e: The invalid, the cattle-tender, one who has superseded h is elder brother, he who neglects the Great Sacrifices, one who is inimical to Brāhmaṇas, he who has been superseded by his younger brother, and one who is member of a company.

3.s: kuśīlavo 'vakīrṇī ca vṛṣalīpatireva ca paunarbhavaśca kāṇaśca yasya caupapatirgṛhe
3.d: कुशीलवो ऽवकीर्णी च वृषलीपतिरेव च पौनर्भवश्च काणश्च यस्य चौपपतिर्गृहे
3.e: An actor, one who has broken the vows of continence, the husband of a Śūdra woman, the son of a re-married woman, one who has only one eye, and he in whose house lives the paramour.

3.s: bhṛtakādhyāpako yaśca bhṛtakādhyāpitastathā śūdraśiṣyo guruścaiva vāgduṣṭaḥ kuṇḍagolakau
3.d: भृतकाध्यापको यश्च भृतकाध्यापितस्तथा शूद्रशिष्यो गुरुश्चैव वाग्दुष्टः कुण्डगोलकौ
3.e: One who teaches for a stipulated fee, he who is taught by one who teaches for a stipulated fee, the pupil and also the teacher of a Śūdra, one who is reprehensible in speech, the son of an adulteress and the son of a widow.

3.s: akāraṇe parityaktā mātāpitrorgurostathā akāraṇaparityaktā brāhmairyaunaiśca saṃbandhaiḥ saṃyogaṃ patitairgataḥ
3.d: अकारणे परित्यक्ता मातापित्रोर्गुरोस्तथा अकारणपरित्यक्ता ब्राह्मैर्यौनैश्च संबन्धैः संयोगं पतितैर्गतः
3.e: The forsaker, without cause, of his mother, father and superior; and he who has formed a connection, through the relationship of either Veda or marriage, with outcasts.

3.s: agāradāhī garadaḥ kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī samudrayāyī bandī ca tailikaḥ kūṭakārakaḥ
3.d: अगारदाही गरदः कुण्डाशी सोमविक्रयी समुद्रयायी बन्दी च तैलिकः कूटकारकः
3.e: The house-burner, the poisoner, one who eats the food of an adulteress’ son, the seller of Soma, the sea-voyager, the bard, the dealer in oils, and the perjuror.

3.s: pitrā vivadamānaśca kitavo madyapastathā pāparogyabhiśastaśca dāmbhiko rasavikrayī
3.d: पित्रा विवदमानश्च कितवो मद्यपस्तथा पापरोग्यभिशस्तश्च दाम्भिको रसविक्रयी
3.e: One quarrelling with one’s father, the keeper of a gambling house, the drunkard, one afflicted with a foul disease, one accused of sins, the hypocrite, and the dealer in essence.

3.s: dhanusśarāṇāṃ kartā ca yaścāgredidhiṣūpatiḥ mitradhrug dyūtavṛttiśca putrācāryastathaiva ca
3.d: धनुस्शराणां कर्ता च यश्चाग्रेदिधिषूपतिः मित्रध्रुग् द्यूतवृत्तिश्च पुत्राचार्यस्तथैव च
3.e: The maker of bows and arrows, he whose wife dallies with another person and he who makes love to his brother’s widow, he who injures a friend, he who subsists by gambling and he who has his own son for his teacher.

3.s: bhrāmarī ganḍamālī ca śvitryatho piśunastathā unmatto 'ndhaśca varjyāḥ syurvedanindaka eva ca
3.d: भ्रामरी गन्डमाली च श्वित्र्यथो पिशुनस्तथा उन्मत्तो ऽन्धश्च वर्ज्याः स्युर्वेदनिन्दक एव च
3.e: An epileptic, one having a string of scrofulous swellings, one who suffers from leucoderma, the backbiter, the lunatic, the blind man, and the derider of the Veda—all these should be avoided.

3.s: hastigo 'śvauṣṭradamako nakṣatrairyaśca jīvati pakṣiṇāṃ poṣako yaśca yuddhācāryastathaiva ca
3.d: हस्तिगो ऽश्वौष्ट्रदमको नक्षत्रैर्यश्च जीवति पक्षिणां पोषको यश्च युद्धाचार्यस्तथैव च
3.e: The tamer of elephants, bulls, horses or camels, one who subsists on stars, bird-keeper and the teacher of warfare.

3.s: srotasāṃ bhedako yaśca teṣāṃ cāvaraṇe rataḥ gṛhasaṃveśako dūto vṛkṣāropaka eva ca
3.d: स्रोतसां भेदको यश्च तेषां चावरणे रतः गृहसंवेशको दूतो वृक्षारोपक एव च
3.e: He who diverts water-courses, he who is addicted to obstructing them, the house-planner, the messenger and

3.s: śvakrīḍī śyenajīvī ca kanyādūṣaka eva ca hiṃsro vṛṣalavṛttiśca gaṇānāṃ caiva yājakaḥ
3.d: श्वक्रीडी श्येनजीवी च कन्यादूषक एव च हिंस्रो वृषलवृत्तिश्च गणानां चैव याजकः
3.e: He who sports with dogs, the falconer, the defiler of virgins, the cruel man, he who derives his subsistence from Śūdras, and he who sacrifices to the Gaṇas.

3.s: ācārahīnaḥ klībaśca nityaṃ yācanakastathā kṛṣijīvī ślīpadī ca sadbhirnindita eva ca
3.d: आचारहीनः क्लीबश्च नित्यं याचनकस्तथा कृषिजीवी श्लीपदी च सद्भिर्निन्दित एव च
3.e: One devoid of right conduct, the man without vigour, the constant beggar, he who lives by agriculture, one suffering from elephantiasis, and he who is spoken ill of by good men.

3.s: aurabhriko māhiṣikaḥ parapūrvāpatistathā pretaniryāpakaścaiva varjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ
3.d: औरभ्रिको माहिषिकः परपूर्वापतिस्तथा प्रेतनिर्यापकश्चैव वर्जनीयाः प्रयत्नतः
3.e: The sheep-dealer, the buffalo-keeper, the husband of a woman who had another previous husband, the carrier of the dead—all these should be avoided with care.

3.s: etān vigarhitācārānapāṅkteyān dvijādhamān dvijātipravaro vidvānubhayatra vivarjayet
3.d: एतान् विगर्हिताचारानपाङ्क्तेयान् द्विजाधमान् द्विजातिप्रवरो विद्वानुभयत्र विवर्जयेत्
3.e: The learned Brāhmaṇa should avoid at both (rites) these l owest of twice-born men, who are of reprehensible conduct and who are unworthy of company.

3.s: brāhmaṇo tvanadhīyānastṛṇāgniriva śāmyati brāhmaṇaḥ hyanadhīyānaḥ tasmai havyaṃ na dātavyaṃ na hi bhasmani hūyate
3.d: ब्राह्मणो त्वनधीयानस्तृणाग्निरिव शाम्यति ब्राह्मणः ह्यनधीयानः तस्मै हव्यं न दातव्यं न हि भस्मनि हूयते
3.e: The unlearned Brāhmaṇa becomes quenched in the same manner as the fire of dry grass. The sacrificial offering should not be presented to him; as no libation is poured upon ashes.

3.s: apāṅktadāne yo dāturbhavatyūrdhvaṃ phalaudayaḥ 'paṅktyadāne daive haviṣi pitrye vā taṃ pravaksyāmyaśeṣataḥ daive karmaṇi
3.d: अपाङ्क्तदाने यो दातुर्भवत्यूर्ध्वं फलौदयः ऽपङ्क्त्यदाने दैवे हविषि पित्र्ये वा तं प्रवक्स्याम्यशेषतः दैवे कर्मणि
3.e: I am going to describe fully the results that afterwards accrue to the giver from giving, out of the offering to gods and to Pitṛs, to one who is unworthy of the line.

3.s: avratairyaddvijairbhuktaṃ parivetryādibhistathā apāṅkteyairyadanyaiśca tadvai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate
3.d: अव्रतैर्यद्द्विजैर्भुक्तं परिवेत्र्यादिभिस्तथा अपाङ्क्तेयैर्यदन्यैश्च तद्वै रक्षांसि भुञ्जते
3.e: Demons indeed consume the food that is eaten by Brāhmaṇas deviod of self-restraint, by such as those who have superseded their elder brother and the like, or by others that are unworthy of company.

3.s: dārāgnihotrasaṃyogaṃ kurute yo 'graje sthite parivettā sa vijñeyaḥ parivittistu pūrvajaḥ
3.d: दाराग्निहोत्रसंयोगं कुरुते यो ऽग्रजे स्थिते परिवेत्ता स विज्ञेयः परिवित्तिस्तु पूर्वजः
3.e: He who unites himself with “wife” and “Agnihotra,” while his elder remains, is to be regarded as the “superseder of his elder;” and the elder is to be regarded as “one who is superseded.”’

3.s: parivittiḥ parivettā yayā ca parividyate sarve te narakaṃ yānti dātṛyājakapañcamāḥ
3.d: परिवित्तिः परिवेत्ता यया च परिविद्यते सर्वे ते नरकं यान्ति दातृयाजकपञ्चमाः
3.e: The superseded elder brother, the superseding younger brother, and she through whom the superseding is done,—all these go to hell, along with the giver and the officiating priest as the fifth.

3.s: bhrāturmṛtasya bhāryāyāṃ yo 'nurajyeta kāmataḥ dharmeṇāpi niyuktāyāṃ sa jñeyo didhiṣūpatiḥ
3.d: भ्रातुर्मृतस्य भार्यायां यो ऽनुरज्येत कामतः धर्मेणापि नियुक्तायां स ज्ञेयो दिधिषूपतिः
3.e: He who would lasciviously make love to the wife of his dead brother, even though she may have been appointed according to law (to bear a child by him), should be known as the “didhiṣūpati.”

3.s: paradāreṣu jāyete dvau sutau kuṇḍagolakau patyau jīvati kuṇḍaḥ syān mṛte bhartari golakaḥ
3.d: परदारेषु जायेते द्वौ सुतौ कुण्डगोलकौ पत्यौ जीवति कुण्डः स्यान् मृते भर्तरि गोलकः
3.e: By the wives of other men two kinds of sons are born: the “Kuṇḍa” and the “Golaka;” he who is born while the husband is alive is the “Kuṇḍa,” and one born after the death of the husband is the “Golaka.”

3.s: tau tu jātau parakṣetre prāṇinau pretya caiha ca te tu jātāḥ parakṣetre prāṇinaḥ dattāni havyakavyāni nāśayanti pradāyinām
3.d: तौ तु जातौ परक्षेत्रे प्राणिनौ प्रेत्य चैह च ते तु जाताः परक्षेत्रे प्राणिनः दत्तानि हव्यकव्यानि नाशयन्ति प्रदायिनाम्
3.e: These creatures, born of other men’s wives, cause, for the giver, the destruction, in this life as well as after death, of their offerings to gods and pitṛs that have been presented to them.

3.s: apāṅktyo yāvataḥ paṅktyān bhuñjānānanupaśyati 'paṅktyo yāvataḥ tāvatāṃ na phalaṃ tatra dātā prāpnoti bāliśaḥ
3.d: अपाङ्क्त्यो यावतः पङ्क्त्यान् भुञ्जानाननुपश्यति ऽपङ्क्त्यो यावतः तावतां न फलं तत्र दाता प्राप्नोति बालिशः
3.e: If one who is unworthy of company happen to look upon a number of those that are worthy of company, while those are eating, then the foolish giver (of food) does not obtain the reward of feeding so many men.

3.s: vīkṣyāndho navateḥ kāṇaḥ ṣaṣṭeḥ śvitrī śatasya tu śatasya ca pāparogī sahasrasya dāturnāśayate phalam
3.d: वीक्ष्यान्धो नवतेः काणः षष्टेः श्वित्री शतस्य तु शतस्य च पापरोगी सहस्रस्य दातुर्नाशयते फलम्
3.e: The blind man, by looking, destroys the feeder’s reward for feeding ninety men, the one-eyed man of sixty, the leper of one hundred, and the man afflicted with a foul disease of a thousand.

3.s: yāvataḥ saṃspṛśedaṅgairbrāhmaṇāṃśūdrayājakaḥ tāvatāṃ na bhaveddātuḥ phalaṃ dānasya paurtikam
3.d: यावतः संस्पृशेदङ्गैर्ब्राह्मणांशूद्रयाजकः तावतां न भवेद्दातुः फलं दानस्य पौर्तिकम्
3.e: As many Brāhmaṇas the officiator at the sacrifices performed by Śūdras may happen to touch with his limbs,—the reward relating to charity in connection with the gift to so many Brāhmaṇas fails to accrue to the giver.

3.s: vedavidcāpi vipro 'sya lobhāt kṛtvā pratigraham vināśaṃ vrajati kṣipramāmapātramivāmbhasi
3.d: वेदविद्चापि विप्रो ऽस्य लोभात् कृत्वा प्रतिग्रहम् विनाशं व्रजति क्षिप्रमामपात्रमिवाम्भसि
3.e: If a Brāhmaṇa, though learned in the Veda, should, through covetousness, accept a gift from him,—he quickly perishes; just like the unbaked vessel in water.

3.s: somavikrayiṇe viṣṭhā bhiṣaje pūyaśoṇitam naṣṭaṃ devalake dattamapratiṣṭhaṃ tu vārdhuṣau
3.d: सोमविक्रयिणे विष्ठा भिषजे पूयशोणितम् नष्टं देवलके दत्तमप्रतिष्ठं तु वार्धुषौ
3.e: What is given to the Soma-seller becomes ordure; to the physician, pus and blood; that to the temple-attendant becomes lost; and that to the usurer has no place.

3.s: yat tu vāṇijake dattaṃ naiha nāmutra tadbhavet bhasmanīva hutaṃ dravyaṃ tathā paunarbhave dvije
3.d: यत् तु वाणिजके दत्तं नैह नामुत्र तद्भवेत् भस्मनीव हुतं द्रव्यं तथा पौनर्भवे द्विजे
3.e: That which is given to the trader is neither here nor there. Similarly, what is given to the Brāhmaṇa born of a remarried woman is like a libation poured on ashes.

3.s: itareṣu tvapāṅktyeṣu yathauddiṣṭeṣvasādhuṣu medo 'sṛlgmāṃsamajjā 'sthi vadantyannaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
3.d: इतरेषु त्वपाङ्क्त्येषु यथौद्दिष्टेष्वसाधुषु मेदो ऽसृल्ग्मांसमज्जा ऽस्थि वदन्त्यन्नं मनीषिणः
3.e: The wise ones declare that food given to the other unfit persons unworthy of company, described above, becomes fat, blood, flesh, marrow and bone.

3.s: apāṅktyaupahatā paṅktiḥ pāvyate yairdvijottamaiḥ apaṅktyaupahatā paṅktiḥ tānnibodhata kārtsnyena dvijāgryān paṅktipāvanān
3.d: अपाङ्क्त्यौपहता पङ्क्तिः पाव्यते यैर्द्विजोत्तमैः अपङ्क्त्यौपहता पङ्क्तिः तान्निबोधत कार्त्स्न्येन द्विजाग्र्यान् पङ्क्तिपावनान्
3.e: Now listen to the full description of those chief of twice-born men, the sanctifiers of company, by which best of the twice-born a company defiled by men unworthy of company becomes purified.

3.s: agryāḥ sarveṣu vedeṣu sarvapravacaneṣu ca śrotriyānvayajāścaiva vijñeyāḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ
3.d: अग्र्याः सर्वेषु वेदेषु सर्वप्रवचनेषु च श्रोत्रियान्वयजाश्चैव विज्ञेयाः पङ्क्तिपावनाः
3.e: Those persons should be known as “sanctifiers of company” who are foremost in all the vedas and in all the explanatory sciences, and who are born in the family of men learned in the veda.

3.s: triṇāciketaḥ pañcāgnistrisuparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit brahmadeyātmasantāno jyeṣṭhasāmaga eva ca brahmadeyānusantāno
3.d: त्रिणाचिकेतः पञ्चाग्निस्त्रिसुपर्णः षडङ्गवित् ब्रह्मदेयात्मसन्तानो ज्येष्ठसामग एव च ब्रह्मदेयानुसन्तानो
3.e: One who has learnt the “Triṇāciketa,” one who knows the science of the five fires, one who has learnt the “Trisuparṇa,” one who knows the six-limbed science, one who is born of a woman married in the “Brahma (Brāhma)” form, one who sings the Jyeṣṭha-sāmas.

3.s: vedārthavit pravaktā ca brahmacārī sahasradaḥ śatāyuścaiva vijñeyā brāhmaṇāḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ
3.d: वेदार्थवित् प्रवक्ता च ब्रह्मचारी सहस्रदः शतायुश्चैव विज्ञेया ब्राह्मणाः पङ्क्तिपावनाः
3.e: He who understands the meaning of the Veda, he who expounds it, the Student, the giver of a thousand, the centenarian;—these Brāhmaṇas should be known as “Sanctifiers of Company.”

3.s: pūrvedyuraparedyurvā śrāddhakarmaṇyupasthite nimantrayeta try 'varān samyag viprān yathauditān nimantrayīta
3.d: पूर्वेद्युरपरेद्युर्वा श्राद्धकर्मण्युपस्थिते निमन्त्रयेत त्र्य् ऽवरान् सम्यग् विप्रान् यथौदितान् निमन्त्रयीत
3.e: When the śrāddha-performance has approaohed, one should invite, either on the preceding day or the next day, in the proper manner, at least three brāhmaṇas, such as have been described.

3.s: nimantrito dvijaḥ pitrye niyatātmā bhavet sadā na ca chandāṃsyadhīyīta yasya śrāddhaṃ ca tadbhavet
3.d: निमन्त्रितो द्विजः पित्र्ये नियतात्मा भवेत् सदा न च छन्दांस्यधीयीत यस्य श्राद्धं च तद्भवेत्
3.e: The brāhmaṇa invited at a rite in honor of Pitṛs shall remain self-controlled and shall not recite the Veda; so also the man who performs the śrāddha.

3.s: nimantritān hi pitara upatiṣṭhanti tān dvijān vāyuvatcānugacchanti tathā 'sīnānupāsate
3.d: निमन्त्रितान् हि पितर उपतिष्ठन्ति तान् द्विजान् वायुवत्चानुगच्छन्ति तथा ऽसीनानुपासते
3.e: The Pitṛs attend upon those invited Brāhmaṇas; like the wind, they follow them and sit down when they are seated.

3.s: ketitastu yathānyāyaṃ havye kavye dvijottamaḥ kathaṃ cidapyatikrāman pāpaḥ sūkaratāṃ vrajet
3.d: केतितस्तु यथान्यायं हव्ये कव्ये द्विजोत्तमः कथं चिदप्यतिक्रामन् पापः सूकरतां व्रजेत्
3.e: The rest of Brāhmaṇas, who, when duly invited at the rite in honour of Gods and Pitṛs, happens, somehow, to neglect it, incurs sin and becomes a hog.’

3.s: āmantritastu yaḥ śrāddhe vṛśalyā saha modate dāturyadduṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tat sarvaṃ pratipadyate
3.d: आमन्त्रितस्तु यः श्राद्धे वृशल्या सह मोदते दातुर्यद्दुष्कृतं किं चित् तत् सर्वं प्रतिपद्यते
3.e: If the man invited at the śrāddha dallies with a woman, he takes upon himself all the sin that there may be in the giver.

3.s: akrodhanāḥ śaucaparāḥ satataṃ brahmacāriṇaḥ nyastaśastrā mahābhāgāḥ pitaraḥ pūrvadevatāḥ
3.d: अक्रोधनाः शौचपराः सततं ब्रह्मचारिणः न्यस्तशस्त्रा महाभागाः पितरः पूर्वदेवताः
3.e: The Pitṛs are the foremost gods, free from anger, ever intent on purity, chaste, rid of all means of offence, and supremely blessed.

3.s: yasmādutpattireteṣāṃ sarveṣāmapyaśeṣataḥ ye ca yairupacaryāḥ syurniyamaistānnibodhata
3.d: यस्मादुत्पत्तिरेतेषां सर्वेषामप्यशेषतः ये च यैरुपचर्याः स्युर्नियमैस्तान्निबोधत
3.e: Now fully learn from whom all these have their origin and who are to be worshipped, by whom and by what roles.

3.s: manorhairaṇyagarbhasya ye marīciādayaḥ sutāḥ teṣāṃ ṛṣīṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ putrāḥ pitṛgaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
3.d: मनोर्हैरण्यगर्भस्य ये मरीचिआदयः सुताः तेषां ऋषीणां सर्वेषां पुत्राः पितृगणाः स्मृताः
3.e: Of Manu, the son of Hiraṇyagarbha, Marīci and the rest were sons; and the sons of all these sages have been declared to constitute the “Body of Pitṛs.”

3.s: virājsutāḥ somasadaḥ sādhyānāṃ pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ agniṣvāttāśca devānāṃ mārīcā lokaviśrutāḥ
3.d: विराज्सुताः सोमसदः साध्यानां पितरः स्मृताः अग्निष्वात्ताश्च देवानां मारीचा लोकविश्रुताः
3.e: The Somasads, the sons of Virāj, have been declared to be the Pitṛs of the Sādhyas; and the Agnisvāttas, the sons of Marīci, are famed in the world as the Pitṛs of the Gods.

3.s: daityadānavayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvauragarakṣasām suparṇakinnarāṇāṃ ca smṛtā barhiṣado 'trijāḥ
3.d: दैत्यदानवयक्षाणां गन्धर्वौरगरक्षसाम् सुपर्णकिन्नराणां च स्मृता बर्हिषदो ऽत्रिजाः
3.e: The Barhisads, the sons of Atri, are declared to be the Pitṛs of Daityas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Uragas, Rākṣasas, Suparṇas and Kinnaras.

3.s: somapā nāma viprāṇāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ havirbhujaḥ vaiśyānāmājyapā nāma śūdrāṇāṃ tu sukālinaḥ
3.d: सोमपा नाम विप्राणां क्षत्रियाणां हविर्भुजः वैश्यानामाज्यपा नाम शूद्राणां तु सुकालिनः
3.e: Those by name Somapās are the Pitṛs of Brāhmaṇas; the Havirbhujs are the Pitṛs of Kṣatriyas; those by name Ājyapas, of Vaiśyas; and of Śūdras, Sukālins.

3.s: somapāstu kaveḥ putrā haviṣmanto 'ṅgiraḥsutāḥ pulastyasyājyapāḥ putrā vasiṣṭhasya sukālinaḥ
3.d: सोमपास्तु कवेः पुत्रा हविष्मन्तो ऽङ्गिरःसुताः पुलस्त्यस्याज्यपाः पुत्रा वसिष्ठस्य सुकालिनः
3.e: Somapas are the sons of Kavi; Haviṣmats are the sons of Aṅgiras; Ājyapās are the sons of Pulastya, and Sukālins, of Vaśiṣṭha.

3.s: agnidagdhānagnidagdhān kāvyān barhiṣadastathā 'nagnidagdhānagnidagdhān agniṣvāttāṃśca saumyāṃśca viprāṇāmeva nirdiśet
3.d: अग्निदग्धानग्निदग्धान् काव्यान् बर्हिषदस्तथा ऽनग्निदग्धानग्निदग्धान् अग्निष्वात्तांश्च सौम्यांश्च विप्राणामेव निर्दिशेत्
3.e: ‘The Anagnidagdhas, the Agnidagdhas, the Kāvyas, the Barhiṣads, the Agniṣvāttas, and the Saumyas,—these one should regard as the Pitṛs of Brāhmaṇas.

3.s: ya ete tu gaṇā mukhyāḥ pitr̥̄ṇāṃ parikīrtitāḥ teṣāmapīha vijñeyaṃ putrapautramanantakam
3.d: य एते तु गणा मुख्याः पित्र्̥̄णां परिकीर्तिताः तेषामपीह विज्ञेयं पुत्रपौत्रमनन्तकम्
3.e: Of the principal bodies of Pitṛs that have been described, know that there are endless sons and grandsons in this world.

3.s: ṛṣibhyaḥ pitaro jātāḥ pitṛbhyo devamānavāḥ devebhyastu jagat sarvaṃ caraṃ sthāṇvanupūrvaśaḥ
3.d: ऋषिभ्यः पितरो जाताः पितृभ्यो देवमानवाः देवेभ्यस्तु जगत् सर्वं चरं स्थाण्वनुपूर्वशः
3.e: From the sages were born the Pitṛs, Gods and Men; and from the gods the entire world, moveable and immoveable, in due order.

3.s: rājatairbhājanaireṣāmatho vā rajatānvitaiḥ vāryapi śraddhayā dattamakṣayāyaupakalpate
3.d: राजतैर्भाजनैरेषामथो वा रजतान्वितैः वार्यपि श्रद्धया दत्तमक्षयायौपकल्पते
3.e: Even water offered to these with faith, in vessels, either made of silver or connected with silver, is conducive to imperishability.

3.s: daivakāryāddvijātīnāṃ pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate daivaṃ hi pitṛkāryasya pūrvamāpyāyanaṃ smṛtam
3.d: दैवकार्याद्द्विजातीनां पितृकार्यं विशिष्यते दैवं हि पितृकार्यस्य पूर्वमाप्यायनं स्मृतम्
3.e: For twice-born men, the rite in honour of the Pitṛs excels that in honour of the gods; the rite in honour of the gods has been declared to be the previous sustainer of the rite in honour of the Pitṛs.

3.s: teṣāmārakṣabhūtaṃ tu pūrvaṃ daivaṃ niyojayet raksāṃsi vipralumpanti śrāddhamārakṣavarjitam
3.d: तेषामारक्षभूतं तु पूर्वं दैवं नियोजयेत् रक्सांसि विप्रलुम्पन्ति श्राद्धमारक्षवर्जितम्
3.e: One should first engage the Brāhmaṇa in honour of the gods, as a protection to these (offerings to) Pitṛs; for the Rākṣasas take away the śrāddha that is devoid of protection.

3.s: daivādyantaṃ tadīheta pitryādyantaṃ na tadbhavet pitryādyantaṃ tvīhamānaḥ kṣipraṃ naśyati sānvayaḥ
3.d: दैवाद्यन्तं तदीहेत पित्र्याद्यन्तं न तद्भवेत् पित्र्याद्यन्तं त्वीहमानः क्षिप्रं नश्यति सान्वयः
3.e: One should first engage the Brāhmaṇa in honour of the gods, as a protection to these (offerings to) Pitṛs; for the Rākṣasas take away the śrāddha that is devoid of protection.

3.s: śuciṃ deśaṃ viviktaṃ ca gomayenaupalepayet dakṣināpravaṇaṃ caiva prayatnenaupapādayet
3.d: शुचिं देशं विविक्तं च गोमयेनौपलेपयेत् दक्षिनाप्रवणं चैव प्रयत्नेनौपपादयेत्
3.e: One should prepare with care a clean and secluded place Sloping towards the south, and smear it with cowdung.

3.s: avakāśeṣu cokṣeṣu jalatīreṣu caiva hi vivikteṣu ca tuṣyanti dattena pitaraḥ sadā
3.d: अवकाशेषु चोक्षेषु जलतीरेषु चैव हि विविक्तेषु च तुष्यन्ति दत्तेन पितरः सदा
3.e: The Pitṛs are always pleased with what is offered in clean places, on water-banks and in secluded places.

3.s: āsaneṣūpakḷpteṣu barhiṣmatsu pṛthakpṛthak upaspṛṣṭaudakān samyag viprāṃstānupaveśayet
3.d: आसनेषूपकॢप्तेषु बर्हिष्मत्सु पृथक्पृथक् उपस्पृष्टौदकान् सम्यग् विप्रांस्तानुपवेशयेत्
3.e: Seats with kuśa grass having been separately placed, he should seat the said Brāhmaṇas who have performed their ablutions.

3.s: upaveśya tu tān viprānāsaneṣvajugupsitān gandhamālyaiḥ surabhibhirarcayeddaivapūrvakam
3.d: उपवेश्य तु तान् विप्रानासनेष्वजुगुप्सितान् गन्धमाल्यैः सुरभिभिरर्चयेद्दैवपूर्वकम्
3.e: Having seated those unreproached Brāhmaṇas on those seats, he should worship them with sweet-smelling perfumes and Garlands, beginning with those invited in honour of the gods.

3.s: teṣāmudakamānīya sapavitrāṃstilānapi agnau kuryādanujñāto brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
3.d: तेषामुदकमानीय सपवित्रांस्तिलानपि अग्नौ कुर्यादनुज्ञातो ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणैः सह
3.e: Having presented to them water, and also sesamum along with kuśa-blade, the Brāhmaṇa, permitted by the Brāhmaṇas collectively, should make an offering into fire.

3.s: agneḥ somayamābhyāṃ ca kṛtvā 'pyāyanamāditaḥ havirdānena vidhivat paścāt saṃtarpayet pitr̥̄n
3.d: अग्नेः सोमयमाभ्यां च कृत्वा ऽप्यायनमादितः हविर्दानेन विधिवत् पश्चात् संतर्पयेत् पित्र्̥̄न्
3.e: Having at fir st brought about the satisfaction of Agni and Soma-Yama by the offering of sacrificial food, he should afterwards satisfy, according to rule, the Pitṛs.

3.s: agniabhāve tu viprasya pāṇāvevaupapādayet yo hyagniḥ sa dvijo viprairmantradarśibhirucyate
3.d: अग्निअभावे तु विप्रस्य पाणावेवौपपादयेत् यो ह्यग्निः स द्विजो विप्रैर्मन्त्रदर्शिभिरुच्यते
3.e: In the absence of Fire, he shall make the offering into the Brāhmaṇa’s hand; for it has been declared by the Brāhmaṇa seers of Vedic texts that what the Fire is, that same is the Brāhmaṇa.

3.s: akrodhanān suprasādān vadantyetān purātanān lokasyāpyāyane yuktān śrāddhadevān dvijottamān śrāddhe devān dvijottamān
3.d: अक्रोधनान् सुप्रसादान् वदन्त्येतान् पुरातनान् लोकस्याप्यायने युक्तान् श्राद्धदेवान् द्विजोत्तमान् श्राद्धे देवान् द्विजोत्तमान्
3.e: The ancients describe these good Brāhmaṇas as the “Gods of Śrāddha,” free from anger, easily satisfied, intent upon sustaining the universe.

3.s: apasavyamagnau kṛtvā sarvamāvṛtya vikramam āvṛtparikramaṃ apasavyena hastena nirvapedudakaṃ bhuvi
3.d: अपसव्यमग्नौ कृत्वा सर्वमावृत्य विक्रमम् आवृत्परिक्रमं अपसव्येन हस्तेन निर्वपेदुदकं भुवि
3.e: Having done the entire serial performance in Fire, in the “Apasavya” form, he should offer water on the ground with the hand in the “Apasavya” position.

3.s: trīṃstu tasmāddhaviḥśeṣāt piṇḍān kṛtvā samāhitaḥ audakenaiva vidhinā nirvapeddakṣiṇāmukhaḥ
3.d: त्रींस्तु तस्माद्धविःशेषात् पिण्डान् कृत्वा समाहितः औदकेनैव विधिना निर्वपेद्दक्षिणामुखः
3.e: Having made these balls out of the remnant of the said sacrificial material, he should, with collected mind and facing the South, offer them in the manner of the water-libations.

3.s: nyupya piṇḍāṃstatastāṃstu prayato vidhipūrvakam teṣu darbheṣu taṃ hastaṃ nirmṛjyātlepabhāginām
3.d: न्युप्य पिण्डांस्ततस्तांस्तु प्रयतो विधिपूर्वकम् तेषु दर्भेषु तं हस्तं निर्मृज्यात्लेपभागिनाम्
3.e: Self-controlled, he should, after having offered those balls on Kuśa-blades, according to rule, wipe that hand on those same (Kuśa-blades), for the sake of the “Partakers of Smearings.”

3.s: ācamyaudakparāvṛtya trirāyamya śanairasūn ṣaḍ ṛtūṃśca namaskuryāt pitr̥̄neva ca mantravat
3.d: आचम्यौदक्परावृत्य त्रिरायम्य शनैरसून् षड् ऋतूंश्च नमस्कुर्यात् पित्र्̥̄नेव च मन्त्रवत्
3.e: Turning to the north, having sipped water and having gently suppressed his breath three times, he shall salute, with proper formulas, the six seasons and also the Pitṛs.

3.s: udakaṃ ninayetśeṣaṃ śanaiḥ piṇḍāntike punaḥ avajighrecca tān piṇḍān yathānyuptān samāhitaḥ
3.d: उदकं निनयेत्शेषं शनैः पिण्डान्तिके पुनः अवजिघ्रेच्च तान् पिण्डान् यथान्युप्तान् समाहितः
3.e: The remaining water he should gently pour near the balls; and with collected mind he should smell those halls in the order in which they were offered.

3.s: piṇḍebhyastvalpikāṃ mātrāṃ samādāyānupūrvaśaḥ piṇḍebhyaḥ svalpikāṃ tāneva viprānāsīnān vidhivat pūrvamāśayet
3.d: पिण्डेभ्यस्त्वल्पिकां मात्रां समादायानुपूर्वशः पिण्डेभ्यः स्वल्पिकां तानेव विप्रानासीनान् विधिवत् पूर्वमाशयेत्
3.e: Having, in due order of sequence, taken very small portions out of the halls, he shall first feed those same seated Brāhmaṇas with them, in accordance with role.

3.s: dhriyamāṇe tu pitari pūrveṣāmeva nirvapet vipravadvā 'pi taṃ śrāddhe svakaṃ pitaramāśayet śrāddhaṃ
3.d: ध्रियमाणे तु पितरि पूर्वेषामेव निर्वपेत् विप्रवद्वा ऽपि तं श्राद्धे स्वकं पितरमाशयेत् श्राद्धं
3.e: While his father holds, one should make the offering to the previous ancestors; or, he may feed his own father at the Śrāddha as a Brāhmana.

3.s: pitā yasya nivṛttaḥ syāj jīveccāpi pitāmahaḥ pitā yasya tu vṛttaḥ syāj pituḥ sa nāma saṅkīrtya kīrtayet prapitāmaham
3.d: पिता यस्य निवृत्तः स्याज् जीवेच्चापि पितामहः पिता यस्य तु वृत्तः स्याज् पितुः स नाम सङ्कीर्त्य कीर्तयेत् प्रपितामहम्
3.e: He whose father is dead, but grandfather is living, should mention the great-grandfather after having pronounced the name of the father.

3.s: pitāmaho vā tatśrāddhaṃ bhuñjītaityabravīn manuḥ kāmaṃ vā samanujñātaḥ svayameva samācaret
3.d: पितामहो वा तत्श्राद्धं भुञ्जीतैत्यब्रवीन् मनुः कामं वा समनुज्ञातः स्वयमेव समाचरेत्
3.e: Manu has declared that either the grandfather may eat at that Śrāddha, or the man himself may, according to his will, perform it, after being permitted by him.

3.s: teṣāṃ dattvā tu hasteṣu sapavitraṃ tilaudakam tatpiṇḍāgraṃ prayaccheta svadhaiṣāmastviti bruvan prayacchet tu
3.d: तेषां दत्त्वा तु हस्तेषु सपवित्रं तिलौदकम् तत्पिण्डाग्रं प्रयच्छेत स्वधैषामस्त्विति ब्रुवन् प्रयच्छेत् तु
3.e: Having poured into their hands water and sesamum along with kuśa blades, he should offer the top portion of the ball, saying “May this be svadhā to these.”

3.s: pāṇibhyāṃ tūpasaṅgṛhya svayamannasya vardhitam varddhitam viprāntike pitr̥̄n dhyāyan śanakairupanikṣipet
3.d: पाणिभ्यां तूपसङ्गृह्य स्वयमन्नस्य वर्धितम् वर्द्धितम् विप्रान्तिके पित्र्̥̄न् ध्यायन् शनकैरुपनिक्षिपेत्
3.e: Taking up with his hands the supply of food, he shall himself gently place it near the Brāhmaṇas, thinking of his Pitṛs (all the time).

3.s: ubhayorhastayormuktaṃ yadannamupanīyate tadvipralumpantyasurāḥ sahasā duṣṭacetasaḥ
3.d: उभयोर्हस्तयोर्मुक्तं यदन्नमुपनीयते तद्विप्रलुम्पन्त्यसुराः सहसा दुष्टचेतसः
3.e: The wicked-minded demons forcibly destroy that food which is abandoned by both hands.

3.s: guṇāṃśca sūpaśākādyān payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ madhu vinyaset prayataḥ pūrvaṃ bhūmāveva samāhitaḥ
3.d: गुणांश्च सूपशाकाद्यान् पयो दधि घृतं मधु विन्यसेत् प्रयतः पूर्वं भूमावेव समाहितः
3.e: Pure and with collected mind, he shall first place on the ground the accessories, such as soups and vegetaui.es, &c., milk, curd, butter and honey.

3.s: bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca vividhaṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca hṛdyāni caiva māṃsāni pānāni surabhīṇi ca
3.d: भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च विविधं मूलानि च फलानि च हृद्यानि चैव मांसानि पानानि सुरभीणि च
3.e: Also hard food and soft food of various kinds, roots, fruits, savoury meat and sweet-smelling drinks.

3.s: upanīya tu tat sarvaṃ śanakaiḥ susamāhitaḥ pariveṣayeta prayato guṇān sarvān pracodayan
3.d: उपनीय तु तत् सर्वं शनकैः सुसमाहितः परिवेषयेत प्रयतो गुणान् सर्वान् प्रचोदयन्
3.e: Having gently brought up all this, he shall, with collected mind and pure, serve it,—describing all its qualities.

3.s: nāsramāpātayej jātu na kupyennānṛtaṃ vadet na pādena spṛśedannaṃ na caitadavadhūnayet
3.d: नास्रमापातयेज् जातु न कुप्येन्नानृतं वदेत् न पादेन स्पृशेदन्नं न चैतदवधूनयेत्
3.e: Never should he shed tears; nor should he become angry; nor tell a lie. He should not touch the food with his foot, nob shake it.

3.s: asraṃ gamayati pretān kopo 'rīnanṛtaṃ śunaḥ pādasparśastu rakṣāṃsi duṣkṛtīnavadhūnanam
3.d: अस्रं गमयति प्रेतान् कोपो ऽरीननृतं शुनः पादस्पर्शस्तु रक्षांसि दुष्कृतीनवधूननम्
3.e: Tears make the food go to ghosts, anger to enemies, lie to dogs, touching with the foot to demons, and shaking to sinners.

3.s: yadyadroceta viprebhyastat taddadyādamatsaraḥ brahmodyāśca kathāḥ kuryāt pitr̥̄ṇāmetadīpsitam
3.d: यद्यद्रोचेत विप्रेभ्यस्तत् तद्दद्यादमत्सरः ब्रह्मोद्याश्च कथाः कुर्यात् पित्र्̥̄णामेतदीप्सितम्
3.e: Whatever may be agreeable to the Brāhmaṇas, that he shall give ungrudgingly. He shall relate stories told in the Veda; as this is liked by the Pitṛs.

3.s: svādhyāyaṃ śrāvayet pitrye dharmaśāstrāṇi caiva hi ākhyānānītihāsāṃśca purāṇāni khilāni ca
3.d: स्वाध्यायं श्रावयेत् पित्र्ये धर्मशास्त्राणि चैव हि आख्यानानीतिहासांश्च पुराणानि खिलानि च
3.e: At the rite in honour of the Pitṛs, one should recite the Vedic text, Legal Institutes, Stories, Histories, Legends and supplementary Texts.

3.s: harṣayedbrāhmaṇāṃstuṣṭo bhojayecca śanaisśanaiḥ annādyenāsakṛccaitān guṇaiśca paricodayet
3.d: हर्षयेद्ब्राह्मणांस्तुष्टो भोजयेच्च शनैस्शनैः अन्नाद्येनासकृच्चैतान् गुणैश्च परिचोदयेत्
3.e: Being happy himself, he shall bring delight to the Brāhmaṇas; he shall feed them, gently and slowly, with dishes, and urge them repeatedly by means of seasonings.

3.s: vratasthamapi dauhitraṃ śrāddhe yatnena bhojayet kutapaṃ cāsanaṃ dadyāt tilaiśca vikiren mahīm
3.d: व्रतस्थमपि दौहित्रं श्राद्धे यत्नेन भोजयेत् कुतपं चासनं दद्यात् तिलैश्च विकिरेन् महीम्
3.e: At a śrāddha he should, with special care, feed the daughter’s son, even though he be still under vows (of studentship). He should offer the blanket as seat and scatter sesamum on the ground.

3.s: trīṇi śrāddhe pavitrāṇi dauhitraḥ kutapastilāḥ trīṇi cātra praśaṃsanti śaucamakrodhamatvarām
3.d: त्रीणि श्राद्धे पवित्राणि दौहित्रः कुतपस्तिलाः त्रीणि चात्र प्रशंसन्ति शौचमक्रोधमत्वराम्
3.e: Three things are sacred at Śrāddhas—the daughter’s son, blanket and sesamum, and they commend three things in this connection—cleanliness, absence of anger and absence of haste.

3.s: atyuṣṇaṃ sarvamannaṃ syādbhuñjīraṃste ca vāgyatāḥ na ca dvijātayo brūyurdātrā pṛṣṭā havirguṇān
3.d: अत्युष्णं सर्वमन्नं स्याद्भुञ्जीरंस्ते च वाग्यताः न च द्विजातयो ब्रूयुर्दात्रा पृष्टा हविर्गुणान्
3.e: All the food should be very hot, and they should eat with controlled speech; when asked by the giver, the Brāhmaṇas should not describe the qualities of the sacrificial food.

3.s: yāvaduṣmā bhavatyannaṃ yāvadaśnanti vāgyatāḥ pitarastāvadaśnanti yāvatnauktā havirguṇāḥ
3.d: यावदुष्मा भवत्यन्नं यावदश्नन्ति वाग्यताः पितरस्तावदश्नन्ति यावत्नौक्ता हविर्गुणाः
3.e: As long as the food is steaming, as long as they eat with speech controlled, so long do the Pitṛs eat, as long as the qualities of the food are not described.

3.s: yadveṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yadbhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ saupānatkaśca yadbhuṅkte tadvai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate
3.d: यद्वेष्टितशिरा भुङ्क्ते यद्भुङ्क्ते दक्षिणामुखः सौपानत्कश्च यद्भुङ्क्ते तद्वै रक्षांसि भुञ्जते
3.e: What the guest eats with his head wound up, what he eats with his face towards the south, what he eats with shoes on, all this verily the demons eat.

3.s: cāṇḍālaśca varāhaśca kukkuṭaḥ śvā tathaiva ca rajasvalā ca ṣaṇḍhaśca naikṣerannaśnato dvijān
3.d: चाण्डालश्च वराहश्च कुक्कुटः श्वा तथैव च रजस्वला च षण्ढश्च नैक्षेरन्नश्नतो द्विजान्
3.e: The Cāṇdāla, the pig, the cock, as also the dog, the unclean woman and the eunuch should not look at the Brāhmaṇas while eating.

3.s: home pradāne bhojye ca yadebhirabhivīkṣyate daive haviṣi pitrye vā tadgacchatyayathātatham
3.d: होमे प्रदाने भोज्ये च यदेभिरभिवीक्ष्यते दैवे हविषि पित्र्ये वा तद्गच्छत्ययथातथम्
3.e: At the offering into Fire, at gifts, at feeding, or at any rite in honour of the Gods or of the Pitṛs,—whatever is seen by these goes wrong.

3.s: ghrāṇena sūkaro hanti pakṣavātena kukkuṭaḥ śūkaro śvā tu dṛṣṭinipātena sparśeṇāvaravarṇajaḥ
3.d: घ्राणेन सूकरो हन्ति पक्षवातेन कुक्कुटः शूकरो श्वा तु दृष्टिनिपातेन स्पर्शेणावरवर्णजः
3.e: The pig defiles by sniffing, the cock by wind raised by its wings, the dog by casting his eye, and the man born of the low caste by touch.

3.s: khañjo vā yadi vā kāṇo dātuḥ preṣyo 'pi vā bhavet hīnātiriktagātro vā tamapyapanayet punaḥ
3.d: खञ्जो वा यदि वा काणो दातुः प्रेष्यो ऽपि वा भवेत् हीनातिरिक्तगात्रो वा तमप्यपनयेत् पुनः
3.e: The cripple, or the one-eyed man, the man without a limb, or the man with a redundant limb,—even if he be the offerer’s servant—he should remove from there.

3.s: brāhmaṇaṃ bhikṣukaṃ vā 'pi bhojanārthamupasthitam brāhmaṇairabhyanujñātaḥ śaktitaḥ pratipūjayet
3.d: ब्राह्मणं भिक्षुकं वा ऽपि भोजनार्थमुपस्थितम् ब्राह्मणैरभ्यनुज्ञातः शक्तितः प्रतिपूजयेत्
3.e: The Brāhmaṇa or the mendicant who comes seeking for food, he shall entertain, to the best of his ability, on being permitted by the Brāhmaṇas.

3.s: sārvavarṇikamannādyaṃ saṃnīyāplāvya vāriṇā samutsṛjedbhuktavatāmagrato vikiran bhuvi
3.d: सार्ववर्णिकमन्नाद्यं संनीयाप्लाव्य वारिणा समुत्सृजेद्भुक्तवतामग्रतो विकिरन् भुवि
3.e: Having mixed up the food of all kinds and wetted it with water, he should throw it before the Brāhmaṇas who have eaten, scattering it on the ground.

3.s: asaṃskṛtapramītānāṃ tyāgināṃ kulayoṣitām ucchiṣṭaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ syāddarbheṣu vikiraśca yaḥ
3.d: असंस्कृतप्रमीतानां त्यागिनां कुलयोषिताम् उच्छिष्टं भागधेयं स्याद्दर्भेषु विकिरश्च यः
3.e: The remnant and that which has been scattered on the Kuśa grass form the share of those who have died without sacraments, and of those who have abandoned family ladies.

3.s: uccheṣaṇāṃ bhūmigatamajihmasyāśaṭhasya ca dāsavargasya tat pitrye bhāgadheyaṃ pracakṣate
3.d: उच्छेषणां भूमिगतमजिह्मस्याशठस्य च दासवर्गस्य तत् पित्र्ये भागधेयं प्रचक्षते
3.e: At the rite in honour of the Pitṛs, the remnant fallen on the ground is regarded as the share of straightforward, dutiful servants.

3.s: āsapiṇḍakriyākarma dvijāteḥ saṃsthitasya tu adaivaṃ bhojayetśrāddhaṃ piṇḍamekaṃ ca nirvapet
3.d: आसपिण्डक्रियाकर्म द्विजातेः संस्थितस्य तु अदैवं भोजयेत्श्राद्धं पिण्डमेकं च निर्वपेत्
3.e: For the twice-born person just dead, there should be (performed) the rite up to the ‘Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa’: one should do the feeding at his Śrāddha without any in honour of the gods, and he shall offer one ball.

3.s: sahapiṇḍakriyāyāṃ tu kṛtāyāmasya dharmataḥ anayaivāvṛtā kāryaṃ piṇḍanirvapanaṃ sutaiḥ
3.d: सहपिण्डक्रियायां तु कृतायामस्य धर्मतः अनयैवावृता कार्यं पिण्डनिर्वपनं सुतैः
3.e: But after the Amalgamating Rite has been duly performed, the offering of balls shall be done by the sons, by this same method.

3.s: śrāddhaṃ bhuktvā ya ucchiṣṭaṃ vṛṣalāya prayacchati sa mūḍho narakaṃ yāti kālasūtramavākṣirāḥ
3.d: श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा य उच्छिष्टं वृषलाय प्रयच्छति स मूढो नरकं याति कालसूत्रमवाक्षिराः
3.e: He who, having eaten at a śrāddha, gives the leavings to a śūdra,—this foolish man falls headlong into the Kālasūtra hell.

3.s: śrāddhabhug vṛṣalītalpaṃ tadaharyo 'dhigacchati tasyāḥ purīṣe taṃ māsaṃ pitarastasya śerate
3.d: श्राद्धभुग् वृषलीतल्पं तदहर्यो ऽधिगच्छति तस्याः पुरीषे तं मासं पितरस्तस्य शेरते
3.e: Having eaten at a Śrāddha, if one enters the bed of a woman on that day, his ancestors lie in her ordure for the whole of that month.

3.s: pṛṣṭvā svaditamityevaṃ tṛptānācāmayet tataḥ ācāntāṃścānujānīyādabhito ramyatāmiti
3.d: पृष्ट्वा स्वदितमित्येवं तृप्तानाचामयेत् ततः आचान्तांश्चानुजानीयादभितो रम्यतामिति
3.e: Having asked—“Have you dined well?”—he shall, after they have been fully satisfied, make them wash; and when they have washed, he shall say—“You may rest where you choose.

3.s: svadhā 'stvityeva taṃ brūyurbrāhmaṇāstadanantaram svadhākāraḥ parā hyāṣīḥ sarveṣu pitṛkarmasu
3.d: स्वधा ऽस्त्वित्येव तं ब्रूयुर्ब्राह्मणास्तदनन्तरम् स्वधाकारः परा ह्याषीः सर्वेषु पितृकर्मसु
3.e: The Brāhmaṇas should thereupon tell him—“May there be svadhā.” at all rites performed in honour of the Pitṛs, the syllable “Svadhā” constitutes the highest benediction.

3.s: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣāmannaśeṣaṃ nivedayet yathā brūyustathā kuryādanujñātastato dvijaiḥ
3.d: ततो भुक्तवतां तेषामन्नशेषं निवेदयेत् यथा ब्रूयुस्तथा कुर्यादनुज्ञातस्ततो द्विजैः
3.e: He shall then inform them of the food that may be left after they have eaten; being permitted by the Brāhmaṇas he shall do as they tell him.

3.s: pitrye svaditamityeva vācyaṃ goṣṭhe tu suśṛtam saṃpannamityabhyudaye daive rucitamityapi saṃpannam
3.d: पित्र्ये स्वदितमित्येव वाच्यं गोष्ठे तु सुशृतम् संपन्नमित्यभ्युदये दैवे रुचितमित्यपि संपन्नम्
3.e: At the rite in honour of the Pitṛs, one should say “svaditam” (well-dined); at the Goṣṭha, “suśṛtam” (well-cooked); at the Ābhyudayika rite, “sampannam” (accomplished); and at the rite in honour of the gods, “rucitam” (agreeable).

3.s: aparāhṇastathā darbhā vāstusaṃpādanaṃ tilāḥ saṃpādanaṃ sṛṣṭirmṛṣṭirdvijāścāgryāḥ śrāddhakarmasu saṃpadaḥ
3.d: अपराह्णस्तथा दर्भा वास्तुसंपादनं तिलाः संपादनं सृष्टिर्मृष्टिर्द्विजाश्चाग्र्याः श्राद्धकर्मसु संपदः
3.e: The afternoon, Kuśa-Grass, setting up of the dwelling, sesamum grains, liberality, cleaning and superior Brāhmaṇas;—these are the essentials of Śrāddha-rites.

3.s: darbhāḥ pavitraṃ pūrvāhṇo haviṣyāṇi ca sarvaśaḥ pavitraṃ yacca pūrvauktaṃ vijñeyā havyasaṃpadaḥ
3.d: दर्भाः पवित्रं पूर्वाह्णो हविष्याणि च सर्वशः पवित्रं यच्च पूर्वौक्तं विज्ञेया हव्यसंपदः
3.e: Kuśa-Grass, the sanctificatory texts, the forenoon, all kinds of sacrificial food, purity and also the afore-mentioned these should be regarded as the essentials of a sacrifice.

3.s: muniannāni payaḥ somo māṃsaṃ yaccānupaskṛtam aksāralavaṇaṃ caiva prakṛtyā havirucyate
3.d: मुनिअन्नानि पयः सोमो मांसं यच्चानुपस्कृतम् अक्सारलवणं चैव प्रकृत्या हविरुच्यते
3.e: The food of hermits, milk, the soma-herb, meat that is not forbidden, salt other than alkaline. are, by nature, called “sacrificial food.”

3.s: visṛjya brāhmaṇāṃstāṃstu niyato vāgyataḥ śuciḥ visarjya brāhmanāṃstāṃstu prayato vidhipūrvakam dakṣiṇāṃ diśamākāṅkṣan yācetaimān varān pitr̥̄n
3.d: विसृज्य ब्राह्मणांस्तांस्तु नियतो वाग्यतः शुचिः विसर्ज्य ब्राह्मनांस्तांस्तु प्रयतो विधिपूर्वकम् दक्षिणां दिशमाकाङ्क्षन् याचेतैमान् वरान् पित्र्̥̄न्
3.e: Having dismissed those Brāhmaṇas, he, with collected mind, controlled in speech and pure, turning towards the southern quarter, shall beg these boons of his ancestors.

3.s: dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ saṃtatireva ca śraddhā ca no mā vyagamadbahudeyaṃ ca no 'stviti
3.d: दातारो नो ऽभिवर्धन्तां वेदाः संततिरेव च श्रद्धा च नो मा व्यगमद्बहुदेयं च नो ऽस्त्विति
3.e: ‘May our benefactors prosper! As also the Vedas and our progeny! May our faith never waver! May there be much for us to give away!’

3.s: evaṃ nirvapaṇaṃ kṛtvā piṇḍāṃstāṃstadanantaram gāṃ vipramajamagniṃ vā prāśayedapsu vā kṣipet
3.d: एवं निर्वपणं कृत्वा पिण्डांस्तांस्तदनन्तरम् गां विप्रमजमग्निं वा प्राशयेदप्सु वा क्षिपेत्
3.e: Having made the offering thus, he should, after this, either make the cow or the Brāhmaṇa or the goat or the fire to eat the balls, or throw them into water.

3.s: piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ ke cit parastādeva kurvate vayobhiḥ khādayantyanye prakṣipantyanale 'psu vā
3.d: पिण्डनिर्वपणं के चित् परस्तादेव कुर्वते वयोभिः खादयन्त्यन्ये प्रक्षिपन्त्यनले ऽप्सु वा
3.e: Some people do the ball-offering afterwards, others cause them to be eaten by birds, or throw them into fire or water.

3.s: pativratā dharmapatnī pitṛpūjanatatparā madhyamaṃ tu tataḥ piṇḍamadyāt samyak sutārthinī
3.d: पतिव्रता धर्मपत्नी पितृपूजनतत्परा मध्यमं तु ततः पिण्डमद्यात् सम्यक् सुतार्थिनी
3.e: The lawful wife, devoted to her husband and intent upon the worshipping of the Pitṛs, should, if desirous of a son, eat in the proper manner, the middlemost ball.

3.s: āyuṣmantaṃ sutaṃ sūte yaśomedhāsamanvitam dhanavantaṃ prajāvantaṃ sāttvikaṃ dhārmikaṃ tathā
3.d: आयुष्मन्तं सुतं सूते यशोमेधासमन्वितम् धनवन्तं प्रजावन्तं सात्त्विकं धार्मिकं तथा
3.e: She brings forth a long-lived son, endowed with fame and intelligence, wealthy, with numerous offspring, good and righteous.

3.s: praksālya hastāvācāmya jñātiprāyaṃ prakalpayet jñātibhyaḥ satkṛtaṃ dattvā bāndhavānapi bhojayet datvā
3.d: प्रक्साल्य हस्तावाचाम्य ज्ञातिप्रायं प्रकल्पयेत् ज्ञातिभ्यः सत्कृतं दत्त्वा बान्धवानपि भोजयेत् दत्वा
3.e: Having washed the hands and sipped water, he should make offerings to his paternal relations; and having treated his paternal relations well, he should feed his other relations also.

3.s: uccheṣaṇaṃ tu tat tiṣṭhedyāvadviprā visarjitāḥ yat tiṣṭhed tato gṛhabaliṃ kuryāditi dharmo vyavasthitaḥ
3.d: उच्छेषणं तु तत् तिष्ठेद्यावद्विप्रा विसर्जिताः यत् तिष्ठेद् ततो गृहबलिं कुर्यादिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः
3.e: The leavings shall remain until the Brāhmaṇas have been dismissed. After that, he should make the domestic offerings. Such is the established law.

3.s: haviryaccirarātrāya yaccānantyāya kalpate pitṛbhyo vidhivaddattaṃ tat pravakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ
3.d: हविर्यच्चिररात्राय यच्चानन्त्याय कल्पते पितृभ्यो विधिवद्दत्तं तत् प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः
3.e: I shall now fully describe what offering-material, on being offered to the Pitṛs, according to role, serves for a long time, and for eternity.

3.s: tilairvrīhiyavairmāṣairadbhirmūlaphalena vā dattena māsaṃ tṛpyanti vidhivat pitaro nṛnām
3.d: तिलैर्व्रीहियवैर्माषैरद्भिर्मूलफलेन वा दत्तेन मासं तृप्यन्ति विधिवत् पितरो नृनाम्
3.e: By the proper offering of sesamum, rice and barley, māṣa, water, roots and fruits, men’s ancestors are satisfied for one month.

3.s: dvau māsau matsyamāṃsena trīn māsān hāriṇena tu aurabhreṇātha caturaḥ śākunenātha pañca vai
3.d: द्वौ मासौ मत्स्यमांसेन त्रीन् मासान् हारिणेन तु औरभ्रेणाथ चतुरः शाकुनेनाथ पञ्च वै
3.e: For two months by fish-meat; for three months by the meat of deer; for four by that of sheep, and for five by that of birds.

3.s: ṣaṇmāsāṃśchāgamāṃsena pārṣatena ca sapta vai aṣṭāvenasya māṃsena rauraveṇa navaiva tu 'iṇeyamāṃsena
3.d: षण्मासांश्छागमांसेन पार्षतेन च सप्त वै अष्टावेनस्य मांसेन रौरवेण नवैव तु ऽइणेयमांसेन
3.e: For six months by the meat of goat; for seven by that of spotted deer; for eight by that of the black antelope, and for nine by that of the Ruru deer.

3.s: daśamāsāṃstu tṛpyanti varāhamahiṣāmiṣaiḥ śaśakūrmayostu māṃsena māsānekādaśaiva tu
3.d: दशमासांस्तु तृप्यन्ति वराहमहिषामिषैः शशकूर्मयोस्तु मांसेन मासानेकादशैव तु
3.e: They are satisfied for ten months by the meat of boars and buffaloes; and for eleven months by the meat of the hare and the tortoise.’

3.s: saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena ca saṃvatsare vārdhrīṇasasya māṃsena tṛptirdvādaśavārṣikī
3.d: संवत्सरं तु गव्येन पयसा पायसेन च संवत्सरे वार्ध्रीणसस्य मांसेन तृप्तिर्द्वादशवार्षिकी
3.e: For one year by cow’s milk and milk-preparations; and by the meat of old goat there is satisfaction lasting for twelve years.

3.s: kālaśākaṃ mahāśalkāḥ khaṅgalohāmiṣaṃ madhu ānantyāyaiva kalpyante muniannāni ca sarvaśaḥ
3.d: कालशाकं महाशल्काः खङ्गलोहामिषं मधु आनन्त्यायैव कल्प्यन्ते मुनिअन्नानि च सर्वशः
3.e: The “Kālaśāka,” the porcupine, the meat of the rhinoceros and the red goat, and honey serve for endless time; as also all kinds ok her mit’s food.

3.s: yat kiṃ cin madhunā miśraṃ pradadyāt tu trayodaśīm tadapyakṣayameva syādvarṣāsu ca maghāsu ca
3.d: यत् किं चिन् मधुना मिश्रं प्रदद्यात् तु त्रयोदशीम् तदप्यक्षयमेव स्याद्वर्षासु च मघासु च
3.e: Whatever thing, mixed with honey, one might offer on the thirteenth day of the month, during the rains, under the asterism of Maghā,—that also would be imperishable.

3.s: api naḥ sa kule bhūyādyo no dadyāt trayodaśīm pāyasaṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ prāk chāye kuñjarasya ca
3.d: अपि नः स कुले भूयाद्यो नो दद्यात् त्रयोदशीम् पायसं मधुसर्पिर्भ्यां प्राक् छाये कुञ्जरस्य च
3.e: ‘May there be one in our family, who may offer milk-rice mixed with honey and butter on the thirteenth, and when the shadow of the elephant falls towards the east.’

3.s: yadyaddadāti vidhivat samyak śraddhāsamanvitaḥ tat tat pitr̥̄ṇāṃ bhavati paratrānantamakṣayam
3.d: यद्यद्ददाति विधिवत् सम्यक् श्रद्धासमन्वितः तत् तत् पित्र्̥̄णां भवति परत्रानन्तमक्षयम्
3.e: Whatever one endowed with faith, offers, according to rule and in the right manner,—that becomes endless and inexhaustible for the Pitṛs in the other world.

3.s: kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyādau varjayitvā caturdaśīm śrāddhe praśastāstithayo yathaitā na tathaitarāḥ
3.d: कृष्णपक्षे दशम्यादौ वर्जयित्वा चतुर्दशीम् श्राद्धे प्रशस्तास्तिथयो यथैता न तथैतराः
3.e: ‘No dates are so commended for the offering of śrāddha as those of the dark fortnight, beginning with the tenth day, leaving out the fourteenth.

3.s: yukṣu kurvan dinaṛkṣeṣu sarvān kāmān samaśnute ayukṣu tu pitr̥̄n sarvān prajāṃ prāpnoti puṣkalām
3.d: युक्षु कुर्वन् दिनऋक्षेषु सर्वान् कामान् समश्नुते अयुक्षु तु पित्र्̥̄न् सर्वान् प्रजां प्राप्नोति पुष्कलाम्
3.e: Performing (the śrāddha) on the even dates and under the even asterisms, one obtains all desires; and honouring the Pitṛs on the odd ones, he obtains prosperous offspring.

3.s: yathā caivāparaḥ pakṣaḥ pūrvapakṣādviśiṣyate tathā śrāddhasya pūrvāhṇādaparāhṇo viśiṣyate
3.d: यथा चैवापरः पक्षः पूर्वपक्षाद्विशिष्यते तथा श्राद्धस्य पूर्वाह्णादपराह्णो विशिष्यते
3.e: Just as, for purposes of śrāddha, the latter half of the month is preferable to the former half, so also, the afternoon is preferable to the forenoon.

3.s: prācīnāvītinā samyagapasavyamatandriṇā pitryamā nidhanāt kāryaṃ vidhivaddarbhapāṇinā
3.d: प्राचीनावीतिना सम्यगपसव्यमतन्द्रिणा पित्र्यमा निधनात् कार्यं विधिवद्दर्भपाणिना
3.e: Until death, one shall perform, with assiduity, the rite in honour of the Pitṛs, according to rule, with the sacred thread passing over the right shoulder, making offerings “from off the left” (to the right) with kuśa-grass in his hand.

3.s: rātrau śrāddhaṃ na kurvīta rākṣasī kīrtitā hi sā saṃdhyayorubhayoścaiva sūrye caivāciraudite
3.d: रात्रौ श्राद्धं न कुर्वीत राक्षसी कीर्तिता हि सा संध्ययोरुभयोश्चैव सूर्ये चैवाचिरौदिते
3.e: One should not perform Śrāddha at night; for the night has been declared to be ‘fit for demons;’—nor at the two twilights, nor when the sun has just risen.

3.s: anena vidhinā śrāddhaṃ trirabdasyaiha nirvapet hemantagrīṣmavarṣāsu pāñcayajñikamanvaham
3.d: अनेन विधिना श्राद्धं त्रिरब्दस्यैह निर्वपेत् हेमन्तग्रीष्मवर्षासु पाञ्चयज्ञिकमन्वहम्
3.e: In accordance with this rule, one should offer Śrāddha thrice in the year—during winter, summer and the rain; and that which forms part of the “five sacrifices” should be done every day.

3.s: na paitṛyajñiyo homo laukike 'gnau vidhīyate na darśena vinā śrāddhamāhitāgnerdvijanmanaḥ
3.d: न पैतृयज्ञियो होमो लौकिके ऽग्नौ विधीयते न दर्शेन विना श्राद्धमाहिताग्नेर्द्विजन्मनः
3.e: The oblation into fire made in connection with the rite in honour of the Pitṛs has not been prescribed as to be offered into the common fire; and for the Brāhmaṇa who has set up the fire, there is no Śrāddha apart from the Moonless day.

3.s: yadeva tarpayatyadbhiḥ pitr̥̄n snātvā dvijottamaḥ tenaiva kṛtsnamāpnoti pitṛyajñakriyāphalam
3.d: यदेव तर्पयत्यद्भिः पित्र्̥̄न् स्नात्वा द्विजोत्तमः तेनैव कृत्स्नमाप्नोति पितृयज्ञक्रियाफलम्
3.e: When the best of Brāhmaṇas, having bathed, satisfies the Pitṛs with water,—by that alone he obtains the whole reward of the performance of the offering to the Pitṛs.

3.s: vasūn vadanti tu pitr̥̄n rudrāṃścaiva pitāmahān prapitāmahāṃstathā 'dityān śrutireṣā sanātanī
3.d: वसून् वदन्ति तु पित्र्̥̄न् रुद्रांश्चैव पितामहान् प्रपितामहांस्तथा ऽदित्यान् श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी
3.e: They call the Fathers “Vasus;” the grandfathers they call “Rudras,” and the great-grandfathers they call “ādityas” such is the ancient text.

3.s: vighasāśī bhavennityaṃ nityaṃ vā 'mṛtabhojanaḥ vighaso bhuktaśeṣaṃ tu yajñaśeṣaṃ tathā 'mṛtam
3.d: विघसाशी भवेन्नित्यं नित्यं वा ऽमृतभोजनः विघसो भुक्तशेषं तु यज्ञशेषं तथा ऽमृतम्
3.e: One should daily live upon “vighasa,” and daily he should eat “amṛta.” “Vighasa” is that which is left by those who must be fed; and “amṛta” is the remnant of sacrific es.
